boundary_rationale: Opens the book's absolute beginning ("In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth") and is organized entirely by the recurring evening-morning day-count refrain; it does not close until the seventh-day rest and blessing in 2:1-3, so the chunk deliberately crosses the chapter line rather than stopping at 1:31.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Stopping at Gen.1.31 (the chapter break) and treating 2:1-3 as belonging to the next unit -- rejected because that would sever the seventh day from the six days it completes.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Gen.1.1 'In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.'
web:Gen.2.2-3 'God finished his work...blessed the seventh day, and made it holy'

boundary_rationale: Opens on its own formula, "This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth" (2:4), which the child span's own texture -- man formed from dust, the garden planted, the animals named, the woman built from the rib -- shows to be a garden-formation narrative in its own right, not a continuation of the day-refrain/'it was so' creation-week form that justifies 'creation_account' for 1:1-2:3 alone. The end at 2:25 rests on the entry of a new participant, the serpent, at 3:1 (a disjunctive clause, והנחש היה ערום) and the deliberate innocence/shame inclusio between 2:25's 'not ashamed' and 3:7's 'knew that they were naked'.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:4-3:15 as one unit, since the WLC runs an unbroken petuchah across the 2:25/3:1 seam -- preserved as single-witness counterevidence, not adopted because the serpent's entry and the innocence/shame inclusio are independent text signals the marker's absence does not override.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Gen.2.4 'This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth'
wlc-parashah(single-witness): petuchah unit Gen.2.4-3.15 crosses the 2:25/3:1 seam

boundary_rationale: Opens on the disjunctive entry of the serpent addressing the woman (3:1, והנחש היה ערום), not on any WEB paragraph mark; the scene runs as one continuous, undeparted three-part judicial oracle (serpent, woman, man in turn, sharing the same curse/consequence form) with no exit until the expulsion. The internal WLC setumah/petuchah breaks at 3:15, 3:16, and 3:21 fall at ordinary addressee shifts inside this single scene, not at any text signal of scene change (new location, new participant set, or new business); under the addendum's symmetry rule a marker of this class is corroboration at most and cannot itself drive a split.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at each addressee shift (3:14 serpent / 3:16 woman / 3:17 man) on the strength of the internal setumah/petuchah pattern alone -- ruled insufficient_evidence_marker_only, since no accompanying text signal of scene change accompanies any of the three divisions, unlike the genuinely new-business transitions later found at Gen.9.8 and (considered but ultimately also rejected) Gen.17.15.
boundary_evidence_refs: wlc-parashah(single-witness): setumah after Gen.3.15, setumah after Gen.3.16, petuchah after Gen.3.21 (addressee-internal, not scene-external)

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 4:8 (the murder itself) to separate 'before' from 'after' -- rejected because that would break the single interrogation-and-verdict dialogue (4:9-15) that depends on the murder just narrated.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the resumptive adverb עוד ('again') plus the return of Adam and Eve as subjects (4:25, וידע אדם עוד את אשתו -- the same referent as 4:1's האדם, not a fresh subject), signaling a discourse resumption after the seven-generation Cain digression; closes on the etiological notice that men began to call on Yahweh's name (4:26), which has no counterpart in the Cain material and functions as this short unit's own closing formula. It stands apart from M8-Gen-005 because the Gen.10 no-split precedent governs branches of one formally-headed list about a single subject, while Cain's and Seth's lines are a genuine subject-return opening a contrasting lineage.

boundary_rationale: Opens on "This is the book of the generations of Adam" (5:1) and repeats one formula (age at first son, years lived after, total years, 'then he died') across nine complete generations, closing at 5:31, the last verse to carry the full formula; 5:32 (Noah begetting Shem, Ham, and Japheth) truncates the formula entirely -- no years-after, no total, no died -- and functions as a hinge to the material that follows, whose own toledot at 6:9-10 restates the begetting. This truncated-member pattern is text-internal, independent of the setumah that also happens to fall after 5:31.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 5:32 inside this unit as the tenth, open-ended member of the same begetting pattern -- a real, textually arguable alternative, not adopted because 5:32 supplies only the begetting half of the formula and leaves its completion to the onward narrative rather than closing itself the way every other member does.

boundary_rationale: Opens at 5:32 (Noah's sons named, the ויהי+בן hinge verse that breaks every prior member's ויחי+numeral pattern), corroborated by the verified WLC setumah after 5:31 and by WEB's own paragraphing, which isolates 5:32 as a single-verse paragraph bracketed on both sides. Moves into the compressed, mixed-register account of pre-flood corruption: 6:1-4 (the Nephilim/renown-men notice, genuinely etiological -- it names a group and accounts for its origin) and 6:5-8 (Yahweh's interior grief and a verdict taking shape, which names nothing and explains no custom, so 'etiological' does not fit this half). Closes on the pivot 'Noah found favor in Yahweh's eyes' (6:8), corroborated by a verified petuchah after 6:8 that was previously uncited. The near-verbatim restatement of 5:32's begetting triad at 6:9-10 (across the intervening 6:1-8) is a resumptive-repetition (Wiederaufnahme) configuration and is directionally ambiguous -- it is at least as consistent with 5:32 closing the preceding genealogy as with 5:32 opening this unit -- and is recorded here as preserved counterevidence rather than one-directional support.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 5:32 as the closing, open-ended member of the Adam genealogy (M8-Gen-007) rather than this unit's opening hinge -- a genuine, preserved alternative given the resumptive-repetition ambiguity of 6:9-10's restatement; not adopted because the register break (ויהי/ויחי) and the shared wayehi frame linking 5:32 to 6:1 are one-directional signals that the restatement itself is not.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a fresh divine command, "Yahweh said to Noah, Come with all of your household into the ship" (7:1), immediately following the double compliance formula that closes the ark commission at 6:22; runs as one continuous action through the seven-day boarding notice (7:5), the flood's onset and rise, closing on 'The waters flooded the earth one hundred fifty days' (7:24). The asymmetry between the two 'did all that X commanded' formulas is text-internal, not marker-only: 6:22's formula closes the ark-commission's own command-and-execution frame immediately before a fresh divine speech opens at 7:1, while 7:5's formula is an abbreviated echo sitting mid-sequence with no new topic following it.

The interior-monologue/externally-addressed-speech shift at 8:21/9:1 is treated as a real, if soft, seam separating this unit from the following covenant chapter, so no forward merge is made.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the blessing-and-mandate speech (9:1, ויברך אלהים את נח ואת בניו), echoing the creation blessing of 1:28 and framed by the same addressee (Noah and his sons); closes at 9:7, immediately before a second, formally re-introduced speech at 9:8 (ויאמר אלהים אל נח ואל בניו אתו לאמר) restating both addressees -- a genuine speech-formula boundary, not a bare repetition, corroborated by a setumah after 9:7. The start at 9:1 itself carries no independent Hebrew marker; it stands on the blessing formula's content echo of 1:28 and the addressee frame, since marker-absence is not counter-evidence under the addendum.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 9:1-17 as one unit on the ground that both halves address the same audience with no scene break -- withdrawn once the fresh speech-introduction formula at 9:8 was recognized as text-driving rather than a bare restatement; see the new M8-Gen-119 (9:8-17) for the covenant-sign continuation.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the re-introduced addressee formula "God said to Noah and to his sons with him" (9:8, ויאמר אלהים אל נח ואל בניו אתו לאמר), the only occurrence in this stretch combining the divine subject, both addressees restated by name, and לאמר. The same verb-plus-divine-subject class recurs twice more inside the span -- 9:12 (וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים, no addressee, no לאמר) and 9:17 (addressee restated, still no לאמר) -- and both are recorded here as internal-seam counterevidence rather than left undisclosed; neither carries the full form that opens the unit, so neither is treated as a chunk edge. The whole span is uninterrupted reported speech: no altar, no divided animals, no enacted rite of any kind, only Yahweh naming a sign already in the sky, which is why the form is a covenant-establishing speech rather than a covenant_ceremony (contrast Gen.15's actual covenant-cutting ritual). Closes on 'This is the token of the covenant which I have established' (9:17), corroborated by a verified petuchah after 9:17.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Labeling this 'covenant_ceremony' by analogy with Gen.15 -- rejected because nothing is enacted here; the whole unit is speech naming an already-existing sign, not a ritual action. Splitting at 9:12 or 9:17 on the strength of the same speech-formula class that opens the unit at 9:8 -- rejected because neither internal occurrence restates both addressees with לאמר the way 9:8 does.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the toledot formula "This is the history of the generations of Shem" (11:10) and repeats one two-part formula -- a begetting notice plus 'lived N years after, and became the father of more sons and daughters' -- across eight complete generations (Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor), each closed by its own setumah; the series stops after 11:25. Verse 11:26 (Terah begetting three sons) supplies only the begetting half and lacks the lived-after/more-sons-and-daughters half every one of the eight prior members carries -- the Gen.11 formula's own and only two-part shape. It does not lack a total-years line or a death notice, since neither element occurs anywhere in this series; those belong to Gen.5's four-part formula (M8-Gen-007), not Gen.11's, and citing them here was a description error, not a feature of this list.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the formal vision-reception formula "Yahweh's word came to Abram in a vision" (15:1, במחזה -- no dream vocabulary occurs anywhere in the chapter); runs as one unbroken two-party dialogue between Abram and Yahweh with no exit or location change anywhere in the chapter, and the WLC treats all of Gen.15 as one undivided paragraph (no marker between the setumah after 14:24 and the setumah after 15:21). The merge does not rest on 'same-night continuity', which the chapter's own time notices contradict (stars are counted at 15:5, Abram drives off birds of prey in daylight at 15:11, the sun is only going down at 15:12 and has gone down again at 15:17) -- that claim is withdrawn. A live internal onset at 15:12 (wayehi plus a state change: deep sleep, terror, and great darkness falling on Abram) is the same signal class recorded as a chunk-relevant onset at Gen.40.20, and is recorded here as preserved counterevidence, subordinated for the same reason: it marks a beat within one continuous, undeparted encounter, not a chunk edge. Closes on the land-grant boundary description (15:18-21). This span exactly equals chapter 15, so confidence is set to medium_low under the pilot-book's mechanical chapter-shape cap; the underlying evidence for the unit's unity (total absence of any WLC division across the whole chapter, no participant/location change) is otherwise strong, and the cap is mechanical, not literary doubt.

boundary_rationale: Opens on Esau's private resolve, "Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing...Then I will kill my brother Jacob" (27:41); runs through Rebekah's countermeasure and her pretext to Isaac (27:46), directly and immediately answered by Isaac's action (28:1) with no reset of any kind, and closes on Esau's own reactive third marriage (28:9). The span contains a real internal recurrence not previously disclosed: 28:6 (וירא עשו כי ברך יצחק) and 28:8 (וירא עשו כי רעות בנות כנען) are the same וירא+subject+כי perception-plus-consequence construction credited as a cycle-opening signal at 30:1 and 30:9, with 28:9 as the resulting action. It is subordinated here rather than treated as a chunk edge because it functions differently from its counterparts: 28:6-9 is Esau reacting to decisions others already made (Jacob's blessing, his own prior marriages), a response-notice closing this unit's aftermath arc, whereas 30:1 and 30:9 each open a new action their subjects themselves initiate (Rachel's and then Leah's surrogate strategies).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 28:6 or 28:8 on the strength of the same construction credited as an edge at 30:1/30:9 -- rejected because the construction's function differs: here it introduces a reactive coda to an already-completed send-off, not a new cycle the perceiving character initiates.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the itinerary notice "They traveled from Bethel...and Rachel travailed" (35:16); runs through Rachel's death and burial, closing on the genuine etiological formula "the Pillar of Rachel's grave to this day" (35:20, הִוא מַצֶּבֶת קְבֻרַת רָחֵל עַד הַיּוֹם). Full arc: round 1 closed this unit at 35:21, crediting its נסע formula as a closing beat despite treating a construction it called 'identical' to this unit's own opener at 35:16, with no stated differentiator; the revision round found no such differentiator and moved the close to 35:20. The micro round corrected the revision's own premise: 35:16 (וַיִּסְעוּ, plural, unexpressed subject, with the min-source phrase מִבֵּית אֵל) and 35:21 (וַיִּסַּע, singular, with the explicit subject יִשְׂרָאֵל itself bearing the verse's atnach, no source phrase) are not identical -- they share only the root נסע. The real, text-supplied differentiator is the participant designation shift from יַעֲקֹב to יִשְׂרָאֵל at exactly 35:20/21 (sustained through two further occurrences in 35:22), which is what actually distinguishes the two itinerary clauses and corroborates, rather than drives, the close at 35:20.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing at 35:21, as this decision held after round 1 -- withdrawn not because the two נסע clauses are grammatically identical (they are not) but because no differentiator was stated for treating the construction as terminal at 35:21 when it opens this same unit five verses earlier, and because the actual עד היום closing formula at 35:20 went unrecorded.

boundary_rationale: Opens on "Israel traveled, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder" (35:21, וַיִּסַּע יִשְׂרָאֵל), the same נסע root as the preceding unit's opener at 35:16 but a morphologically distinct clause (see M8-Gen-077), now correctly read as this unit's own onset. This resolves the anaphor at 35:22a: 'While Israel lived in that land' (בָּאָרֶץ הַהִוא) refers back to Migdal Eder, named in 35:21. Verse 35:22 remains bipartite and is retained whole under the whole-verse span constraint: the Masoretic mid-verse break, a petuchah functioning as piska be'emtsa pasuq (single-witness, retagged consistently with the 35:29 marker below), separates Reuben's sin (22a, narrative continuation of 35:21) from the list header 'Now the sons of Jacob were twelve' (22b), which is itself a boundary-driving list-register formula launching the four-member Leah/Rachel/Bilhah/Zilpah series (23-26) and bound by inclusio to 35:26's closing 'these are the sons of Jacob'. This internal 22a|22b seam -- narrative giving way to register, reinforced by the coinciding mid-verse petuchah and the verse's own atnach -- is a real sub-unit division; it is not enacted as a chunk edge only because the whole-verse constraint forbids splitting 22a from 22b, not because no seam exists there. The span is accordingly composite rather than a pure list: itinerary/narrative (21-22a), register list (22b-26), and a death-and-burial report (27-29) -- outnumbering the list in verse count -- closing on Isaac's death formula (35:27-29), corroborated by a petuchah after 35:29 (single-witness) before the fresh toledot at 36:1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Starting at 35:22, leaving 35:21 with the preceding unit -- withdrawn because it separated the נסע construction's two instances inconsistently and left 35:22a's locative anaphor without its antecedent. A second, distinct alternative -- splitting at 35:22a|22b, where the register formula actually begins -- is acknowledged as a real seam rather than a null option: it is suppressed only by the whole-verse span constraint (Reuben's sin and the list header cannot be separated at the verse level), not by any absence of textual signal.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the journey's first leg, "Israel traveled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices" (46:1); the reassurance that follows is explicitly framed as מַרְאֹת הַלַּיְלָה, 'visions of the night' (46:2) -- no form of חלם/חֲלוֹם occurs anywhere in this span, unlike the genuine dream-reports elsewhere in Genesis (37:5, 40:5), so the label reflects the span's own reception vocabulary rather than the dream_report label used for formally different spans. Closes on the itinerary summary listing the household's departure (46:5-7).

boundary_rationale: Opens on "Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way...to Goshen" (46:28, fronted-object-plus-qatal וְאֶת יְהוּדָה שָׁלַח לְפָנָיו), corroborated by a verified WLC petuchah after 46:27 falling exactly at this unit's own start -- strong-class corroboration under the addendum, previously uncited. Runs through the reunion, Joseph's same-day coaching of his brothers on how to answer Pharaoh (46:31-34, using the hiphil נגד, 'I will go up and tell Pharaoh'), and the audience with Pharaoh itself (47:1, 'Joseph went in and told Pharaoh', the same hiphil נגד verbatim executing the stated plan) -- an announcement-and-fulfillment continuity that is itself a text signal binding the units regardless of the chapter line between them. Jacob's own presentation and blessing follow, closing on Joseph's provisioning of the family (47:12), text-internally carried into the following material by 47:13's own disjunctive picking up 47:12's 'bread' (לֶחֶם).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at the chapter boundary (46:34/47:1), treating the audience with Pharaoh as its own scene -- rejected because the identical verb root and the verbatim match between plan and execution show the chapter division, not the Hebrew, was doing the separating.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a new occasion notice, "After these things, someone said to Joseph, Behold, your father is sick" (48:1); Joseph brings Manasseh and Ephraim with him in this same verse, and Jacob's sustained first-person speech (48:3-7) both recounts the Luz theophany and Rachel's death AND formally names and adopts the two sons already present (48:5-6), so the sons' absence is not, and cannot be, the ground for the 48:7/48:8 division. The real division is discourse mode: Jacob's first-person speech, including the fronted וַאֲנִי at 48:7, gives way to wayyiqtol narration at 48:8 ('Israel saw Joseph's sons, and said, Who are these?'), which restarts the scene's action as if seeing them for the first time.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Claiming the sons are not yet brought forward as the ground for this division -- withdrawn, directly contradicted by 48:1b and 48:5-6 within this same span; the real ground is the discourse-mode shift from sustained first-person speech to narrated action.

Closes on the extra-portion promise to Joseph (48:21-22).

boundary_rationale: Opens on verse 49:28, which the Masoretic athnach divides into an enumerative colophon closing the preceding poem (28a, 'All these are the twelve tribes of Israel...he blessed everyone according to his own blessing' -- in form, a closing summary belonging with M8-Gen-114's material) and the prose resumption this decision is actually about (28b, 'and this is what their father spoke to them, and blessed them', itself already a summary transitioning into the burial instructions). Verse-level tiling cannot split 28a from 28b, so the whole verse is retained here, with 28a's residue recorded rather than left implicit. Runs through Jacob's burial instructions, closing on his death (49:33).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Describing 49:28 as if it were straightforwardly this chunk's own 'opening' evidence without noting its bipartite, colophon-then-resumption character -- withdrawn as imprecise; the corrected description above is more accurate about what the verse actually contains.

boundary_rationale: This is one unbroken divine turn from Moses's first objection through the elders/Pharaoh script, opening on Moses's own speaker-turn away from the divine commission that closes at 3:10, 'ויאמר משה אל האלהים' ('Moses said to God'). 3:15's 'ויאמר עוד' (said further) is a same-speaker continuation particle, not a fresh-turn formula -- the same class of particle recurs mid-unit, non-boundary, at 4:6 inside the uncontested sign-sequence decision 012 (word order differs: עוד precedes the subject at 3:15 but follows the addressee at 4:6, so the two are same-class continuatives rather than an identical construction). 3:16's bare imperative continues that same speech with no intervening speaker change. The real seam is Moses's own speaker-turn at 4:1, 'Moses answered, But, behold, they will not believe me.'

boundary_rationale: Restored to its original span after a round-1 split-then-reversal: round 1 split this into 014 (4:18-20) and a new sibling 145 (4:21-23) on the strength of 4:21's messenger formula, but the round-1 record never explained why that formula counts as boundary-driving there while the identical formula at 4:19 does not. Both v.19 ('Yahweh said to Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt') and v.21 ('Yahweh said to Moses, When you go back into Egypt...') are symmetric bare divine-speech reopenings addressed to Moses with no stated differentiator between them; under the same continuation-class precedent that governs 3:15/4:6 (a same-speaker reopening is not automatically a fresh-turn boundary), neither reopening is treated as boundary-driving here, and the whole of Jethro's farewell, the go-return command, Moses's departure, and the firstborn oracle stay together as one preparation-and-departure unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could still split at either 4:19 or 4:21 (but not both, absent a stated differentiator), or split at both if a rule is adopted that every bare 'Yahweh said to Moses' reopening is independently boundary-driving regardless of symmetry with its neighbors; that rule is not adopted here because it would also force splits at comparable reopenings elsewhere (e.g. within the sign-sequence unit, decision 012) that this campaign treats as internal.

boundary_rationale: The Sabbath-sign speech (31:12-17) and its closing colophon (31:18, 'he gave Moses the two tablets...written with God's finger') together close the whole Sinai instruction-giving complex begun at 25:1. 31:18's 'ככלתו לדבר אתו' is not the same construction as 31:11's 'ככל אשר צויתך יעשו' -- ככלתו is כ plus the infinitive construct of כלה ('finish') with a 3ms suffix, a temporal clause subordinate to the wayyiqtol main verb ויתן ('when he had finished speaking with him'), while 31:11 is כ plus the noun כל with a relative clause naming a prospective, first-person divine command; the shared כ- is coincidental, not a shared construction. Nor does 31:11 belong to the book's retrospective כן-colophon family (39:32, 39:42, 40:16), so 31:18 has no genuine construction-parallel anywhere nearby; it stands as its own distinct completion-of-speech idiom. 31:18 still reads backward on ordinary syntax (a wayyiqtol matrix clause with a subordinate temporal clause naturally continues the speech just concluded), and this unit's own opening is independently corroborated by a WLC setumah after 31:17.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could still keep 31:18 attached forward to the golden-calf narrative as its dramatic-irony setup; that reading was the original one and is not without merit, and without any named colophon-family match the case for reading 31:18 backward rests on ordinary syntax alone.

oshb:Exod.31.18 'ויתן אל משה ככלתו לדבר אתו' -- כ + infinitive construct + suffix, subordinate temporal clause, its own distinct idiom
oshb:Exod.31.11 'ככל אשר צויתך יעשו' -- prospective divine speech, not a construction parallel to 31:18 and not a member of the retrospective 39:32/39:42/40:16 colophon family either

The people have no knowledge of the tablets (Moses's private possession); the true antecedent for their alarm is the forty-day sojourn established at 24:18, not the tablet-giving specifically, so this scene is read as its own narrative unit rather than a chapter-crossing continuation of 31:18's colophon.

boundary_rationale: The covenant stipulations restated after the divine self-proclamation run through the command to write them down and Moses's forty-day fast, closing at 'he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten commandments' (34:28). The tablet framework at 34:1 ('Chisel two stone tablets like the first') is recorded as evidence for a larger 34:1-28 frame, not as a boundary marker for this narrower 34:10-28 span, since that verse lies outside this unit's own edges. A WLC petuchah falls after 34:26, inside this span, and is recorded as an internal, unadopted seam bearing on the 34:27-28 placement rather than as this unit's own boundary evidence.

boundary_rationale: This one-verse notice, 'Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting was finished. The children of Israel did according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses; so they did,' is a standalone completion colophon rather than the tail of the preceding gold-plate item panel. Its construction, 'ותכל...ככל אשר צוה יהוה את משה כן עשו,' is the fuller ככל...כן עשה/עשו colophon-family formula, genuinely distinct in scope and construction from the short item-specific refrain ('כאשר צוה יהוה את משה') that closes every other panel in this chapter, including the gold plate immediately preceding it. The true family has exactly three members: this verse, 39:42 ('ככל אשר צוה יהוה את משה כן עשו בני ישראל,' verbatim identical to 39:32b), and 40:16. 31:11 ('ככל אשר צויתך יעשו') is not a member despite the earlier record's claim: it is first-person divine speech (צויתך) with a prospective yiqtol (יעשו) and no כן apodosis, a forward-looking command about Bezalel and Oholiab's future work, not a retrospective compliance report -- it is this family's prospective counterpart, not one of its members. The WLC brackets 39:32 as its own one-verse paragraph, with a setumah after 39:31 and a petuchah after 39:32, corroborating its independence -- the same one-verse-decision precedent already established at decision 158 (38:8).

This is not adopted because 39:33 opens with its own fresh, independent head, 'ויביאו את המשכן אל משה' -- a new participant movement (the finished work brought TO Moses) -- while 39:32's ותכל is completion-scoped over the construction narrative that precedes it, not an introduction to what follows; the envelope is a genuine literary echo but not a claim on this verse's own syntactic head.

boundary_rationale: Yahweh's final instruction speech runs from 'On the first day of the first month you shall raise up the tabernacle' through the anointing and consecration commands, closing on the backward-facing compliance colophon at v.16. This is one continuous command speech to one addressee (Moses) throughout, with an unbroken weqatal chain across most of vv.9-15 -- but 40:14, 'ואת בניו תקריב' ('and his sons you shall bring near'), is a fronted-object-plus-yiqtol clause, word-for-word identical to 29:8 and the same construction decision 156 treats as boundary-driving at 29:15. The differentiator that keeps this a single unit despite that fronting is scope: ch.29's fronted items (the bull, the first ram, the second ram) each open a substantial, multi-verse standalone rite warranting its own decision, whereas 40:14's fronting sits inside one rapid, single-addressee checklist of setup actions within an otherwise unbroken command speech, not a rite-boundary of comparable weight. 40:16's colophon, 'ככל אשר צוה יהוה אתו כן עשה,' belongs to the same retrospective family as 39:32 and 39:42, not to 31:11 (a distinct, prospective formula wrongly cited as a parallel in an earlier record).
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could still split at 40:14 on the strength of the same fronted-object construction that drives the 156 boundary, treating any instance of that construction as boundary-driving regardless of scope; that rule is not adopted here because 40:14 is one clause inside a checklist rather than the head of its own substantial rite.

strongest_rejected_alternative: A reader could treat 1:1-2 as its own one-paragraph superscription separate from the herd case, but the herd case has no independent opening formula of its own -- it is simply the first of three 'if' clauses hanging off the general instruction in v.2, so severing them manufactures a boundary the text does not mark.

The parallel to MT 6:11 (=WEB 6:18) offered against this boundary fails on inspection: MT 6:11's יֹאכֲלֶנָּה is 3ms, not 2mp, so that verse carries no addressee shift and is not 'the same formula class.'
