boundary_rationale: A single-verse prohibition, 'you shall not sacrifice to Yahweh your God an ox or a sheep in which is a defect' (לֹא תִזְבַּח֩ לַיהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ שׁ֣וֹר וָשֶׂ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה בוֹ֙ מ֔וּם...), stands bracketed by a setumah on each side -- one after 16:22 closing the Asherah-pole/pillar pair, another after 17:1 itself -- both of the same samekh class that also stands after 16:20 and, internal to the preceding decision (096), after 16:21. The object class shifts across that first bracket, from planted or erected cultic objects (אֲשֵׁרָה, מַצֵּבָה) to a sacrificial animal's physical qualification (שׁוֹר וָשֶׂה ... מוּם), a genuine content break rather than the chapter number, and the setumah bracket corroborates it on both ends before the idolatry-investigation case law opens its own fresh כִּי protasis at v.2. That bracket is corroboration only, not the driver, and it is not distinctive within its own neighborhood: 096, the immediately preceding decision, treats a setumah of this same class -- the one after 16:21 -- as real countervailing evidence it merges across rather than as confidence-lifting support, so the same marker class cannot be overridable at 16:21 and confidence-raising at 16:22/17:1 without an argument for the asymmetry, and none is available. The break across the 16:22|17:1 seam is also less clean than a bare object-class shift suggests: 16:22 closes on אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׂנֵ֖א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ ('which Yahweh your God hates') and 17:1 closes on כִּ֧י תוֹעֲבַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ הֽוּא ('for it is an abomination to Yahweh your God') -- both prohibitions end on the same kind of divine-attitude rationale clause, a formal tie running across the very seam this decision calls a clean content break. Disclosed rather than suppressed, that residual link, together with the marker-class asymmetry against 096, caps confidence at medium: the object-class shift and the setumah bracket still support the span, but neither the marker class nor the content break is as clean as a high rating would require.

boundary_rationale: A temporal clause opens on 'It shall be, when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write himself a copy of this law' (וְהָיָ֣ה כְשִׁבְתּ֔וֹ עַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֣א מַמְלַכְתּ֑וֹ וְכָ֨תַב ל֜וֹ אֶת מִשְׁנֵ֨ה הַתּוֹרָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ עַל סֵ֔פֶר מִלִּפְנֵ֥י הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים הַלְוִיִּֽם), closing ch.17 and the king law on the not-lifted-up-above-his-brothers formula. This decision is held at low confidence rather than lifted from insufficient_evidence: WLC brackets the whole of 17:14-20 as one paragraph, with no mark internal to it; the sole textual argument for the cut, the וְהָיָה כְשִׁבְתּוֹ clause, has no Masoretic corroboration of its own; and the same formula-family (וְהָיָה כִּי/אִם/כְ) receives inconsistent treatment across this book -- unit-opening at 11:13 where a setumah backs it, contested as unit-opening at 11:29 within this same range, and now asserted here with no marker at all. The grammatical-subject claim once made for this span is corrected rather than repeated: the whole of vv.15-20 is not uniformly third-person. 17:15 addresses the people directly in the second singular about installing the king (שׂ֣וֹם תָּשִׂ֤ים עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ מֶ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בּ֑וֹ מִקֶּ֣רֶב אַחֶ֗יךָ תָּשִׂ֤ים עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ מֶ֔לֶךְ לֹ֣א תוּכַ֗ל לָתֵ֤ת עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ אִ֣ישׁ נָכְרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא אָחִ֖יךָ הֽוּא), and 17:16 turns to the people again in the plural mid-verse, citing Yahweh's own prior word to them (וַֽיהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר לָכֶ֔ם לֹ֣א תֹסִפ֗וּן, 'you shall never again return that way'). Because that plural citation still falls inside v.16, the uninterrupted third-person-singular run about the king cannot begin at 17:16b as earlier stated; it begins only at 17:17 (וְלֹ֤א יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ֙ נָשִׁ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָס֖וּר לְבָב֑וֹ וְכֶ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב לֹ֥א יַרְבֶּה לּ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד), the first verse entirely after the plural re-addressing, and continues without a further re-addressing of the people through v.20. That narrower run is what argues, weakly, for treating v.18 as a fresh moment within it, and this held-low disposition is unchanged by the correction.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 17:14-20 as one undivided king law, closed only by the setumah after v.20, is at least as defensible as the split: nothing marks the 17|18 seam internally, the subject does not shift again after 17:16, and the accumulation clauses of vv.16-17 and the writing clause of v.18 are equally third-person predications about the same figure. I do not adopt the merge outright because the temporal clause at v.18 does mark a real shift in the king's own timeline (a later moment, once enthroned, rather than the initial restrictions on his power), but I also do not force the split to a confident verdict, since neither reading has the kind of textual or Masoretic support this campaign otherwise requires.

boundary_rationale: Ch.18 opens on Levi's landless-status principle, 'The priests and the Levites — all the tribe of Levi — shall have no portion nor inheritance with Israel' (לֹֽא יִ֠הְיֶה לַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם כָּל שֵׁ֧בֶט לֵוִ֛י חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה עִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל), closing on the same principle restated in v.2 ('Yahweh is his inheritance'), before a fresh schedule-head formula opens the specific priestly dues in v.3 (see the new sibling decision). A setumah closes v.2 exactly at this span's end, corroborating the split.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping vv.1-5 merged as one continuous priestly-support unit reads smoothly, since the dues in vv.3-5 illustrate the principle just stated; the setumah after v.2 and the formula-headed opening of v.3 — the same וְזֶה + construct-noun device used at 15:2 and 19:4 to open a schedule — both mark a real internal seam the merged reading would erase.

boundary_rationale: A fresh schedule-head formula opens the unit, 'And this shall be the priests' due from the people' (וְזֶ֡ה יִהְיֶה֩ מִשְׁפַּ֨ט הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ת הָעָ֗ם), the same וְזֶה + construct-noun device this campaign already credits as opening a schedule at 15:2 (וְזֶה֮ דְּבַ֣ר הַשְּׁמִטָּה֒) and 19:4 (וְזֶה֙ דְּבַ֣ר הָרֹצֵ֔חַ), listing the shoulder, jaws, and stomach from slaughtered animals, the firstfruits of grain, wine, oil, and fleece, closing on the election-and-service rationale (v.5) before the migrating-Levite case opens fresh at v.6. A setumah closes 18:2 immediately before this span begins, corroborating the split from the preceding decision.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The whole of 18:1-5 could remain one Levitical-support unit, general principle plus specific dues; the setumah after 18:2 and the formula-headed opening at v.3, matching a device this campaign treats as boundary-marking elsewhere in the same law code, both argue for treating the schedule as its own decision.

strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could treat this brief provision as an appendix to the general priestly-portion law rather than its own case, but its fresh protasis addressing a specific relocation scenario, distinct from the general rule’s blanket statement, marks a real case-chain seam.

boundary_rationale: A fresh conditional opens the divination prohibition, 'When you have come into the land which Yahweh your God gives you, you shall not learn to imitate the abominations of those nations' (כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ בָּ֣א אֶל הָאָ֔רֶץ...לֹֽא תִלְמַ֣ד לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּתוֹעֲבֹ֖ת הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָהֵֽם), cataloguing diviners, sorcerers, and necromancers, and closing on the self-sufficiency demand 'You shall be blameless before Yahweh your God' (תָּמִ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה עִ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ, v.13). A setumah closes v.13 exactly at this span's end; v.14's own contrastive clause, 'but Yahweh your God has not given you thus' (וְאַתָּ֕ה לֹ֣א כֵ֔ן נָ֛תַן לְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ), is syntactically incomplete without v.15's answer and belongs to the following decision as its contrastive setup.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping v.14 inside this decision, as originally drafted, reads the driven-out-because-of-abominations theme as running through the verse; that clause actually stands at v.12, one verse earlier, and v.14's own contrastive complement is left dangling without v.15 — the setumah after v.13 marks the more defensible close.

boundary_rationale: The contrastive setup opens on 'But Yahweh your God has not given you thus' (וְאַתָּ֕ה לֹ֣א כֵ֔ן נָ֛תַן לְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ), the pivot of a them/you opposition that v.14 states and v.15 answers: the nations 'listen' to diviners and soothsayers (אֶל מְעֹנְנִ֥ים וְאֶל קֹסְמִ֖ים יִשְׁמָ֑עוּ) where Israel instead 'listens' to the prophet Yahweh raises up (אֵלָ֖יו תִּשְׁמָעֽוּן) -- the shared שמע root marking two different objects of the same verb of attention, deliberately set against each other rather than two independent statements. That contrast, not a syntactic dependency, is what binds v.14 to v.15: v.14's own clause is grammatically complete on its own (נָתַן takes the adverbial לֹא כֵן with לְךָ as its indirect object), and v.15 is an independent clause with its own verb (יָקִ֥ים), its own fronted object (נָבִ֨יא), and its own indirect object (לְךָ֖); v.15 supplies nothing that v.14's sentence itself lacks. The unit runs through Yahweh's ratifying speech (vv.17-19), grounded explicitly in the people's own Horeb request for a mediator (v.16), closing on the accountability formula before the false-prophet test opens with its own אַךְ pivot at v.20.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening this decision at v.15, as originally drafted, is defensible if v.14 is read purely as the divination law's closing generalization, complete in itself and not part of the mediator promise. Checked against the grammar, that reading is not ruled out syntactically -- v.14's clause does not depend on v.15 for its completion -- but it is ruled out by the them/you, שמע-root contrast the two verses build together, and the setumah closing v.13 (not v.14) confirms that the Masoretic tradition already treats v.14 as belonging with what follows rather than what precedes.

boundary_rationale: Two prohibitions share one exact closing formula and near-identical syntax: 'You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together' (לֹֽא תַחֲרֹ֥שׁ בְּשׁוֹר וּבַחֲמֹ֖ר יַחְדָּֽו) and 'You shall not wear a mixed fabric, wool and linen together' (לֹ֤א תִלְבַּשׁ֙ שַֽׁעַטְנֵ֔ז צֶ֥מֶר וּפִשְׁתִּ֖ים יַחְדָּֽו), both closing on יַחְדָּו and both naming two disparate things joined that should stay apart — a genuine lexical and structural pairing that the seed-mixture prohibition immediately before them (22:9) does not share, since it lacks יַחְדָּו entirely and carries its own פֶּן clause instead. A setumah stands after each of 22:10 and 22:11 individually, marking against as well as for this merge; the shared formula is judged to outweigh the internal mark, but only at low confidence, since the Masoretic tradition itself keeps the two verses apart.
strongest_rejected_alternative: WLC's own individual setumah after 22:10 argues for keeping the two prohibitions apart as separate decisions, matching the manuscript's granularity exactly; I merge them instead because they are the only pair in this run of three that actually share both their closing word (יַחְדָּו) and their syntactic shape, a bond the seed-mixture prohibition preceding them lacks — but the internal mark is real countervailing evidence, not merely absent, and confidence is set low to reflect that.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse positive command, 'you shall make yourselves fringes on the four corners of your cloak' (גְּדִלִ֖ים תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּ֑ךְ עַל אַרְבַּ֛ע כַּנְפ֥וֹת כְּסוּתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּכַסֶּה בָּֽהּ), stands as its own case between the mixture prohibitions and the virginity-dispute law: 22:9's לֹא תִזְרַ֥ע, 22:10's לֹֽא תַחֲרֹ֥שׁ and 22:11's לֹ֤א תִלְבַּשׁ֙ are all prohibitions, and 22:12 alone commands positively, before 22:13 opens a fresh case on its own כִּֽי יִקַּ֥ח protasis. That mood contrast -- the sole positive command in a run of לֹא-prohibitions -- is the text signal driving this decision. The setumah after 22:11 opening this span and the one after 22:12 closing it are real, but they are not distinctive within the run: Deut.22.9, 22.10, 22.11 and 22.12 each carry a samekh-class mark, so every member of the run is bracketed the same way, and the bracket around 22:12 corroborates the boundary without adding anything a plain content-and-mood reading does not already supply. That is the same configuration the campaign already prices at medium one verse earlier: M8-Deut-126 is a one-verse span in this identical series (22:9), bracketed by a samekh at each edge exactly as this one is, resting on a text signal of comparable weight -- a unique elaborating פֶּן clause and vocabulary distinct from its neighbors -- and it is priced medium. High for 127 and medium for 126 could not both stand without an explicit argument for treating 127's signal as stronger, and the mood contrast does not obviously outrank 126's grounds. Confidence is capped at medium so the two single-verse decisions in this run are priced alike.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might attach this to the preceding mixture cluster as a related garment law, but it is the only positive command in the group and concerns marking a garment rather than prohibiting a mixture, a real functional difference.

This is MT's own 23:1, the second WEB/MT chapter-line offset in the book, so every original-language citation across this seam must carry the MT number with a (=WEB ...) pairing rather than a bare WEB number under an oshb: prefix. Two samekh markers bracket the verse on both sides (after MT 22:29 and after MT 23:1) per parashah_two_witness.json -- weak-class corroboration for treating it as its own transmitted unit, not the driver of the cut. Content pulls in both directions: the verse completes the sexual-offense case chain preceding it, but MT 23:2's מַמְזֵר (illegitimate birth) reads naturally as its own forward sequel into the assembly-exclusion list, which is why the singleton stays low confidence rather than folding into either neighbor.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reader following MT's own chapter division would attach this verse to the assembly-exclusion unit opening at 23:2 rather than closing the preceding sexual-offense chain; its content (a father's-wife prohibition, structurally identical to curse six of the Ebal liturgy at 27:20) still reads more naturally as the last entry in the case-law sequence than as the first entry in a list of who may not enter the assembly, so the chain-closing reading is kept, with the citation defect that obscured the underlying MT verse now corrected.

The unifying signal is the refrain בִּקְהַל יְהוָה ('into Yahweh's assembly'), recurring at MT 23:2, 3, 4, and 9 regardless of which class is being excluded or readmitted -- a register bound by repeated formula rather than four independent case-law protases. strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could split the permanent exclusions (vv.1-3) from the qualified, time-limited exclusions (vv.4-8), since the Ammonite/Moabite ban is 'forever' while Edomites/Egyptians are readmitted after three generations, and the internal setumot after MT 23:2, 3, 7, and 8 would even support such a division. But all four entries share the one בִּקְהַל יְהוָה refrain opening and (for the readmitted classes) closing their own clause, building one cumulative membership rule rather than four unrelated statutes, so the weak-class internal markers are outweighed by the refrain.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse exemption, “When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out in the army…he shall be free at home one year” (כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה חֲדָשָׁה לֹא יֵצֵא בַּצָּבָא), echoes the officers’ speech of 20:7 but stands here as its own brief case bracketed by unrelated pledge and kidnapping laws.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might merge this with ch.20’s war exemptions given the shared topic, but the two passages are not adjacent and serve different functions (a battlefield announcement there, a standalone civil law here), so I keep it as its own case in its own context.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse prohibition, “No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone as a pledge, for he takes a life in pledge” (לֹא יַחֲבֹל רֵחַיִם וָרָכֶב כִּי נֶפֶשׁ הוּא חֹבֵל), stands alone between the newlywed exemption and the kidnapping law, its own rationale (a millstone is a household’s livelihood, “a life”) closing it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could group this with the later pledge-taking etiquette of vv.10-13 as one pledge-law cluster, but three unrelated cases (kidnapping, leprosy, pledge etiquette itself opening fresh) intervene, showing the chapter proceeds case by case rather than by topical grouping.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Deut.24.6 “No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone as a pledge, for he takes a life in pledge.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse capital law, “If a man is found stealing any of his brothers of the children of Israel…that thief shall die” (כִּי יִמָּצֵא אִישׁ גֹּנֵב נֶפֶשׁ מֵאֶחָיו מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל…וּמֵת הַגַּנָּב הַהוּא), closing on the purge-the-evil refrain shared with several other capital cases in this code, before the leprosy protocol opens v.8.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might attach this to the millstone-pledge law as another “taking” offense, but kidnapping a person and pledging a millstone share no legal logic beyond a coincidental adjacency; each opens its own fresh protasis.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Deut.24.7 “If a man is found stealing any of his brothers of the children of Israel…
oshb:Deut.24.7 וּמֵת הַגַּנָּב הַהוּא וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ

boundary_rationale: A fresh imperative opens, 'Be careful in the plague of leprosy, that you observe diligently and do according to all that the Levitical priests teach you' -- oshb:Deut.24.8 הִשָּׁמֶר בְּנֶגַע הַצָּרַעַת לִשְׁמֹר מְאֹד וְלַעֲשׂוֹת, addressed in second-plural instruction through the priests, closing on the priestly-teaching clause before the memory-command register of v.9 opens fresh. Formerly grouped with v.9 as a single decision; the identical זָכוֹר אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה construction that M8-Deut-155 already treats as unit-opening at 25:17 recurs verbatim at v.9, so the two verses are now split to apply that criterion consistently. Setumah after MT 24.8 corroborates the close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping vv.8-9 as one instruction, with the Miriam memory functioning merely as the diligence command's grounding illustration, was the prior reading; it cannot stand alongside M8-Deut-155's own citation of this exact verse as the construction's precedent for independent-decision status.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Deut.24.8 הִשָּׁמֶר בְּנֶגַע הַצָּרַעַת לִשְׁמֹר מְאֹד וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּ אֶתְכֶם הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם

boundary_rationale: A fresh imperative-memory formula opens, 'Remember what Yahweh your God did to Miriam by the way as you came out of Egypt' -- oshb:Deut.24.9 זָכ֕וֹר אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְמִרְיָ֑ם בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם -- an opening that is near-verbatim the construction M8-Deut-155 treats as opening its own decision at 25:17 (זָכ֕וֹר אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ עֲמָלֵ֑ק בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם), both closing on the identical four-word phrase בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶם מִמִּצְרָיִם. That verbatim recital-opening parallel, not a register switch, is what carries the boundary: neither v.8 nor v.9 holds a single number throughout. v.8 opens with the singular imperative הִשָּׁמֶר (הִשָּׁ֧מֶר בְּנֶֽגַע) before turning plural at יוֹר֨וּ אֶתְכֶ֜ם ... תִּשְׁמְר֥וּ, and v.9 itself ends in the plural (בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם) after opening with the second-singular imperative זָכ֕וֹר and the 2ms suffix on אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ -- עָשָׂ֛ה itself is third-masculine-singular, with יְהוָ֥ה as its subject, not a second-singular form. No clean register switch exists at the 8|9 seam in either direction; the two verses share the same singular/plural mixture rather than being distinguished by it. Setumah after MT 24:9 closes the span, matching the marker pattern already used to bracket the corresponding Amalek command at 25:17.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The verse could still be read as v.8's grounding illustration rather than its own unit, but that reading is what created the inconsistency with M8-Deut-155's own citation of this verse as precedent for the construction's unit-opening force; splitting resolves it.

oshb:Deut.24.9 זָכ֕וֹר אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְמִרְיָ֑ם בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם (singular opening, plural close)

Every man shall be put to death for his own sin” (לֹא יוּמְתוּ אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים…אִישׁ בְּחֶטְאוֹ יוּמָתוּ), stands as its own general jurisprudential rule, distinct from the surrounding vulnerable-party protection cases on either side.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might attach this to the wage-law case preceding it as a related justice principle, but it addresses a wholly different legal question (transgenerational culpability, not labor practice), a real topic shift within the chapter’s case chain.

strongest_rejected_alternative: The trial procedure (v.1) and the stripe-limit ruling (vv.2-3) could be split into two decisions, but v.1’s “they shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked” is the premise the stripe-limit directly qualifies, one continuous judicial ordinance.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse prohibition, “You shall not muzzle the ox when he treads out the grain” (לֹא תַחְסֹם שׁוֹר בְּדִישׁוֹ), stands as its own brief case, unconnected in topic to either the corporal-punishment limit before it or the levirate-marriage law after it, one of this code’s many short interposed rules.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could attach this to the corporal-punishment law as a shared “measured treatment even of the guilty/laboring” principle, but the ox-muzzling law concerns animal treatment during labor, not judicial punishment, a distinct legal domain.

boundary_rationale: A fresh conditional opens the levirate-marriage law, “If brothers dwell together, and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger” (כִּי יֵשְׁבוּ אַחִים יַחְדָּו וּמֵת אַחַד מֵהֶם וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ לֹא תִהְיֶה אֵשֶׁת הַמֵּת הַחוּצָה), including the sandal-removal shaming ritual for refusal, closing on the “house of him who had his sandal removed” naming formula before the genital-seizure case opens v.11.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The base levirate obligation (vv.5-6) and the refusal-and-shaming procedure (vv.7-10) could be split into two decisions, but v.7’s “And if the man doesn’t want to take his brother’s wife” is the built-in contingency for the very obligation just stated, one continuous ordinance.

boundary_rationale: A fresh casuistic protasis opens, “When men strive against each other, and the wife of one draws near to deliver her husband…and grabs him by his private parts” (כִּי יִנָּצוּ אֲנָשִׁים יַחְדָּו…וְשָׁלְחָה יָדָהּ וְהֶחֱזִיקָה בִּמְבֻשָׁיו), closing on the hand-severing penalty before the honest-weights law opens v.13.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might connect this to the levirate law by shared vocabulary (both involve brothers/husbands), but the two cases share no legal logic — one regulates inheritance continuity, the other a specific bodily-harm penalty — and each opens its own fresh protasis.

strongest_rejected_alternative: The weights prohibition (v.13) and the measures prohibition (v.14) could be split into two decisions, but both share the identical “diverse, one large one small” structure and are bound together by the single positive formula of v.15 that answers both, one register.

boundary_rationale: A fresh imperative-memory formula closes ch.25 and the case-law chain, “Remember what Amalek did to you by the way as you came out of Egypt” (זָכוֹר אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְךָ עֲמָלֵק בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶם מִמִּצְרָיִם), commanding the blotting-out of Amalek’s memory once settled, closing before the firstfruits liturgy opens ch.26.

boundary_rationale: A fresh temporal formula opens the triennial-tithe instruction, 'When you have finished tithing all the tithe of your increase in the third year' -- oshb:Deut.26.12 כִּי תְכַלֶּה לַעְשֵׂר אֶת כָּל מַעְשַׂר תְּבוּאָתְךָ בַּשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁלִישִׁת, directing the tithe to the Levite, foreigner, orphan, and widow for local consumption, closing before the scripted declaration formula of v.13 opens fresh. Formerly grouped with the declaration through v.15; splitting off the procedural instruction from the performed speech that follows applies the same performance-formula criterion the campaign already used to separate M8-Deut-156 (firstfruits instructions) from M8-Deut-157 (firstfruits recitation).

boundary_rationale: The twelve-curse liturgy's shared ground is not primarily the offense named in each clause but the discrete performative response that closes it. This first curse, 'Cursed is the man who makes an engraved or molten image' -- oshb:Deut.27.15 אָר֣וּר הָאִ֡ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַעֲשֶׂה֩ פֶ֨סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֜ה תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה מַעֲשֵׂ֛ה יְדֵ֥י חָרָ֖שׁ וְשָׂ֣ם בַּסָּ֑תֶר וְעָנ֧וּ כָל הָעָ֛ם וְאָמְר֖וּ אָמֵֽן, is answered by the assembly's own plural variant of the series' refrain, וְעָנ֧וּ כָל הָעָ֛ם וְאָמְר֖וּ אָמֵֽן ('and all the people shall answer and say, Amen'); every one of the eleven curses that follow closes on the four-word singular form וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן. That per-curse ritual response -- present without exception after all twelve entries -- is what the agricultural-futility catalog at 28:38-42 conspicuously lacks: five items sharing a fronted object, four of the five (vv.38-41) closed by a כִּי-clause naming the cause of loss and the fifth (v.42) fronting its object with no כִּי-clause at all, and none of the five closed by a response formula of any kind. Offense-differentiation among the twelve (idolatry here, filial dishonor next, and so on through incest, murder, and bribery) remains real color, but standing alone it is in tension with the 28:38-42 merge, which differentiates its own five items by object and agent just as clearly and is still read as one catalog. The performative-response criterion is what actually distinguishes a performed liturgy of twelve discrete units from an unbroken descriptive list. parashah_two_witness.json corroborates unusually densely here: a samekh follows every one of MT 27:15 through 27:25, and a petuchah -- the strongest class recorded anywhere in this book -- closes MT 27:26, an unbroken run of independent Masoretic section punctuation matching every one of the twelve seams. That density lifts confidence from low to medium.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading all twelve curses as one 27:15-26 register, on the model applied to the six-fold blessing/curse domain lists of ch.28, is the recurring objection; it is more evidence-full than it first appears, since ch.28's domain lists genuinely do lack any per-item response formula. Twelve seams that each close on their own Amen are formally closer to twelve performed cases than to one repeated-template blessing list, and the two-witness file's near-total marker density for this specific series (absent from the ch.28 blessing/curse registers) corroborates treating it differently.

boundary_rationale: Secret murder reopens the social-order theme at curse ten, after the incest run: oshb:Deut.27.24 אָרוּר מַכֶּה רֵעֵהוּ בַּסָּתֶר, closed by its own Amen. boundary_rationale: Judicial bribery, the eleventh curse, closes on its own Amen: oshb:Deut.27.25 אָרוּר לֹקֵחַ שֹׁחַד לְהַכּוֹת נֶפֶשׁ דָּם נָקִי. strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this final curse as continuous with the eleven specific-offense curses that precede it (vv.15-25; v.15 shares the asher-frame with v.26 while vv.16-25 are participial) would erase the shift from a named act to a whole-law summary that the poem's own diction marks (אֲשֶׁר-clause matching the opening frame at v.15, not another participle); the petuchah at its close, unmatched in strength anywhere else in this series, corroborates treating it as the deliberate capstone.

boundary_rationale: A fresh escalation wave opens on “Yahweh will send on you cursing, confusion, and rebuke in all that you put your hand to do” (יְשַׁלַּח יְהוָה בְּךָ אֶת הַמְּאֵרָה אֶת הַמְּהוּמָה וְאֶת הַמִּגְעֶרֶת), moving through plague, drought, military defeat, and unburied corpses in one sustained verb-chain (יַדְבֵּק, יַכְּכָה, יִתֵּן, יִתֶּנְךָ), closing before a distinct bodily-affliction sub-wave opens fresh imagery in v.27.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might split this seven-verse wave at the shift from disease imagery (vv.21-22) to weather imagery (vv.23-24) to military defeat (v.25) to unburied dead (v.26), but no fresh introducing formula marks these as separate units; they read as one accumulating catalog of national disaster.

boundary_rationale: A shift into named bodily and mental affliction opens this span, 'Yahweh will strike you with the boils of Egypt' -- oshb:Deut.28.27 יַכְּכָה יְהוָה בִּשְׁחִין מִצְרַיִם, adding tumors, scurvy, madness, blindness, and confusion of heart, closing on the groping-at-noonday image before the property-and-family-loss wave opens v.30. The prior ground for this seam -- that יַכְּכָה יְהוָה marks a 'fresh sub-wave' at v.27 -- does not survive scrutiny: the identical verb opens MT 28:22 (inside the preceding decision's own span, treated there as one link in an undifferentiated chain) and recurs again at MT 28:28, still inside this very decision's own span, never itself treated as opening anything. The verb is retired as boundary evidence. What remains is a genuine content signal: vv.27-29 name a cluster of personal bodily and mental afflictions (boils, tumors, scurvy, itch, madness, blindness, confusion of mind) categorically distinct from the national-scale plague, drought, military defeat, and corpse-desecration imagery of vv.20-26. No Masoretic marker exists anywhere in this stretch (OSHB records nothing between MT 28:14 and 28:68), so, as with its neighbors on both sides, the seam rests on this content shift alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging back into M8-Deut-182 as one unbroken 28:20-29 catalog is a live alternative once the verb-recurrence claim is dropped, since no formula, marker, or addressee change exists at the 26/27 line either. The content shift from national disaster to personal affliction is kept as the deciding factor because the campaign treats comparable un-marked content turns as sufficient boundaries elsewhere in this same chapter (the foreigner-ascendancy image at v.43, the causal clause at v.47), so applying a different standard here for consistency's sake would itself be the inconsistency.

boundary_rationale: A fresh register opens on 'You will betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her' -- oshb:Deut.28.30 אִשָּׁ֣ה תְאָרֵ֗שׂ וְאִ֤ישׁ אַחֵר֙ ישגלנה/יִשְׁכָּבֶ֔נָּה (ketiv/qere as printed) בַּ֥יִת תִּבְנֶ֖ה וְלֹא תֵשֵׁ֣ב בּ֑וֹ כֶּ֥רֶם תִּטַּ֖ע וְלֹ֥א תְחַלְּלֶּֽנּוּ, fronting the object before the verb with no Yahweh subject at all, cataloging loss of house, vineyard, ox, donkey, sheep, and children to captivity through v.34's 'you will be maddened by the sight your eyes see' (וְהָיִ֖יתָ מְשֻׁגָּ֑ע מִמַּרְאֵ֥ה עֵינֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּרְאֶֽה). The span is now drawn at 28:30-34 rather than through v.35: v.35 restores both the divine subject and the striking-formula that vv.30-34 pointedly lack -- יַכְּכָ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה בִּשְׁחִ֣ין רָ֗ע -- and returns to the disease register of the preceding decision, echoing MT 28:27's שְׁחִין and its verbatim closing clause אֲשֶׁר לֹא תוּכַל לְהֵרָפֵא. The prior attachment of v.35 to this span rested only on adjacency (v.35 'cannot stand alone and cannot read forward'), which is not itself a text signal under mesh-r2's rule that markers corroborate but text drives; content decides here, and v.35's content is 183's disease cluster, not this span's deprivation-and-loss catalog. v.35 is accordingly re-cut as its own decision, M8-Deut-254. No Masoretic marker exists anywhere in this stretch (OSHB records nothing between MT 28:14 and 28:68), so, as with its neighbors, the seam at 34/35 rests on this content contrast alone. The seam at 29/30 rests on the same kind of content contrast in reverse -- affliction imagery giving way to deprivation imagery -- but that contrast is one of content, not of grammatical subject: v.29, the verse immediately before this seam, already has no divine subject of its own (וְהָיִ֜יתָ מְמַשֵּׁ֣שׁ בַּֽצָּהֳרַ֗יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יְמַשֵּׁ֤שׁ הָעִוֵּר֙ בָּאֲפֵלָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תַצְלִ֖יחַ אֶת דְּרָכֶ֑יךָ וְהָיִ֜יתָ אַ֣ךְ עָשׁ֧וּק וְגָז֛וּל כָּל הַיָּמִ֖ים וְאֵ֥ין מוֹשִֽׁיעַ), so the Yahweh-subject/no-subject framing that distinguishes 183's affliction wave from this deprivation wave holds wave against wave, not verse against verse at the 29/30 seam itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping v.35 folded into this span as a one-verse coda, per the prior treatment, is a live alternative and is what this campaign drew before re-examination: v.35 genuinely cannot stand as the opening of v.36's fresh יוֹלֵ֨ךְ ... מַלְכְּךָ֙ material, so attaching it somewhere is unavoidable. It is not kept here because the row's own strongest evidence for it -- the verbatim echo of 28:27's אֲשֶׁר לֹא תוּכַל לְהֵרָפֵא and the shared שְׁחִין vocabulary -- argues for grouping v.35 with the disease material it echoes, not with the property-and-family-loss catalog it is merely adjacent to; using 'it has nowhere else to go' as the ground for a merger is the same move mesh-r2 forbids when a marker is silent, applied instead to content, and the campaign should not reward it just because the alternative is a bare one-verse decision.

boundary_rationale: Verse 35 does not belong in the property-and-family-loss catalog it was previously read as closing, and it does not open the exile-to-unknown-nation material that follows either. It restores the divine subject and striking-formula that MT 28:30-34 conspicuously omit -- יַכְּכָ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה בִּשְׁחִ֣ין רָ֗ע עַל הַבִּרְכַּ֨יִם֙ וְעַל הַשֹּׁקַ֔יִם -- and the clause אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא תוּכַ֖ל לְהֵרָפֵ֑א, which stands mid-verse here (v.35 continues מִכַּ֥ף רַגְלְךָ֖ וְעַ֥ד קָדְקֳדֶֽךָ), repeats verbatim the clause that closes MT 28:27, with the same שְׁחִין vocabulary (בִּשְׁחִ֤ין מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ at 28:27, בִּשְׁחִ֣ין רָ֗ע here); no other verse in the יַכְּכָה יְהוָה series (28:22, 28:28) shares both the שחין term and the cannot-be-healed clause with this one. The content is a return to the personal disease register of the preceding decision (183, MT 28:27-29), not a continuation of the deprivation register of 28:30-34, so v.35 is treated as its own low-confidence unit rather than folded into either neighbor by adjacency. Forward attachment into v.36 is excluded on the same ground already established for 184: v.36 opens on the fresh verb יוֹלֵ֨ךְ ('he will lead you away') naming 'your king' (מַלְכְּךָ֙), a term occurring nowhere else in the chapter, a clean formal seam that has nothing to do with v.35's content. This decision does not revive the retired warrant of the old M8-Deut-185, which isolated v.35 on the claim that the recurrence of the verb יַכְּכָה יְהוָה itself marked a fresh sub-wave; that claim is false, since the same verb opens MT 28:22 and MT 28:28 without being treated as a boundary anywhere else, and 183 already retires it explicitly. The warrant here is content alone: the disease vocabulary and the verbatim echo of 28:27, not the recurring verb. No Masoretic marker exists anywhere in this stretch (parashah_two_witness records nothing between Deut.28.14 and Deut.28.68), so, like its neighbors on both sides, this one-verse decision rests on an unmarked content signal, priced at low confidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v.35 back into M8-Deut-184 as a one-verse coda to the property-and-family-loss catalog (28:30-35) was the prior treatment and remains the main alternative. It is not adopted because its only textual support was adjacency -- v.35 cannot stand as the opening of v.36's fresh material, so it was attached to whatever preceded it -- while the verse's own content (a Yahweh-subject striking-formula naming שחין and repeating 28:27's cannot-be-healed clause verbatim) points the other way, back to the disease cluster of 183. A merger justified only by 'nowhere else to put it' is the same kind of non-signal mesh-r2 excludes when the absent party is a Masoretic mark; content should not be held to a lower standard than markers are. Merging forward with 183 (MT 28:27-29) was also considered and rejected: 183's own span already closes cleanly at v.29, corroborated by nothing more than the same absence of markers this decision shares, and v.35 sits two verses past that close with an intervening deprivation catalog (30-34) between them, so extending 183 backward through the gap would itself be an adjacency-only move of the same kind rejected above. A standalone low-confidence decision is the reading that does not manufacture false support in either direction.

boundary_rationale: A fresh אֵלֶּה-colophon opens the Moab covenant address, 'These are the words of the covenant which Yahweh commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab' -- oshb:Deut.28.69 (=WEB Deut.29.1) אֵלֶּה֩ דִבְרֵ֨י הַבְּרִ֜ית אֲֽשֶׁר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֣ה אֶת מֹשֶׁ֗ה לִכְרֹ֛ת אֶת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֑ב מִלְּבַ֣ד הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁר כָּרַ֥ת אִתָּ֖ם בְּחֹרֵֽב. The forward-reading is supported by a genuine structural precedent inside the book, corrected here: 4:44-49's own אֵלֶּה heading (אֵ֚לֶּה הָֽעֵדֹ֔ת וְהַֽחֻקִּ֖ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם), followed by four verses of geographic and historical description (4:46-49), is not 'immediately' followed by the summons at 5:1 -- a petuchah closes 4:49 first (וְכָל הָ֨עֲרָבָ֜ה עֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה וְעַ֖ד יָ֣ם הָעֲרָבָ֑ה תַּ֖חַת אַשְׁדֹּ֥ת הַפִּסְגָּֽה), and only then does 5:1 open with וַיִּקְרָ֣א מֹשֶׁה֮ אֶל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם. That correction makes the precedent stronger rather than weaker: in both places a petuchah stands between the אֵלֶּה heading block and the summons that follows it (petuchah after 4:49 at Horeb; petuchah after 28:69 here at Moab), so the petuchah after MT 28:69 stops being a counter-signal against forward reading and becomes part of the very pattern that supports it. Disclosed candidly: a setumah still precedes this verse (after MT 28:68), a real, if now lesser, counter-signal for reading 28:69 backward as ch.28's colophon rather than forward as ch.29's heading. That asymmetry -- petuchah after matching petuchah on the forward reading, against one setumah on the backward reading -- bears on confidence rather than on the boundary itself, since the decision already brackets this verse as its own singleton rather than annexing it to either neighbor; given the strength of the corrected 4:44-49/5:1 precedent, confidence is raised from low to medium. This verse is MT's own 28:69, the third WEB/MT chapter-line offset in this book, requiring dual citation across the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reader following MT's chapter division would read this verse as the closing colophon of the ch.28 curse material rather than the opening of ch.29's address; the setumah before this verse is a real counter-signal for that direction, and is disclosed here as such. It does not carry the day because the corrected 4:44-49/5:1 precedent -- heading block, petuchah, then summons -- is the stronger book-internal pattern for reading אֵלֶּה forward across a petuchah, which is why the verse is still bracketed on the forward side rather than reassigned.

boundary_rationale: Ch.30 opens on a fresh conditional, 'It shall happen, when all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse... and you shall call them to mind' -- oshb:Deut.30.1 וְהָיָה֩ כִֽי יָבֹ֨אוּ עָלֶ֜יךָ כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה הַבְּרָכָה֙ וְהַקְּלָלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ֙ אֶל לְבָבֶ֔ךָ בְּכָל הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִדִּיחֲךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ שָֽׁמָּה, promising restoration, curse-transfer to Israel's enemies, and circumcision of the heart, in one unbroken waw-consecutive-perfect chain (וְשָׁ֨ב v.3, וֶהֱבִֽיאֲךָ֞ v.5, וּמָ֨ל v.6, וְנָתַן֙ v.7, וְהוֹתִֽירְךָ֩ v.9) bound together by a return-and-obey refrain recurring at vv.2, 8, and 10, closing before the Torah-accessibility passage opens its own fresh declarative at v.11. This decision now absorbs the material previously split off as its own decision at v.7: nothing marks 30:7 as a fresh unit rather than the fourth of five identical chain links, and the transfer of curses to Israel's enemies is simply the next promise in the same sequence, not a new topic. Samekh closes the preceding unit at Deut.29.28 (MT) = web:Deut.29.29 -- this citation sits inside the non-identical web Deut.29.1-29.29 = mt Deut.28.69-29.28 segment and requires the dual label -- and petuchah, the strongest marker class, closes this one at Deut.30.10 (identical numbering in both traditions), with no site anywhere between; syntax and Masoretic tradition converge exactly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v.7 on the reasoning that the curse-transfer clause is a distinct turn in the promise's logic was the prior reading; every other link in the same five-part chain would support an equally plausible split on the same logic (each verse introduces its own specific blessing), which is precisely why treating v.7 alone as a boundary while leaving vv.3, 5, 6, and 9 unsplit cannot be sustained -- the whole chain stands or falls together, and it stands as one unit closed by the petuchah at v.10.

boundary_rationale: A fresh declarative opens the accessibility passage, “For this commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant” (כִּי הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לֹא נִפְלֵאת הִוא מִמְּךָ וְלֹא רְחֹקָה הִיא), denying that Torah requires heavenly or transoceanic retrieval, closing on “the word is very near you” before the climactic choose-life charge opens v.15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might fold this into the closing choose-life charge as its rhetorical preparation, but it makes a distinct, self-contained argument (accessibility, not choice) with its own closing formula (“that you may do it”) before the choose-life charge opens on a fresh imperative of its own.

boundary_rationale: Ch.31 opens the succession narrative on its own notice, “Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel. He said to them, I am one hundred twenty years old today” (וַיֵּלֶךְ מֹשֶׁה וַיְדַבֵּר אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֶל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל…בֶּן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם), announcing his incapacity and Yahweh’s and Joshua’s roles, closing on “be strong and courageous” before the direct charge to Joshua opens v.7.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One farewell scene running from this address straight into the direct Joshua charge that follows has surface appeal; v.7’s “Moses called to Joshua” instead shifts the addressee from all Israel to Joshua specifically, a real change of recipient the text itself marks.

strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could fold this into the farewell address as its natural continuation, but the shift to direct second-person address to Joshua specifically (“in the sight of all Israel” as witnesses, not addressees) marks a formally distinct commissioning act.

boundary_rationale: A fresh narrative act opens, 'Moses wrote this law and delivered it to the priests the sons of Levi... Moses commanded them, saying, At the end of every seven years' -- oshb:Deut.31.9 וַיִּכְתֹּב מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת וַיִּתְּנָהּ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים, instituting the septennial Sukkot public reading, closing before the Tent of Meeting summons opens v.14. boundary_rationale: A fresh divine summons opens, “Yahweh said to Moses, Behold, your days approach that you must die. Call Joshua” (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הֵן קָרְבוּ יָמֶיךָ לָמוּת קְרָא אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ), narrating the pillar-of-cloud theophany at the Tent’s door, closing before Yahweh’s own apostasy-prediction speech opens v.16.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A single Tent-of-Meeting scene spanning this summons and the apostasy-prediction speech that follows has some pull; this span is instead the narrated summons-and-appearance (third-person action), while v.16 shifts into Yahweh’s own quoted first-person speech, a real formal seam.

This people will rise up and play the prostitute” (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הִנְּךָ שֹׁכֵב עִם אֲבֹתֶיךָ וְקָם הָעָם הַזֶּה וְזָנָה), predicting future covenant-breaking and Yahweh’s hidden face, closing before the Song-command opens fresh in v.19.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might read this as continuous with the Song command that follows since both concern the coming apostasy, but v.19’s “Now therefore write this song for yourselves” opens a fresh imperative addressed to Moses with a distinct topic (a literary remedy), not a continuation of the prediction itself.

boundary_rationale: A fresh fulfillment notice opens, 'So Moses wrote this song the same day, and taught it to the children of Israel' -- oshb:Deut.31.22 וַיִּכְתֹּב מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וַיְלַמְּדָהּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, reporting compliance with the command given in vv.19-21, and containing the sole 'that day' temporal marker in this pair of verses. Formerly grouped with v.23 as one merged narrator-report unit; the merge's own stated grounds (a shared 'same day' frame and uniform third-person report) do not hold once checked against the Hebrew -- v.23 carries no temporal phrase and opens its own introducing formula rather than continuing v.22's.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping vv.22-23 together as one compact closing beat, on the reasoning that both fall within the same narrative moment, was the prior reading; it required treating v.23 as uniform third-person report about Moses, but v.23's own first-person oath language ('I will be with you... which I swore to them') is not narration about Moses at all, which is the deeper problem the temporal-frame and introducing-formula errors were both symptoms of.

oshb:Deut.31.23 וַיְצַו אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן וַיֹּאמֶר חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ (fresh formula, no temporal phrase; now a separate decision)

boundary_rationale: A fresh command-plus-speech formula opens, 'He commissioned Joshua the son of Nun, and said, Be strong and courageous' -- oshb:Deut.31.23 וַיְצַ֞ו אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן נ֗וּן וַיֹּאמֶר֮ חֲזַ֣ק וֶֽאֱמָץ֒ כִּ֣י אַתָּ֗ה תָּבִיא֙ אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתִּי לָהֶ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֖י אֶֽהְיֶ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ. A sweep of every וַיְצַו in Deuteronomy -- 27:1 (וַיְצַ֤ו מֹשֶׁה֙ וְזִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁמֹר֙ אֶת כָּל הַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם), 27:11 (וַיְצַ֤ו מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹֽר), 31:10 (וַיְצַ֥ו מֹשֶׁ֖ה אוֹתָ֣ם לֵאמֹ֑ר מִקֵּ֣ץ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֗ים בְּמֹעֵ֛ד שְׁנַ֥ת הַשְּׁמִטָּ֖ה בְּחַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת), and 31:25 (וַיְצַ֤ו מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת הַלְוִיִּ֔ם נֹ֥שְׂאֵ֛י אֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר) -- shows every one of them continuing with לֵאמֹר; 31:23's וַיְצַו...וַיֹּאמֶר pairing is the only one in the book that does not. That formula is unique, not shared with 31:7's structurally different וַיִּקְרָ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה לִֽיהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו (a call-plus-speech, not a command-plus-speech), and its uniqueness strengthens rather than weakens the case for a fresh address here: a formula found nowhere else in the book marks this moment as distinct from the book's own command-giving pattern, not merely as a repetition of it. The genuine link to 31:7 is not the introducing verb but the commissioning speech itself -- both address Joshua directly with חֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָץ֒ כִּ֣י אַתָּ֗ה ... The speaker is best read as Yahweh rather than Moses: אֶהְיֶ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ ('I will be with you') and אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתִּי לָהֶ֑ם echo v.21's אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבָּֽעְתִּי almost verbatim, first-person oath language this book gives to Yahweh, never to Moses speaking of himself. No temporal phrase ties this verse to v.22's 'that day'; the two verses share adjacency but not grammar.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v.23 as Moses's own continued narrated action (grouped with v.22 under a single narrator-report label) was the prior treatment; it cannot be sustained once the verse's first-person oath content is taken seriously, since the book nowhere else puts such language in Moses's own mouth.

boundary_rationale: A fresh temporal clause opens, 'When Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book, until they were finished, Moses commanded the Levites... to put it by the side of the ark' -- oshb:Deut.31.24 וַיְהִי כְּכַלּוֹת מֹשֶׁה לִכְתֹּב אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת עַל סֵפֶר, opening a single quoted command (לֵאמֹר, v.25) that runs unbroken through the ark-deposit instruction, the rebellion-foreseen rationale, the elders' assembly summons, and the corruption prediction, closing only where the narrator resumes naming Moses at v.30. The span is extended from its prior close at v.27 to v.29, since nothing inside vv.28-29 reintroduces the quotation or changes speaker -- the whole stretch stays inside the לֵאמֹר opened at v.25. Petuchah after MT 31.30 confirms the true close, with no Masoretic site anywhere between v.15 and v.30 to suggest an earlier one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing the span at v.27, on the reasoning that the ark-deposit instruction and its witness-against-you rationale form a complete unit, leaves vv.28-29 (the elders' summons and corruption prediction) stranded as an orphan opening for the following decision even though they carry no reintroducing formula of their own -- the quotation frame itself settles where the real seam falls, at v.29/30.

boundary_rationale: A fresh narrative report closes ch.31 and hinges into the Song, 'Moses spoke in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, until they were finished' -- oshb:Deut.31.30 וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה בְּאָזְנֵי כָּל קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת עַד תֻּמָּם, third-person narration naming Moses again after the whole quoted command of vv.25-29 closes. This decision no longer includes vv.28-29 (the elders' summons and corruption prediction), which sit inside that same quotation and now belong to M8-Deut-211. Petuchah after MT 31.30 confirms the close and matches the strongest available marker between v.15 and v.30.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Retaining vv.28-30 together as this decision's own span, on the reasoning that the elders' summons functions as a hinge toward the Song, was the prior reading; v.28 carries no reintroducing formula of its own and stays inside the quotation opened at v.25, so it belongs with the command it is part of, not with the narrator's resumption at v.30.

boundary_rationale: The Song of Moses opens on its own cosmic-witness invocation, “Give ear, you heavens, and I will speak. Let the earth hear the words of my mouth” (הַאֲזִינוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וַאֲדַבֵּרָה וְתִשְׁמַע הָאָרֶץ אִמְרֵי פִי), closing on the “ascribe greatness to our God” doxology before the Rock’s-justice indictment opens v.4; no |b stanza-break marker intervenes before v.4, but the shift from invocation to accusation is a real content turn.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might keep the whole invocation-through-indictment span (vv.1-6) as one opening movement, but the shift from addressing heaven-and-earth as witnesses (vv.1-3) to addressing Israel directly with an accusation (vv.4-6) is a real change of addressee within the poem’s own rhetoric.

boundary_rationale: A fresh indictment opens on “The Rock: his work is perfect, for all his ways are just” (הַצּוּר תָּמִים פָּעֳלוֹ כִּי כָל דְּרָכָיו מִשְׁפָּט), turning immediately to accusation, “They have dealt corruptly with him. They are not his children” (v.5), closing on the rhetorical “Is this how you repay Yahweh” question before the historical recital opens v.7.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A single sustained argument for Yahweh’s faithfulness running from this indictment into the historical recital that follows is tempting; v.7’s “Remember the days of old” instead opens a fresh imperative shifting from present accusation to a backward-looking historical appeal, a real rhetorical turn.

boundary_rationale: A fresh imperative opens the historical recital, “Remember the days of old. Consider the years of many generations” (זְכֹר יְמוֹת עוֹלָם בִּינוּ שְׁנוֹת דּוֹר וָדוֹר), covering the nations’ apportionment, the eagle-and-nest care image, and the abundant-produce catalog, closing on the wine-from-grapes image before the apostasy turn opens v.15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the election narrative (vv.7-12) from the abundance catalog (vv.13-14) is possible, but v.13’s “He made him ride on the high places” is the direct continuation of Yahweh’s care just narrated, one sustained historical movement.

boundary_rationale: A fresh adversative turn opens, “But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked. You have grown fat…Then he abandoned God who made him” (וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט…וַיִּטֹּשׁ אֱלוֹהַ עָשָׂהוּ), naming the strange-gods apostasy, closing on “you have forgotten God who gave you birth” before Yahweh’s wrathful response opens v.19.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could keep this bound to the preceding abundance catalog as cause-and-effect (prosperity leading to apostasy), but its own fresh adversative opening (“But Jeshurun grew fat”) marks the poem’s own deliberate rhetorical pivot from blessing to betrayal.

boundary_rationale: The opening is genuine but was misdescribed: v.19's וַיַּ֥רְא יְהוָ֖ה וַיִּנְאָ֑ץ ('Yahweh saw and abhorred') does not make Yahweh the grammatical subject for the first time since the poem opened -- Yahweh is already the explicit subject at v.12 (יְהוָ֖ה בָּדָ֣ד יַנְחֶ֑נּוּ וְאֵ֥ין עִמּ֖וֹ אֵ֥ל נֵכָֽר) and the implicit third-masculine-singular subject of the wilderness-care sequence around it (יִמְצָאֵ֨הוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִדְבָּ֔ר וּבְתֹ֖הוּ יְלֵ֣ל יְשִׁמֹ֑ן יְסֹֽבְבֶ֨נְהוּ֙ יְב֣וֹנְנֵ֔הוּ יִצְּרֶ֖נְהוּ כְּאִישׁ֥וֹן עֵינֽוֹ). What is genuinely distinctive at v.19 is that it resumes wayyiqtol narration with Yahweh as subject immediately after the second-person accusation that closes the historical recital -- צ֥וּר יְלָדְךָ֖ תֶּ֑שִׁי וַתִּשְׁכַּ֖ח אֵ֥ל מְחֹלְלֶֽךָ at v.18 -- and that resumption introduces the quoted divine speech. The closing edge is corrected: the quoted speech opened by וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַסְתִּ֤ירָה at v.20 runs in unbroken first-singular forms (אַסְפֶּ֥ה, אֲשַׁלַּח, אָמַ֖רְתִּי) through v.27's וְלֹ֥א יְהוָ֖ה פָּעַ֥ל כָּל זֹֽאת, so the WEB stanza mark after v.22 previously used to close this span sits inside a single continuous quotation rather than at its edge, and cannot be the boundary's evidence under the rule that translation typesetting is metadata only. This span now absorbs the material previously split off as M8-Deut-218: nothing distinguishes v.23's אַסְפֶּ֥ה עָלֵ֨ימוֹ֙ רָע֔וֹת as a fresh strophe-opener from the vengeance material immediately before it -- same first person, no new subject, no vocative, no particle. The real formal seam is one strophe later, at 27/28, where v.28's כִּי ג֛וֹי אֹבַ֥ד עֵצ֖וֹת הֵ֑מָּה וְאֵ֥ין בָּהֶ֖ם תְּבוּנָֽה drops out of Yahweh's first-person voice into third-person reflection on the enemies -- exactly where the following decision (M8-Deut-219) already opens. Disclosed for the whole Song: MT carries no pe or samekh anywhere inside 32:1-43 (parashah_two_witness.json's nearest sites are petuchah after Deut.31.30 before and petuchah after Deut.32.43 after), so every internal seam in this poem, including this one, rests on text signal alone -- discourse frame and speaker change, not layout.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the prior two-decision split at 22/23, with the WEB \b mark as its stated evidence, cannot stand once that mark is treated as metadata rather than a driver: the Hebrew shows one uninterrupted first-person divine speech from v.20 to v.27, and merging is the only reading consistent with the mesh-r2 rule that translation stanza breaks never drive a boundary on their own.

boundary_rationale: The poem's own theophany exordium opens on 'Yahweh came from Sinai, and rose from Seir to them. He shone from Mount Paran' -- oshb:Deut.33.2 וַיֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֞ה מִסִּינַ֥י בָּא֙ וְזָרַ֤ח מִשֵּׂעִיר֙ לָ֔מוֹ הוֹפִ֨יעַ֙ מֵהַ֣ר פָּארָ֔ן וְאָתָ֖ה מֵרִבְבֹ֣ת קֹ֑דֶשׁ מִֽימִינ֕וֹ אשדת אֵ֥שׁ דָּ֖ת לָֽמוֹ, closing on 'when the heads of the people were gathered, all the tribes of Israel together' (v.5) -- a fitting close to the introit before the tribal sayings begin. The prior rationale claimed the per-tribe 'About X he said' formula itself opens at v.6; checked directly, v.6 (Reuben's saying) carries no introducing formula at all -- יְחִ֥י רְאוּבֵ֖ן וְאַל יָמֹ֑ת וִיהִ֥י מְתָ֖יו מִסְפָּֽר opens with a bare jussive, third-person about Reuben rather than to him. The formula device does not actually begin until v.7's וְזֹ֣את לִֽיהוּדָה֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒. The seam at 5/6 is retained on a narrower ground than before: the collective assembly notice of v.5 gives way to individually named reference starting at v.6, and v.6 is also the poem's first jussive, a shift in verbal mood as well as reference. This is priced honestly as a thin signal. The seam carries no Masoretic mark of any kind: the first section mark anywhere in ch.33 falls only after 33:6, so MT groups 33:1-6 as a single paragraph against the cut this decision draws, and the per-tribe formula that defines the series being opened is, by this decision's own finding, absent from v.6 -- the very verse the cut assigns to that series. What remains is one positive signal (collective-to-individual reference, reinforced by the mood shift to a jussive) working against an MT grouping and a formula gap at the seam's near edge, a weaker configuration than the campaign has priced above low elsewhere in this book: M8-Deut-244 sets low where a real formula is crossed by a single internal samekh, and M8-Deut-037 holds low where a real waw-chain is crossed by several internal samekh sites. A thinner signal, crossed by an actual MT grouping rather than by internal marks alone, does not price higher than either, so confidence is lowered from medium to low.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this exordium through the Reuben saying (v.6) as one continuous opening movement is a live alternative once the false formula-claim is dropped, since v.6 genuinely lacks the device that marks every later saying; the collective-to-individual reference shift at v.5/6 -- the assembly named as one body in v.5 versus a single tribe named for the first time in v.6, spoken about rather than addressed -- is kept as the operative signal instead, consistent with the twelve tribal-saying decisions that follow it.

boundary_rationale: The tribal-sayings sequence opens on Reuben, 'Let Reuben live, and not die; nor let his men be few' -- oshb:Deut.33.6 יְחִי רְאוּבֵן וְאַל יָמֹת וִיהִי מְתָיו מִסְפָּר, the first of the individually addressed sayings, with (from v.7 onward) an explicit 'About X he said' introducing formula the poem repeats. Correcting a count carried in the prior rationale: this is not 'the first of twelve sayings.' Working through ch.33, the poem gives ten sayings for twelve tribes -- Zebulun and Issachar share one saying (vv.18-19), Joseph's saying (vv.13-17) covers both Ephraim and Manasseh without a saying of their own, and Simeon receives no saying at all. The boundary is unaffected; the count in the descriptive prose is fixed.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all the tribal sayings as one undivided poetic register, as a repeated-template list might be merged elsewhere in this book, is not supported here: each saying (or paired saying) addresses genuinely different content -- life-and-numbers for Reuben, priestly office for Levi, agricultural abundance for Joseph -- matching this campaign's real-content-variance standard for splitting a register, regardless of the corrected count of how many such sayings there are.

He said, Hear, Yahweh, the voice of Judah” (וְזֹאת לִיהוּדָה וַיֹּאמַר שְׁמַע יְהוָה קוֹל יְהוּדָה), a brief petition for Judah’s military success distinct in content from Reuben’s numeric-survival blessing before it and Levi’s priestly saying after it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might merge this short saying with Reuben’s as one twin-blessing opening pair, but each carries its own explicit “about/for X he said” formula and addresses a wholly different tribe with a wholly different concern (battle aid, not survival), a real per-tribe seam.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the priestly-office description (vv.8-10) from the closing blessing petition (v.11) into two decisions is an option, but both remain governed by the single “About Levi he said” formula with no fresh introducing clause between them, one continuous saying.

boundary_rationale: A fresh introducing formula opens, “About Benjamin he said, The beloved of Yahweh will dwell in safety by him” (לְבִנְיָמִן אָמַר יְדִיד יְהֹוָה יִשְׁכֹּן לָבֶטַח עָלָיו), a brief image of divine shelter (“covers him all day long…dwells between his shoulders”) distinct from Levi’s priestly saying before it and Joseph’s abundance saying after it.

strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer could group this with the Dan saying as a pair of brief northern-tribe blessings, but each opens its own “About X he said” formula and each names a distinct territorial or characterological blessing, the poem’s consistent per-tribe unit.

boundary_rationale: The per-tribe formula runs its final instance here, 'About Asher he said, Asher is blessed with children. Let him be acceptable to his brothers' -- oshb:Deut.33.24 וּלְאָשֵׁר אָמַר בָּרוּךְ מִבָּנִים אָשֵׁר יְהִי רְצוּי אֶחָיו, promising iron-and-bronze bars and strength matching his days, closing before v.26's אֵין כָּאֵל יְשֻׁרוּן drops the וּלְ...אָמַר pattern entirely and turns to a universal address, closing the tribal-sayings sequence. Correcting a count carried in the prior rationale: this is not 'the twelfth and final individually named tribal saying.' As already corrected at M8-Deut-227, the poem gives ten sayings for twelve tribes -- Zebulun/Issachar share one, Joseph covers Ephraim and Manasseh without their own, and Simeon has none -- so Asher's saying is well short of a twelfth in sequence, not the poem's twelfth entry. The boundary itself is unaffected.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the Asher saying through v.26 as part of one continuous close is excluded on formal grounds regardless of the count correction: v.26 abandons the וּלְ-name-אָמַר pattern entirely for a universal second-person address to all Israel, a real formal seam closing the tribal-sayings sequence, independent of how many sayings preceded it.

strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might read this doxology as simply the final tribal saying (implicitly for Israel-as-a-whole) continuing the per-tribe pattern, but it lacks the “About X he said” formula entirely, marking a deliberate formal shift from individual tribal address to a closing peroration for the whole assembly.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the panoramic viewing (vv.1-3) from Yahweh’s closing word (v.4) into two decisions is an option, but v.4’s “Yahweh said to him, This is the land which I swore” is grammatically the direct commentary on the very panorama just described, one continuous scene.

boundary_rationale: A fresh narrative report opens, “So Moses the servant of Yahweh died there in the land of Moab, according to Yahweh’s word” (וַיָּמָת שָׁם מֹשֶׁה עֶבֶד יְהוָה בְּאֶרֶץ מוֹאָב עַל פִּי יְהוָה), reporting the unknown burial place, Moses’s undiminished vigor at death, and the thirty-day mourning, closing before Joshua’s commissioning-fulfilled notice opens v.9.

boundary_rationale: The book’s final colophon opens on “Since then, there has not arisen a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom Yahweh knew face to face” (וְלֹא קָם נָבִיא עוֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמֹשֶׁה אֲשֶׁר יְדָעוֹ יְהוָה פָּנִים אֶל פָּנִים), recapitulating the signs-and-wonders theme from 4:34 and 26:8 one last time, closing the whole book on “in the sight of all Israel,” a retrospective evaluative note that could only be written after Moses’s death just narrated.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A reviewer might fold this into the preceding Joshua notice as one continuous closing unit, but its own fresh, explicitly retrospective formula (“Since then, there has not arisen”) marks a vantage point after the fact, evaluating Moses’s whole career rather than continuing the narrated installation of Joshua.

literature_type_guess: divine commission speech (land-grant charge with law-observance appendix)
boundary_rationale: The book opens with a death-notice for Moses that pivots straight into a messenger formula, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ ... לֵאמֹֽר, and the quoted divine speech runs unbroken through v.9 with no re-introduction of speaker or addressee. The internal turn at v.6 ('be strong and courageous... you shall cause this people to inherit') is a topic shift within the same speech, not a new formula, so it stays inside the unit. The unit's far edge is confirmed by a petuchah after v.9 in both witnesses.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v.5/v.6 on the WEB paragraph break (Yahweh's land-oath vs. the courage charge) was considered, since the content genuinely pivots there, but there is no new אמר-formula or addressee change at v.6 - only WEB's editorial paragraphing, which is metadata, not a text signal.

literature_type_guess: officers' mobilization and procession instructions (ark-following protocol)
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ הַשֹּׁטְרִ֖ים בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה opens with the three-day interval as the officers' own temporal frame, and the same officers are the unbroken subject of the command next, וַיְצַוּוּ֮ אֶת הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ כִּרְאֽוֹתְכֶ֗ם אֵ֣ת אֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית יְהוָה֙ - one wayyiqtol chain, no subject reset from v.2b into v.3, transmitting the ark-following protocol. The far edge is driven by the speaker change at v.5, where Joshua takes over from the officers, וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל הָעָ֖ם; the samekh after v.4 corroborates that seam but does not itself close it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping v.2 with the arrival notice (v.1) was this draft's original position; corrected because the wayyiqtol chain into v.3 has no subject reset, a stronger signal than the notice's own bracket. Merging with Joshua's sanctification command (v.5) as one 'preparation speech' was considered, but the speaker changes from officers to Joshua at v.5, which this campaign treats as a real boundary even across adjacent verses - that speaker change, not the samekh, is what closes this unit.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.3.2 וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ הַשֹּׁטְרִ֖ים בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה
oshb:Josh.3.3 וַיְצַוּוּ֮ אֶת הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ כִּרְאֽוֹתְכֶ֗ם אֵ֣ת אֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית יְהוָה֙

boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל הָעָ֖ם הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ is a full messenger formula marking a change of speaker, not a change of addressee: the officers who commanded הָעָם in 3:3 (וַיְצַוּוּ֮ אֶת הָעָ֣ם) give way to Joshua speaking in his own voice at 3:5, while the addressee, הָעָם, stays constant across the 3:4|5 seam. That speaker-change-plus-fresh-formula is the near-edge driver. The far edge is where the addressee genuinely does change: 3:6 turns from הָעָם to הַכֹּהֲנִים, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֔ר.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Describing the evidence as 'thin, marker-only' and capping confidence at medium_low was this draft's original position; it misclassified the evidence. A later revision misdescribed the near edge as an addressee change from officers to people, but 3:3's officers already address הָעָם, so the addressee does not shift there - the real near-edge signal is the speaker change from officers to Joshua. Absorbing this verse into the following priestly command (v.6) as a single 'Joshua's instructions' block remains a live alternative, since both are Joshua speaking on the same day, but the different addressees (people vs. priests) keep 3:5 and 3:6 apart on the same driving-signal basis this draft uses throughout ch.3.

literature_type_guess: command to the priests to bear the ark (command-plus-fulfillment)
boundary_rationale: A new addressee (הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים) and an immediate fulfillment clause within the same verse (וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת אֲר֣וֹן הַבְּרִ֔ית) make this a compact command-and-execution unit, distinct from the exhortation to the people in v.5 and from Yahweh's word to Joshua that follows in v.7. A samekh after v.6, previously uncited by the draft, corroborates this far edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Combining this verse with vv.7-8 (Yahweh's subsequent word to Joshua) as one 'ark preparation' sequence was considered; it loses because v.7 opens with its own fresh וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ formula and a new speaker (Yahweh rather than Joshua).

literature_type_guess: divine word to Joshua (exaltation promise plus priestly instruction)
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ is a full messenger-formula reset with Yahweh as speaker and Joshua as sole addressee, distinct in both direction and content from the priestly command of v.6. A petuchah follows v.8.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading vv.6-8 together as one seamless 'ark-crossing preparation' sequence was considered given the shared topic, but the formula reset and speaker change are the same signal already used throughout this chapter to separate short adjacent speeches, so consistency favors the split.

parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.3.8 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: summons formula: call to attention before Joshua's proclamation
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גֹּ֣שׁוּ הֵ֔נָּה וְשִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶֽם opens a fresh messenger formula with the addressee shifted to the whole nation (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), distinct from vv.7-8's Joshua-alone address to the priests. Its content is a bare summons to attention rather than the promise itself; the actual content commences at 3:10 with its own explicit-subject reset, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ, naming Joshua again rather than continuing null-subject. That renewed named subject is the same class of signal this cluster already treats as boundary-forming at 3:5, 3:6 and 3:7 (short units opened by a repeated, explicitly named אמר-formula), so consistency favors reading 3:9 as its own brief unit rather than folding it into 3:10-13's proclamation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 3:9-13 as one unbroken proclamation, on the ground that both verses share the same speaker and addressee and the summons naturally introduces what follows, was this draft's original position. It is abandoned because the original rationale claimed no new אמר-formula interrupts the span, and 3:10's וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ contradicts that claim directly - it is a full, explicit-subject reset, not a null-subject continuation like 4:21's (see M8-Josh-022), so the campaign's own explicit-subject-reset principle argues for the split rather than against it.

literature_type_guess: Joshua's proclamation of the sign of the living God
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בְּזֹאת֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּן renews the formula with Joshua explicitly named again (not a null-subject continuation of 3:9), opening the substantive proclamation - nations to be dispossessed, the twelve-tribesmen instruction, the Jordan-cut-off prediction - running unbroken to v.13's close with no further אמר-formula inside it. v.12 has no speech-formula of its own and stays inside this proclamation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v.12 from vv.10-11/13 was considered, but v.12 has no new אמר-formula, so it stays with its speech. Attaching v.10 back to v.9 as one unbroken unit was the superseded draft's position; rejected because v.10 carries its own explicit-subject reset, the signal class this cluster treats as boundary-forming throughout ch.3.

literature_type_guess: fulfillment narrative: the crossing on dry ground
boundary_rationale: The discourse mode itself shifts from direct speech to third-person narration of the predicted sign actually occurring - the priests' feet touching the water, the heap standing at Adam, the nation crossing - a genre change from proclamation to event-report. The far edge is corroborated by a Wiederaufnahme at 4:1, but the degree of the repetition should be stated rather than assumed: 3:17 closes עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר תַּ֨מּוּ֙ כָּל הַגּ֔וֹי לַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּֽן against 4:1's וַיְהִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּ֣מּוּ כָל הַגּ֔וֹי לַעֲב֖וֹר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן - close but not identical (עַד אֲשֶׁר against כַּאֲשֶׁר; defective לַעֲבֹר against plene לַעֲבוֹר). A resumptive repetition of this kind is evidence the narrative continues across the seam as much as it is evidence of a boundary, so it is not treated as decisive on its own.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Citing high confidence on the strength of the Wiederaufnahme alone, with an accent on אֲשֶׁר that MT does not carry, was this draft's original position. It is corrected because a device used elsewhere in this campaign's own cross-chapter rule to argue continuity cannot simultaneously be cited as proof of a hard break; medium is the price the corrected evidence supports.

literature_type_guess: divine command for the twelve memorial stones
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּ֣מּוּ כָל הַגּ֔וֹי לַעֲב֖וֹר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן resumes 3:17's closing wording almost verbatim (Wiederaufnahme), a bridging device that signals continuity of the crossing event while the following וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹֽר opens a genuinely new divine speech-act - the twelve-stone command - so the resumption closes off the previous scene rather than merging with it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 4:1 as still part of the crossing narrative proper (attaching it to 3:14-17) was considered because of the verbal echo, but the presence of a fresh messenger formula immediately after the resumptive clause marks a new command, matching how this chapter treats every other Yahweh-to-Joshua formula as unit-opening.

literature_type_guess: Joshua's charge to the twelve regarding the future sign
boundary_rationale: וַיִּקְרָ֣א יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ אֶל שְׁנֵ֤ים הֶֽעָשָׂר֙ אִ֔ישׁ shifts speaker from Yahweh to Joshua and addressee to the twelve chosen men specifically, with content that anticipates future children's questions - didactic material distinct from the bare instruction of vv.1-3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with vv.1-3 as a single relay of the same command was considered, but Joshua's speech adds the child-catechesis frame ('what do you mean by these stones') absent from Yahweh's original instruction, making it a distinguishable speech-act worth its own unit.

literature_type_guess: execution notice: stones carried to camp
boundary_rationale: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵ֣ן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֒ is mainline wayyiqtol fulfillment of vv.1-7, no closure of its own; the compliance-report half of the pair, closed off by v.9's shift to a new subject and a new, uncommanded action.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping vv.8-9 as one register, resting on v.9's lack of a speech-formula, was original; abandoned because the operative test is register-closure: v.9 (וּשְׁתֵּ֧ים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֲבָנִ֗ים הֵקִ֣ים) carries its own עַד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה, the class credited at 5:9/6:25, while v.8 has none.

literature_type_guess: etiological notice: a second set of twelve stones erected within the riverbed
boundary_rationale: וּשְׁתֵּ֧ים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֲבָנִ֗ים הֵקִ֣ים יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ is a disjunctive fronted-object qatal reporting a distinct, uncommanded action, closed by its own עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה - the class decisive at 5:9/6:25.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v.9 into v.8, resting on the absence of a speech-formula, was superseded; once the closure is credited, splitting is better-supported, though this remains an unexplained doublet with vv.1-7, capping confidence.

literature_type_guess: notice of completion: priests remain until the word is finished, then the ark and people finish crossing
boundary_rationale: The near edge is v.10's disjunctive participial clause, וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֞ים נֹשְׂאֵ֣י הָאָר֗וֹן עֹמְדִים֮ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן֒, opening this pair's own completion report through v.10's עַ֣ד תֹּ֣ם כָּֽל הַ֠דָּבָר into v.11a's וַיְהִ֛י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר תַּ֥ם כָּל הָעָ֖ם לַֽעֲב֑וֹר. That formula matches 4:1's, but here it bridges into further narration (וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֲרוֹן יְהוָ֛ה), not new direct speech as at 4:1; it is unit-opening only when it introduces fresh speech, so here it is the report's own internal hinge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 4:10/4:11 by strict analogy to 4:1 was considered; not adopted because 4:1's instance changes discourse mode into divine speech, while 4:11a continues narration begun at v.10 - a materially weaker signal.

boundary_rationale: וַ֠יַּעַבְרוּ בְּנֵי רְאוּבֵ֨ן וּבְנֵי גָ֜ד וַחֲצִ֨י שֵׁ֤בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה֙ חֲמֻשִׁ֔ים opens with a new subject crossing armed 'as Moses spoke to them' (callback to 1:12-15), and runs through v.13's troop count. The far edge is driven by v.14's own dated formula and its subject switch to Yahweh (the row's own 'mini-colophon'); a samekh after v.13, previously uncited, corroborates that seam but does not itself close it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through v.14 as one 'crossing and exaltation' notice, on the ground Joshua remains implicit subject, was original; abandoned because v.14 opens its own dated formula and changes subject to Yahweh - the row itself called it a 'mini-colophon,' a signal class this campaign treats as unit-forming and the actual driver of this far edge, with the samekh after v.13 serving only as corroboration.

boundary_rationale: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא גִּדַּ֤ל יְהוָה֙ אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בְּעֵינֵ֖י כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל opens its own dated formula with a changed subject (Yahweh acting to exalt Joshua), echoing 3:7's promise ('I will begin to exalt you'); the near edge is corroborated by the samekh after 4:13. The pe after 4:14 sits at this same seam and corroborates it, but only as weak corroboration in a Prophets book; it is not what drives the boundary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v.14 as vv.12-13's concluding line was superseded; a self-described 'mini-colophon' is unit-forming in this campaign's own terms. The far edge was originally argued from the pe after v.14 alone, with the seam asserted through the mark and nothing else; that is corrected here, since a parashah mark cannot drive a boundary in a Prophets book. 4:15's own messenger formula was already treated as canonical elsewhere in this freeze (M8-Josh-024, M8-Josh-154) and supplies the text-internal driver this seam needs, with the pe demoted to corroboration only.
