boundary_rationale: A fresh messenger formula וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹֽר reopens direct divine speech after the exaltation notice, commanding the priests' exit, immediately fulfilled in v.18 as the waters return 'as before' - a tight command-fulfillment pair.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with the following Gilgal encampment notice (vv.19-24) as one 'aftermath' unit was considered, but v.19 opens a new subject (the people, not the priests) and a new location (Gilgal), which the next decision isolates.

literature_type_guess: Gilgal encampment, stones erected, and Joshua's didactic speech to the assembly
boundary_rationale: A dated notice, בֶּעָשׂ֖וֹר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן, marks arrival at Gilgal, followed by the stones' placement and a didactic speech. 4:21's אמר-formula has no named subject and continues the referent active since v.20 (הֵקִ֥ים יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בַּגִּלְגָּֽל); per the operative principle - explicit-subject resets (3:5, 3:6, 3:10) are boundary signals, null-subject continuations (4:21) are not - the speech stays inside this unit, closing with a purpose clause ('that all the peoples of the earth may know').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting vv.19-20 from vv.21-24 on 4:21's fresh formula, LF's reading, was tested and rejected: the formula is null-subject, not an explicit reset, and this campaign treats the two differently once stated.

literature_type_guess: transitional notice: the kings' fear at the Jordan's drying
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֣י כִשְׁמֹ֣עַ כָּל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֡י opens with the same וַיְהִי-plus-circumstantial device opening units at 1:1, 3:14, 4:1. Its close echoes 2:11's report of Rahab's speech but is not a verbatim match. 5:1's וַיִּמַּ֣ס לְבָבָ֗ם ('their heart melted') repeats 2:11's וַיִּמַּ֣ס לְבָבֵ֔נוּ ('our heart melted') verb-for-verb with only the pronoun suffix changed, but the second clause diverges: 5:1 continues וְלֹא הָ֨יָה בָ֥ם עוֹד֙ ר֔וּחַ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵֽל ('there was no longer spirit in them, because of the sons of Israel'), where 2:11 has וְלֹא קָ֨מָה ע֥וֹד ר֛וּחַ בְּאִ֖ישׁ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֑ם ('there arose no longer spirit in any man, because of you all') - a different verb (hayah against qamah) and a different prepositional object (bam against be-ish). The echo is real - one verb-phrase repeated exactly, the same two-part 'heart melts / spirit gone' idiom, the same closing מִפְּנֵי-clause pattern - but it is a partial, inexact allusion, not the verbatim two-clause fulfilment previously claimed.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Describing the echo as thematic, capping confidence at medium_low, was original; describing it as a verbatim two-clause fulfilment with the pronoun flipped, as later revised, overcorrected in the other direction - only the first clause is verbatim, and the second clause changes verb and preposition. Reassessed honestly, the echo is a genuine but partial allusion, standing alongside the unit's own independently-evidenced opening formula (matched at 1:1/3:14/4:1); together they support medium without needing an identity the text does not supply. Attaching v.1 to the circumcision unit (vv.2-9) as its frame remains a live alternative, but v.1's subject is the foreign kings, a discrete summary notice.

literature_type_guess: ritual command and etiology: circumcision at Gilgal
boundary_rationale: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ opens a divine command on circumcision; its narratorial rationale (vv.4-7) and fulfillment-plus-encampment closure at v.8, וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתָּ֛ם בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה עַ֥ד חֲיוֹתָֽם, bracket one command-fulfillment sequence. The unit stops at v.8 because v.9 opens its own full messenger formula, the construction unit-opening at 3:7/4:1/4:15/6:2/7:10; the pe cited as support falls after v.8, corroborating this edge rather than sitting inside a 5:2-9 span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 5:2-9 whole at high confidence was original; abandoned because v.9's far edge cuts through the exact formula type elsewhere decisive, and the cited pe in fact falls at the v.8/v.9 boundary. Splitting v.3/v.4 (command vs. rationale) was considered, but vv.4-7 are expository support for the one command, not a new speech-act.

oshb:Josh.5.8 וַיְהִ֛י כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּ֥מּוּ כָל הַגּ֖וֹי לְהִמּ֑וֹל וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתָּ֛ם בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה עַ֥ד חֲיוֹתָֽם

parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.5.8 (far edge, not interior)

literature_type_guess: divine word and place-name etiology: the reproach of Egypt and the naming of Gilgal
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ הַיּ֗וֹם גַּלּ֛וֹתִי אֶת חֶרְפַּ֥ת מִצְרַ֖יִם מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֑ם opens a fresh, complete messenger formula (unit-opening at 3:7/4:1/4:15/6:2/7:10) and closes on its own naming-etiology, וַיִּקְרָ֞א שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ גִּלְגָּ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה, the 'to this day' class decisive at 6:25/7:26/8:29. Both edges are independently formula-evidenced despite the unit being one verse. The forward pull toward 5:10-12 is real and is engaged rather than dismissed: 5:9 itself supplies the place name Gilgal that 5:10 immediately repeats, וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּגִּלְגָּ֑ל, and 5:10 opens with two ordinary wayyiqtol clauses - encamping, then keeping the Passover - not a 'date-formula'; the fourteenth-of-the-month date sits mid-verse, inside the Passover clause, not at its head. That catchword link is a genuine bridge between adjacent units, but it does not override the formal seam: 5:9 is Yahweh's quoted speech, sealed by its own decisive etiological closure, while 5:10 is narrated report with the nation, not Yahweh, as grammatical subject, opening an unrelated topic with no quotation formula of any kind. The closure-type and the speech-to-narration shift are what actually separate the two verses; the shared place name is a link between neighbouring units, not evidence that they are one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v.9 into 5:2-8 as its capstone, the previous position, does not survive the formula test applied elsewhere. Attaching v.9 forward to Passover (5:10-12) is the more serious alternative, and it was previously dismissed on a false description of 5:10 as opening 'its own date-formula with no connecting particle and unrelated content' - 5:10 in fact opens on two plain wayyiqtol verbs and its date phrase falls mid-verse, and its very first action-clause names Gilgal again, the place 5:9 has just named. That catchword is acknowledged rather than argued away; the merge is still not adopted, because 5:9 remains Yahweh's own quoted word sealed by a discrete 'to this day' etiology, while 5:10 is third-person narration of the nation's own action opening a new topic (Passover) with no speech formula - a stronger pair of differentiators than the mark-based or formula-shape claims previously offered.

literature_type_guess: Passover notice and the cessation of manna
boundary_rationale: A new calendrical notice, בְּאַרְבָּעָ֨ה עָשָׂ֨ר י֥וֹם לַחֹ֛דֶשׁ, opens a self-contained cultic report (Passover kept, unleavened cakes eaten, manna ceasing) with its own closing time-marker, בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִֽיא, distinguishing it from the circumcision etiology just concluded and the theophany that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with the circumcision unit as one 'rites at Gilgal' block was considered, since both are cultic preparations before Jericho, but each has its own opening date-formula and closing summary, so the register criterion favors treating them as separate, self-closing notices.

literature_type_guess: theophany: the commander of Yahweh's army
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְי֣וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ בִּירִיחוֹ֒ opens a wholly new scene - Joshua alone, a strange armed figure, a question-and-revelation exchange culminating in the holy-ground command that parallels Moses at the bush - clearly demarcated from the cultic notices before it and from Jericho's siege that begins ch.6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit into 6:1 (Jericho's shut gates) as one continuous 'approach to Jericho' sequence was considered, but 6:1 is a circumstantial/nominal clause introducing the siege premise rather than a continuation of the theophany dialogue, and is treated separately below.

oshb:Josh.5.15 שַׁל נַֽעַלְךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֔ךָ כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עָלָ֖יו קֹ֣דֶשׁ ה֑וּא

literature_type_guess: divine battle-plan speech, with its circumstantial premise (Jericho shut up) and the seven-day circuit tactics
boundary_rationale: The unit now opens with its circumstantial frame, וִֽירִיחוֹ֙ סֹגֶ֣רֶת וּמְסֻגֶּ֔רֶת מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל - a disjunctive background clause that fronts its subject (וִירִיחוֹ) before a double participial predicate (סֹגֶרֶת וּמְסֻגֶּרֶת, 'shut up and barred'), with no wayyiqtol anywhere in the verse - which the following divine word directly answers: רְאֵה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי בְיָֽדְךָ֔ אֶת יְרִיח֖וֹ. From v.2, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ opens the full tactical plan - six days of single circuits, a seventh day of sevenfold circuits, trumpets, the shout - as one continuous divine speech, closed before Joshua's relay-command begins in v.6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating v.1 as its own separate decision was original; abandoned because 6:1's fronted-subject-plus-participle clause carries no wayyiqtol and functions as pure scene-setting background, directly answered by v.2's own wayyiqtol. Citing 2:6 and 4:9 as parallels of the same verbless shape was the earlier ground for that reading; both are withdrawn as parallels, since 2:6 (וְהִ֖יא הֶעֱלָ֣תַם הַגָּ֑גָה) and 4:9 (וּשְׁתֵּ֧ים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֲבָנִ֗ים הֵקִ֣ים) are each a finite qatal clause, not verbless at all - and 4:9 carries its own 'to this day' closure and forms its own unit (M8-Josh-152), the opposite of background material. The merge does not depend on either parallel: 6:1's own syntax - fronted subject, double participle, no finite narrative verb - is what marks it as background answered by v.2's wayyiqtol. Splitting vv.3-4 from v.5 was also considered, but both remain inside the same uninterrupted quotation with no new formula between them.

literature_type_guess: Joshua's commands to priests and people
boundary_rationale: Two command notices transmit the battle plan before marching begins in v.8: v.6's וַיִּקְרָ֞א יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בִּן נוּן֙ אֶל הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים addresses the priests, and v.7 continues with Joshua as subject under the qere (ketiv ויאמרו unpointed; qere וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙, singular) now addressing הָעָם. The pair is bound by Joshua's own constant agency across both addressees, not by a priest-to-people relay only the unvocalized ketiv would support.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v.7 as a priestly relay per the unpointed ketiv's plural form was original; abandoned because the campaign's convention takes ketiv/qere as printed, and the qere's singular verb keeps Joshua as the constant speaking subject.

literature_type_guess: fulfillment narrative: day one of the circuits
boundary_rationale: The mode shifts from command to execution, וַיְהִ֗י כֶּאֱמֹ֣ר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ אֶל הָעָם֒..., narrating day one's single circuit in full, closing on its own return-and-lodging formula, וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה, corroborated by a pe immediately after v.11.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping vv.8-14 as one uniform cycle, on the premise no day carries its own closure formula, was original at high confidence; the premise is false - day one closes at v.11, the six-day summary closes to match at v.14, and v.12's rise-early formula is the same construction opening fresh units at 3:1 and 7:16.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.6.8 וַיְהִ֗י כֶּאֱמֹ֣ר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ אֶל הָעָם֒
oshb:Josh.6.11 וַיַּסֵּ֤ב אֲרוֹן יְהוָה֙ אֶת הָעִ֔יר הַקֵּ֖ף פַּ֣עַם אֶחָ֑ת וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה

literature_type_guess: fulfillment narrative: the repeated circuits of days two through six, summarized
boundary_rationale: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֥ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בַּבֹּ֑קֶר reopens the rise-early formula marking a fresh day at 3:1 and 7:16, narrating the remaining circuits in compressed, uniform register and closing on its own camp-return notice, וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה ('and they returned to the camp'). That closure shares its FUNCTION and its day-cycle position with v.11's own camp notice, וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה ('and it came to the camp') - both mark the end of a day's circuit before lodging or resuming - but the two are not a verbal match: v.11 uses בוא ('come'), v.14 uses שוב ('return'), and וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה is otherwise unattested elsewhere in the book. The real far-edge signal is the summary that follows it, כֹּ֥ה עָשׂ֖וּ שֵׁ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים ('thus they did six days'), sealing the whole day-two-through-six cycle immediately before v.15's distinct, formally marked seventh-day opener, וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping this joined to day one (vv.8-11) as one undifferentiated cycle was original, abandoned for the reasons given at M8-Josh-030: day one has its own closure, this summary has a matching one, and the rise-early formula is a real day-boundary elsewhere.

oshb:Josh.6.14 וַיָּסֹ֨בּוּ אֶת הָעִ֜יר בַּיּ֤וֹם הַשֵּׁנִי֙ פַּ֣עַם אַחַ֔ת וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה כֹּ֥ה עָשׂ֖וּ שֵׁ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים

literature_type_guess: the seventh day: sevenfold circuit and herem instructions
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י marks the day-shift called for in the original plan (v.4's 'on the seventh day'), and the unit adds new material absent from the six-day cycle: Joshua's shout-command and the herem instructions protecting Rahab and reserving metal for the treasury.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the seventh day into the six-day cycle as one 'circuits' unit spanning vv.8-19 was considered on register grounds (all are circuit-marching), but the seventh day is explicitly marked as unique in the text itself, רַ֚ק בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא סָבְב֥וּ אֶת הָעִ֖יר שֶׁ֥בַע פְּעָמִֽים, which is a content-differentiation strong enough to break the uniform register.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.6.19 וְכֹ֣ל כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֗ב... אוֹצַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה יָבֽוֹא

literature_type_guess: the shout, the wall's fall, and the city's destruction
boundary_rationale: The mode shifts sharply from command to a compressed climactic report - shout, wall-fall, capture, total destruction - marked by וַיָּ֣רַע הָעָ֔ם וַֽיִּתְקְע֖וּ בַּשֹּׁפָר֑וֹת, the fulfillment of the sign predicted back in v.5.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through the Rahab rescue (vv.22-25) as one 'fall of Jericho' block was considered, but vv.22 opens a new command from Joshua to the spies specifically about Rahab, distinct from the general destruction just narrated, so it is treated as its own unit below.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.6.20 וַיָּ֣רַע הָעָ֔ם וַֽיִּתְקְע֖וּ בַּשֹּׁפָר֑וֹת... וַתִּפֹּ֨ל הַֽחוֹמָ֜ה תַּחְתֶּ֗יהָ
oshb:Josh.6.21 וַֽיַּחֲרִ֨ימוּ֙ אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּעִ֔יר

literature_type_guess: Rahab's household spared and Jericho burned
boundary_rationale: וְלִשְׁנַ֨יִם הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים הַֽמְרַגְּלִ֤ים אֶת הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ opens with a fronted-PP-plus-qatal address formula (waw, prepositional phrase naming the addressees, then אָמַ֣ר), the identical construction unit-opening at 1:12, וְלָרֽאוּבֵנִי֙ וְלַגָּדִ֔י וְלַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ. As a backgrounding, topicalizing construction it is a real but comparatively softer scene-opening signal than a fresh wayyiqtol, fulfilling the oath of chapter 2 by dispatching the spies to retrieve Rahab. The unit closes with וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בְּקֶ֣רֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה, corroborated by a pe after v.25.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Citing a wayyiqtol וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ as the near-edge formula, matching the mainline-formula splits elsewhere, was original; the text does not support it. Reading v.22 as a mere continuation of vv.20-21's destruction report was also considered, but the shift to naming the two spies and reopening the Rahab plot is a real topic change even under the weaker formula, so the boundary holds - only the strength of evidence changes.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.6.22 וְלִשְׁנַ֨יִם הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים הַֽמְרַגְּלִ֤ים אֶת הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בֹּ֖אוּ בֵּית הָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַזּוֹנָ֑ה
oshb:Josh.1.12 וְלָרֽאוּבֵנִי֙ וְלַגָּדִ֔י וְלַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹֽר
oshb:Josh.6.25 וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בְּקֶ֣רֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה

literature_type_guess: Joshua's rebuilding curse-oath and closing fame notice
boundary_rationale: A distinct oath-formula, וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖יא לֵאמֹ֑ר, closes the Jericho campaign with a curse on any future rebuilder, and v.27's fame notice, וַיְהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ, functions as the chapter's summary colophon, matching the pattern of closing theological asides seen elsewhere in the book.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping this with the Rahab unit as the chapter's single closing movement was considered, but the curse-oath is addressed to no one present in the narrative (a standing proclamation 'before Yahweh') and is thematically distinct from the household-rescue notice, warranting separation.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.6.26 וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖יא לֵאמֹ֑ר אָר֨וּר הָאִ֜ישׁ
oshb:Josh.6.27 וַיְהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וַיְהִ֥י שָׁמְע֖וֹ בְּכָל הָאָֽרֶץ

literature_type_guess: narratorial trespass notice (thematic introduction to the Achan crisis)
boundary_rationale: A summary-judgment sentence in the narrator's voice, וַיִּמְעֲל֧וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מַ֖עַל בַּחֵ֑רֶם, names the offender by a four-generation genealogy and closes on וַיִּֽחַר אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בִּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל ('the anger of Yahweh burned'). That anger-onset is answered, root for root, by 7:26's close, וַיָּ֥שָׁב יְהוָ֖ה מֵחֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ ('Yahweh turned from the fierceness of his anger') - a verifiable חֲרוֹן אַף inclusio bracketing the whole Achan pericope, a real structural marker carried by the verse itself, not the parashah layer, and not a mere thematic resemblance as originally described.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v.1 into the spy-dispatch of vv.2-5 as one 'introduction to Ai' unit was considered, but v.1 names Achan and states Yahweh's anger as an omniscient aside vv.2ff's characters do not yet know, a distinguishable narratorial frame. Pricing the row on the genealogical-superscription argument alone, as originally drafted, undersold the unit; the חֲרוֹן אַף inclusio gives this opening verse more structural weight, even though its partner clause sits twenty-five verses later in the same chapter, not - as an earlier draft of this row stated - five chapters away.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.7.1 וַיִּמְעֲל֧וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מַ֖עַל בַּחֵ֑רֶם וַיִּקַּ֡ח עָכָ֣ן בֶּן כַּרְמִי֩ ... וַיִּֽחַר אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בִּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
web:Josh.7.1 the children of Israel committed a trespass in the devoted things

literature_type_guess: reconnaissance and the defeat at Ai
boundary_rationale: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מִֽירִיח֗וֹ הָעַ֞י opens the actual scene, spies sent to Ai, advice to send a small force, and the resulting rout, closing on the people's melted hearts, וַיִּמַּ֥ס לְבַב הָעָ֖ם וַיְהִ֥י לְמָֽיִם - an ironic echo of 2:11 and 5:1 now turned against Israel itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this into Joshua's lament (vv.6-9) as one 'defeat and reaction' unit was considered, but v.6 opens with a new subject and posture (Joshua tearing his clothes before the ark) that begins a distinct prayer scene rather than continuing the battle report.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.7.2 וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מִֽירִיח֗וֹ הָעַ֞י
oshb:Josh.7.5 וַיִּמַּ֥ס לְבַב הָעָ֖ם וַיְהִ֥י לְמָֽיִם
web:Josh.7.5 The hearts of the people melted, and became like water

boundary_rationale: וַיִּקְרַ֨ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ שִׂמְלֹתָ֗יו opens a mourning posture and a prayer-complaint addressed to Yahweh, אֲהָ֣הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה, distinct in mode (address to the deity, not narration of battle) and closing on the rhetorical question about Yahweh's great name.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging the lament with Yahweh's response (vv.10-15) as one continuous exchange was considered, but v.10 opens with a fresh divine speech-formula that rebukes Joshua's posture ('why have you fallen on your face'), a clear turn answered by new content, not a continuation of Joshua's own words.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.7.6 וַיִּקְרַ֨ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ שִׂמְלֹתָ֗יו וַיִּפֹּל֩ עַל פָּנָ֨יו אַ֜רְצָה
parashah_two_witness: samekh after Josh.7.9 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: divine response: instructions for the lot-casting process
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ קֻ֣ם לָ֑ךְ opens Yahweh's rebuke and the detailed tribe-family-household-man procedure for identifying the offender, self-contained through the burning-with-fire sentence in v.15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the rebuke (v.10-12) from the procedural instructions (vv.13-15) was considered, since the tone shifts from accusation to procedure, but both remain inside the same uninterrupted divine speech with no new formula, so they stay together.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.7.10 וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ קֻ֣ם לָ֑ךְ
oshb:Josh.7.14 וְהָיָ֡ה הַשֵּׁבֶט֩ אֲשֶׁר יִלְכְּדֶ֨נּוּ יְהוָ֜ה יִקְרַ֣ב לַמִּשְׁפָּח֗וֹת
web:Josh.7.14 the tribe which Yahweh selects shall come near by families

literature_type_guess: the lot narrows to Achan (procedural fulfillment)
boundary_rationale: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֤ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר shifts to fulfillment mode, executing the four-stage procedure just commanded (tribe, family, household, man) and closing when Achan himself is taken, וַיִּלָּכֵ֖ד עָכָ֞ן.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with the interrogation that follows (vv.19-21) as one 'identification and confession' unit was considered, but v.19 opens fresh direct speech, Joshua's appeal for confession, distinct from the silent, mechanical lot-narrowing just narrated.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.7.16 וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֤ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיַּקְרֵ֥ב אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לִשְׁבָטָ֑יו

boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶל עָכָ֗ן opens a direct appeal for confession answered by Achan's own first-person account of coveting the robe, silver, and gold wedge, a self-contained speech exchange closed by his admission of where the goods are hidden.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this through the retrieval of the goods (vv.22-23) as one 'confession and verification' unit was considered, but v.22 shifts to Joshua dispatching messengers - a new action initiated by Joshua rather than continued speech from Achan - so it is treated separately.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.7.19 וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶל עָכָ֗ן בְּנִי֙ שִֽׂים נָ֣א כָב֗וֹד
oshb:Josh.7.21 וְהִנָּ֨ם טְמוּנִ֥ים בָּאָ֛רֶץ בְּת֥וֹךְ הָאָֽהֳלִ֖י וְהַכֶּ֥סֶף תַּחְתֶּֽיהָ
web:Josh.7.21 they are hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent

boundary_rationale: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים opens a brief dispatch-and-retrieval notice confirming Achan's confession physically, closing when the goods are 'laid down before Yahweh' - a short verification act bridging confession and sentence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this into the confession unit (vv.19-21) as its natural continuation was considered, since it is simply confirming what Achan just said; it is kept separate because it is Joshua's own initiated action (messengers running to the tent) rather than reported speech, matching this chapter's pattern of separating speech from action.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.7.22 וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיָּרֻ֖צוּ הָאֹ֑הֱלָה

literature_type_guess: execution in the Valley of Achor and etiology
boundary_rationale: וַיִּקַּ֣ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ אֶת עָכָ֣ן opens the final act - Achan, his family, and goods taken up to the valley, stoned and burned - and closes with a double naming etiology, גַּל אֲבָנִ֣ים גָּד֗וֹל עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה and קָרָ֞א שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ עֵ֣מֶק עָכ֔וֹר, that closes the whole Achan crisis and reverses its opening 'anger burned' notice with 'Yahweh turned from the fierceness of his anger.'
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the execution (v.24-25) from the etiological colophon (v.26) was considered, but the 'to this day' formula in v.26 functions as the closing bracket for the entire trespass narrative opened in v.1, and separating it would strand the colophon from the event it explains.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.7.25 וַיִּרְגְּמ֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶ֔בֶן
parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.7.26 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אַל תִּירָ֣א reopens direct divine speech after the Achan crisis is resolved, explicitly permitting the plunder this time (a contrast with Jericho's total herem), and authorizes the ambush strategy elaborated in the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this brief authorization with Joshua's elaborated battle plan (vv.3-9) as one continuous speech was considered, but v.3 shifts from Yahweh speaking to Joshua acting and then speaking to his own troops, a speaker change the chapter consistently treats as boundary-forming.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.8.1 וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אַל תִּירָ֣א וְאַל תֵּחָ֔ת
oshb:Josh.8.2 רַק שְׁלָלָ֥הּ וּבְהֶמְתָּ֖הּ תָּבֹ֣זּוּ לָכֶ֑ם

boundary_rationale: וַיָּ֧קָם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ shifts to Joshua acting on Yahweh's word, choosing thirty thousand men and giving detailed feigned-retreat instructions, closing when the ambush party takes position, וַיָּ֧לֶן יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַה֖וּא בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעָֽם ('and Joshua lodged that night among the people') - the qamats-pointed וַיָּלֶן, deliberately distinct from 8:13's וַיֵּלֶךְ ('and Joshua went'), the verb closing the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the deployment (v.3) from Joshua's spoken instructions (vv.4-8) was considered, but the instructions are Joshua's own direct elaboration of the same command just given, with no addressee change, so the whole planning sequence stays one unit.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.8.3 וַיָּ֧קָם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ וְכָל עַ֥ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה לַעֲל֣וֹת הָעָ֑י
oshb:Josh.8.9 וַיָּ֧לֶן יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַה֖וּא בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעָֽם
oshb:Josh.8.13 וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַה֖וּא בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעֵֽמֶק

boundary_rationale: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֤ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר marks a new day and troop muster, positioning the main force north of the city and the ambush west of it, closing with Joshua entering the valley by night - purely logistical narration without direct speech, distinct from the planning speech that precedes it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the positioning into the planning unit (vv.3-9) as one seamless 'preparation' block was considered, since it executes the same plan without interruption; it is kept separate because a new-day marker and a shift from command-speech to silent troop movement mark a discrete narrative beat.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.8.10 וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֤ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּפְקֹ֖ד אֶת הָעָ֑ם
oshb:Josh.8.13 וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַה֖וּא בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעֵֽמֶק

literature_type_guess: Ai's king draws out the city and Israel feigns retreat
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֞י כִּרְא֣וֹת מֶֽלֶךְ הָעַ֗י shifts viewpoint to Ai's king, who rushes out to battle unaware of the ambush, and the unit closes on the notice that not a man remained in Ai or Bethel, וְלֹֽא נִשְׁאַ֣ר אִ֗ישׁ בָּעַי֙ וּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔ל - the precondition the ambush plan required.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this through the javelin signal (vv.18-19) as one 'battle unfolds' unit was considered, but v.18 opens a fresh Yahweh-to-Joshua command that triggers the ambush's actual assault, a distinct command-and-signal beat from the maneuvering just described.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.8.17 וְלֹֽא נִשְׁאַ֣ר אִ֗ישׁ בָּעַי֙ וּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יָצְא֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.8.17 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: the javelin signal and the ambush's capture of the city
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ נְ֠טֵה בַּכִּיד֤וֹן reopens divine speech giving the signal, immediately fulfilled as the ambush 'ran as soon as he had stretched out his hand,' and the unit closes with the king of Ai taken alive, a discrete tactical climax before the destruction report.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the signal-and-capture (vv.18-19) from the pincer-and-king-capture (vv.20-23) was considered, but there is no new formula between them - the men of Ai's confused retreat directly continues the same tactical sequence set in motion by the javelin sign, so they remain one unit.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.8.18 וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ נְ֠טֵה בַּכִּיד֤וֹן אֲשֶׁר בְּיָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל הָעַ֔י
oshb:Josh.8.23 וְאֶת מֶ֥לֶךְ הָעַ֖י תָּ֣פְשׂוּ חָ֑י

literature_type_guess: destruction of Ai and the king's execution
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֣י כְּכַלּ֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל לַהֲרֹג֩ shifts to the mopping-up and total-count report, the king's hanging and cairn, closing with a second 'to this day' notice, גַּל אֲבָנִ֣ים גָּד֔וֹל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה, mirroring 7:26's Achan cairn. This וַיְהִי כְּכַלּוֹת clause is boundary-forming here on positional grounds: it stands at the head of a fresh report - the total count of the fallen (v.25), the burning of the city, and the king's execution and cairn (vv.26-29) all follow as content the preceding decision (M8-Josh-047, closing at 8:23 with the king taken alive) does not reach. The same construction recurs at 10:20 inside M8-Josh-059 without opening a unit there, because it sits inside a pursuit already underway since 10:19's command and closes off action already in progress rather than heading a fresh report; the two instances are resolved by that positional principle, not by any claim about which side's killing had or had not already been narrated.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this into the Ebal altar-building of vv.30-35 as one 'aftermath of Ai' unit was considered, but v.30's אָ֣ז marks a fresh, undated jump away from Ai entirely, treated as its own scene by the next decision. An earlier version of the reconciliation with M8-Josh-059 claimed the field-slaughter of Ai's other inhabitants 'is new' at this verse; that is inaccurate - 8:21-22, inside the immediately preceding M8-Josh-047 span, already narrate the field-slaughter twice (וַיָּשֻׁ֕בוּ וַיַּכּ֖וּ אֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעָֽי; וַיַּכּ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִ֥יר) before this verse's completion clause restates it. The positional principle above - fresh report versus already-open pursuit - replaces that narrated/unnarrated test.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.8.25 וַיְהִי֩ כָל הַנֹּ֨פְלִ֜ים בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙
oshb:Josh.8.29 וַיָּקִ֤ימוּ עָלָיו֙ גַּל אֲבָנִ֣ים גָּד֔וֹל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה
oshb:Josh.8.23 וְאֶת מֶ֥לֶךְ הָעַ֖י תָּ֣פְשׂוּ חָ֑י וַיַּקְרִ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל יְהוֹשֻֽׁעַ
oshb:Josh.10.20 וַיְהִי֩ כְּכַלּ֨וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְהַכּוֹתָ֛ם

literature_type_guess: Ebal altar-building, law inscription, and covenant reading
boundary_rationale: אָ֣ז יִבְנֶ֤ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ opens with the אָז+yiqtol construction this book uses to jump scenes, matching 10:12 (אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֤ר) and 22:1 (אָ֚ז יִקְרָ֣א), a real comparative pattern against 10:33's אָז+qatal (אָ֣ז עָלָ֗ה), left unit-internal by this draft. That signal is secondary - established only by comparison across three other passages - but genuine, and co-occurs with a total location change to Mount Ebal. Participants do carry over: כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ appears at 8:24 and וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל at 8:33, so the unit is not the clean break 'no participant carried over except Joshua' suggested. The far edge is undisputed: a double register shift into torah-citation content, a pe after v.35, and 9:1's fresh coalition-response formula immediately following.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 8:30-35 as chronologically displaced material is a long-standing critical alternative this non-authorizing draft does not adopt, since owner rules require the text's received order. Pricing the near edge at 'no independently driving signal at all' was original; not defensible once the אָז+yiqtol/אָז+qatal contrast and participant continuity are checked; medium_low, not low, is the supported price.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.10.33 אָ֣ז עָלָ֗ה הֹרָם֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ גֶּ֔זֶר

literature_type_guess: coalition notice: the kings gather against Israel
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֣י כִשְׁמֹ֣עַ כָּֽל הַמְּלָכִ֡ים is the recurring type-scene formula this book uses to open king-response pericopae (compare 5:1, 10:1, 11:1), here summarizing a six-nation coalition 'with one accord,' פֶּ֖ה אֶחָֽד, before the Gibeonites' contrasting response is narrated in v.3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this into the Gibeonite ruse narrative that follows (vv.3-13) as one 'nations respond to the conquest' unit was considered, but vv.1-2 describe a general coalition that never actually appears again in this chapter (contrast with Gibeon's separate strategy in v.3), making it a distinct scene-setting notice.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.9.1 וַיְהִ֣י כִשְׁמֹ֣עַ כָּֽל הַמְּלָכִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ בְּעֵ֨בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֜ן
oshb:Josh.9.2 וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עִם יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וְעִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל פֶּ֖ה אֶחָֽד
parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.9.2 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: the Gibeonite ruse and its presentation to Joshua
boundary_rationale: וְיֹשְׁבֵ֨י גִבְע֜וֹן שָׁמְע֗וּ opens Gibeon's response, a deception prepared in vv.4-5 and carried to the Israelite camp at Gilgal in v.6, where it is defended and runs continuously through v.13's closing claim about the moldy bread and worn-out garments. Location shifts to Gilgal at v.6 and Joshua/אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל enter as new participants there, but this is the ruse's own delivery, not an independent scene break: the deception prepared in vv.4-5 has no payoff until presented and defended.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the preparation (vv.3-6) from the defending speech (vv.7-13) was considered. Splitting instead at v.5/v.6, where location and cast change, is the stronger untested alternative and is taken seriously; not adopted because the change is the ruse's own delivery to its intended audience, not a new inciting action.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.9.3 וְיֹשְׁבֵ֨י גִבְע֜וֹן שָׁמְע֗וּ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֧ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ
oshb:Josh.9.6 וַיֵּלְכ֧וּ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הַגִּלְגָּ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו וְאֶל אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל

boundary_rationale: A short narratorial verdict, וְאֶת פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א שָׁאָֽלוּ ('and they did not ask counsel at the mouth of Yahweh'), interrupts the dialogue to render the men's error explicit, then the treaty is concluded and sworn - a hinge bridging deception to discovery. (Accent correction: the particle אֶת carries no accent of its own in MT; the previous rationale's pointing was in error.)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this pair to the preceding negotiation as its natural conclusion was considered, but the narratorial aside is an omniscient judgment absent from the Gibeonites' own speech, marking a shift from reported dialogue to narratorial commentary.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.9.14 וַיִּקְח֥וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֖ים מִצֵּידָ֑ם וְאֶת פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א שָׁאָֽלוּ

literature_type_guess: discovery of the ruse and the princes' decision to spare them
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים marks a temporal jump of three days and a new discovery ('they heard that they were their neighbors'), opening the congregation's murmur and the princes' oath-bound decision, closed by the princes' own ruling that the Gibeonites become woodcutters and water-drawers.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this through Joshua's direct address to the Gibeonites (vv.22-27) as one 'consequences of the ruse' unit was considered, but v.22 opens Joshua's own speech-formula, a distinct confrontation scene following the princes' internal deliberation, so it is treated separately.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.9.16 וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֕י אֲשֶׁר כָּרְת֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם בְּרִ֑ית
oshb:Josh.9.21 וַ֠יִּֽהְיוּ חֹטְבֵ֨י עֵצִ֤ים וְשֹֽׁאֲבֵי מַ֨יִם֙

literature_type_guess: Joshua's curse and permanent servitude assignment
boundary_rationale: וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ opens Joshua's own direct confrontation and curse, distinct from the princes' internal ruling just narrated, and the unit closes the chapter with a colophon-style notice, וּלְמִזְבַּ֤ח יְהוָה֙ עַד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחָֽר, projecting the servitude arrangement forward to the (still future) chosen sanctuary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Joshua's curse-speech with the princes' preceding decision as one continuous 'resolution' unit was considered, but Joshua's speech-formula and his direct second-person address to the Gibeonites themselves ('why have you deceived us') mark a new confrontation the princes never staged.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.9.22 וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר
parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.9.27 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: coalition notice: five Amorite kings mobilize against Gibeon
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹֽנִי צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם opens the same recurring 'when [king] heard' type-scene as 9:1, naming Adoni-Zedek and the four kings he recruits, closing when the coalition 'encamped against Gibeon, and made war against it.' (Accent correction: the telisha qetana on וַיְהִי is postpositive in OSHB, after the final yod, not before it as previously printed.)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the initial hearing-and-fear (vv.1-2) from the mustering of allies (vv.3-5) was considered, but both remain a single uninterrupted narratorial report with no speech-formula reset between them.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.10.1 וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹֽנִי צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם
oshb:Josh.10.5 וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ עַל גִּבְע֔וֹן וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ

boundary_rationale: A new messenger formula, וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ גִבְע֨וֹן אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ, opens Gibeon's plea invoking chapter 9's treaty, answered by Joshua's march from Gilgal - a compact pair distinct from the coalition notice before it and the divine assurance after it. Convention note: the two-witness site 'pe after Josh.10.7' names the seam it follows (v.7/v.8), so it corroborates this decision's far edge rather than contesting its near edge at v.6, worth stating explicitly since the convention has been misread against this row before.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the appeal into the coalition-formation unit (vv.1-5) as one continuous 'siege of Gibeon' report was considered, but the appeal introduces Gibeon's own direct speech and Joshua as a new responding subject.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.10.6 וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ גִבְע֨וֹן אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֣לָה
parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.10.7 (names the v.7/v.8 seam)

literature_type_guess: divine assurance, the battle, and the hailstones
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אַל תִּירָ֣א reopens divine speech, immediately followed by the night march, the rout at Gibeon, and the extraordinary hailstone notice ('more who died from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel killed with the sword') that theologically frames the battle before the sun-standing-still episode.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this through the sun-and-moon episode (vv.12-14) as one continuous 'battle account' unit was considered, but v.12 opens with אָ֣ז ('then') and a shift to Joshua's own poetic speech, a distinct mode (quoted verse) from the third-person battle report just given.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.10.8 וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אַל תִּירָ֣א מֵהֶ֔ם
oshb:Josh.10.11 רַבִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁר מֵ֨תוּ֙ בְּאַבְנֵ֣י הַבָּרָ֔ד מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרְג֛וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּחָֽרֶב
parashah_two_witness: samekh after Josh.10.11 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: the Book-of-Jashar poem citation: sun and moon halted
boundary_rationale: אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה is the narrator's frame introducing Joshua's own quoted words, שֶׁ֚מֶשׁ בְּגִבְע֣וֹן דּ֔וֹם, which the narrator then explicitly sources, הֲלֹא הִ֥יא כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל סֵ֣פֶר הַיָּשָׁ֑ר, before v.14 closes with a narratorial theological comment ('there was no day like that') that caps the citation rather than continuing the poem itself; the whole three-verse unit is kept together because the closing comment interprets the just-quoted poem and cannot stand alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating v.13's citation formula alone as its own micro-unit, separate from Joshua's introductory speech (v.12) and the narrator's closing comment (v.14), was considered, but splitting a quotation from its introducing frame and its interpreting comment would fragment a single citation event that the text presents as one rhetorical whole; confidence is capped at medium because the quotation's exact boundaries (where poetry ends and prose resumes) remain genuinely disputed among readers.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.10.13 הֲלֹא הִ֥יא כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל סֵ֣פֶר הַיָּשָׁ֑ר
parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.10.14 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: return to Gilgal and the five kings found in the cave
boundary_rationale: וַיָּ֤שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ marks a return-to-base notice (v.15) immediately undercut by the discovery report about the hiding kings and Joshua's command to seal the cave and continue pursuit (vv.16-19), closing with the army's peaceful return to Makkedah (v.21). The completion clause at v.20, וַיְהִי֩ כְּכַלּ֨וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְהַכּוֹתָ֛ם, matches the construction opening M8-Josh-048 at 8:24, but is not boundary-forming here. The two instances are distinguished by their position relative to the surrounding report, not by which side had already narrated its killing: 8:24 stands at the head of a fresh report - the total count, the city's burning, and the king's execution and cairn all follow it as new content - while 10:20 sits inside a pursuit already opened at v.19's imperative, רִדְפוּ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֹֽיְבֵיכֶ֔ם, with the same participants (Joshua and the sons of Israel) carried forward without a subject reset, and no closure tag anywhere between v.19 and v.21's own return-to-camp notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 10:15-19/10:20-21 by bare analogy to 8:24 was considered and rejected on the position-based principle above. An earlier version of this reconciliation tested whether each construction's content had already been narrated, stating that 8:24 was boundary-forming because 'the field-slaughter is not yet narrated' there, against 10:20 merely 'closing off action already commanded.' That test in fact ran backward: 8:21-22 (וַיָּשֻׁ֕בוּ וַיַּכּ֖וּ אֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעָֽי; וַיַּכּ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִ֥יר) narrate the field-slaughter twice before 8:24's completion clause, while 10:19 only commands the pursuit and nothing narrates its execution before 10:20 declares it complete - the opposite of what the test assumed. That narrated/unnarrated test is dropped here in favor of the position-based one above: 10:20 stays inside this span because it closes off pursuit already commanded within it, with unbroken participant continuity and no intervening closure tag, not because of any claim about what had or had not been told.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.10.15 וַיָּ֤שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עִמּ֔וֹ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הַגִּלְגָּֽלָה
oshb:Josh.10.20 וַיְהִי֩ כְּכַלּ֨וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְהַכּוֹתָ֛ם

literature_type_guess: the five kings brought out, executed, and entombed
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ פִּתְח֖וּ אֶת פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֑ה opens the ceremonial extraction of the kings, the neck-treading gesture, execution, and their disposal back into the very cave that had hidden them, closed by the 'to this day' cairn notice matching the pattern of 7:26 and 8:29.

boundary_rationale: This is the first of a run of near-identical city-capture reports; its opening syntax, וְאֶת מַקֵּדָה֩ לָכַ֨ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא, fronts the object before a bare qatal rather than the march-formula (וַיַּעֲבֹר) of the middle entries - the same disjunctive construction later opening 11:12's generalizing notice - marking a deliberate opening beat. Its closure, כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיחֽוֹ, ties it back to Jericho, marking it complete in itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the whole southern city run as one uniform register-unit, on the model of ch.12's tally, was considered; rejected not because ch.10's entries carry more individualized detail (M8-Josh-075 shows detail alone does not force a split) but because every entry here closes on its own comparative formula naming an antecedent city - even where that antecedent repeats, as 10:28 and 10:30 both close by comparison with the king of Jericho - a discrete per-entry closure ch.12 never supplies. The discriminator is the presence of that per-entry closure, not whether the compared city changes from entry to entry.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Gezer's relief notice (v.33) from Lachish's capture (vv.31-32) was considered, since the interior pe marks a real seam; not adopted because v.33 lacks its own capture or comparative-closure formula and would stand orphaned. boundary_rationale: וַיַּ֣עַל יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָֽל יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מֵעֶגְל֖וֹנָה חֶבְר֑וֹנָה shifts the motion verb from וַיַּעֲבֹר (Libnah, Lachish, Eglon) to וַיַּ֣עַל, tracking Hebron's elevation, closing on its own comparative formula to Eglon, כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה לְעֶגְל֑וֹן. Better described as a family of motion-verb-plus-destination constructions with Makkedah's opening as the deliberate exception. Folding Debir into the colophon (vv.40-43) was considered, but it still opens with its own motion-verb-plus-destination pattern, so it stays a peer entry.

boundary_rationale: וְֽאֶת כָּל עָרֵ֣י הַמְּלָכִֽים generalizes from Hazor to 'all the cities of those kings,' noting they were not burned, and closes with a Mosaic-obedience colophon, לֹֽא הֵסִ֣יר דָּבָ֔ר מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת מֹשֶֽׁה. Disclosed: this same four-word close recurs at 11:20's ...כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה, a genuine echo independent of paragraphing, read as a wider bracket over the whole 11:12-20 complex rather than proof v.15 belongs forward with vv.16-20: v.15's closest tie is backward to the execution notice just narrated, and v.16 opens its own fresh territorial register bracketing forward to 11:23 (M8-Josh-074).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Re-cutting to bracket 11:15-20 as one refrain-closed unit was seriously considered given the genuine echo; not adopted because v.15's strongest formal tie is backward to the obedience-colophon pattern closing vv.12-14, while the 15/20 echo operates at the level of the larger complex. Leaving v.15 to open 072 alone was also considered, but it would then introduce nothing of its own (v.16 is territorial summary, not obedience).

literature_type_guess: colophon: the whole land taken, land rests from war
boundary_rationale: This single verse closes the entire conquest narrative (chs.1-11) with a summary formula, וַיִּקַּ֨ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶת כָּל הָאָ֗רֶץ, and the refrain וְהָאָ֥רֶץ שָׁקְטָ֖ה מִמִּלְחָמָֽה, which recurs verbatim - letter for letter, including accents - at 14:15. The near edge is now also evidenced: 11:16 opens with the same five-word formula, וַיִּקַּ֨ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶת כָּל הָאָ֗רֶץ, extending it with one further word, הַזֹּ֗את, not present at 11:23 - the consonants match across both openings, though the accentuation of ha-arets differs between them (unlike the 11:23/14:15 refrain, which matches down to the accents) - an inclusio bracketing the whole 11:16-23 complex. With both edges independently formula-evidenced, this row clears the both-edges bar for confidence above medium.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this verse into the preceding Anakim notice was considered, but the totalizing language and land-rest refrain mark this as the book's structural hinge into the allotment section. Leaving the near edge unevidenced, as originally drafted, undersold the row; once the 11:16/11:23 inclusio is credited, both edges are independently held.

literature_type_guess: register: kings defeated by Moses east of the Jordan, with boundary description
boundary_rationale: וְאֵ֣לֶּה מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֗רֶץ opens a distinct superscription formula naming only two Transjordan kings, Sihon and Og, each given a full boundary description rather than a bare tally, and the unit closes with Moses' own grant formula to Reuben, Gad, and half-Manasseh - a register genuinely different in form from the thirty-one-king tally that follows in vv.9-24.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all of chapter 12 (Transjordan and Cisjordan kings alike) as one undivided register was considered, but v.7's fresh superscription, 'these are the kings... whom Joshua and the children of Israel struck,' explicitly reopens the list with a new subject (Joshua, not Moses) and a new geographic scope, which this draft treats as the operative division.

literature_type_guess: superscription: transition to the western kings register
boundary_rationale: וְאֵ֣לֶּה מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֡רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ הִכָּ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ repeats the superscription formula of v.1 but changes the subject to Joshua and the geographic frame to west of the Jordan, functioning as a heading for the list that follows rather than part of either the eastern register before it or the bare tally after it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this heading directly to the thirty-one-king tally (vv.9-24) as its introductory frame was considered and is a reasonable alternative reading; it is kept separate here because vv.7-8 still uses full-sentence narrative prose (ethnic groups, terrain types) rather than the bare 'king of X, one' formula that begins abruptly at v.9, marking a genre shift within the superscribed material.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.12.7 וְאֵ֣לֶּה מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֡רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ הִכָּ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ יָ֔מָּה

literature_type_guess: register: the thirty-one defeated kings, per-entry tally formula
boundary_rationale: From v.9 the list drops the narrative prose of vv.7-8 for the formula מֶ֥לֶךְ [place] אֶחָ֑ד, varying only by appositional geographic disambiguators (12:9's אֲשֶׁר מִצַּ֥ד בֵּֽית אֵ֖ל, 12:20's שִׁמְר֤וֹן מְראוֹן֙, 12:23's two packed entries), closed by one summary total, כָּל מְלָכִ֖ים שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְאֶחָֽד. The template's accentuation tracks verse position, not entry: אֶחָד takes zaqef qatan on a verse's first member and silluq on its second across 12:10-22, but not at boundary verses 12:9/12:23, which open on atnach instead. Applying register-closure on this corrected basis: no entry carries its own individualized closure the way each ch.10 city does; the sole closure for the whole block is the aggregate total at 12:24, and there are zero interior parashah marks across 12:9-23 against five structuring ch.10's run. The near edge is credited with the same genre shift M8-Josh-076 relies on for its own far edge, corroborated by the pe after 12:8; even so, v.9 remains in form a continuation of 12:7's superscription, so the near edge is real but secondary, and the row does not clear the both-edges-independent bar for confidence above medium.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting into thirty-one one-line decisions, by analogy to ch.10, was considered; rejected because the differentiator that splits ch.10 is not 'individualized detail' in the abstract (M8-Josh-075 shows detail alone does not force a split) but a discrete, entry-specific comparative closure this block never supplies except its single aggregate total. 'Grammatically identical apart from the proper name' was original and overstated, corrected above.

literature_type_guess: divine mandate to divide the land, with an inventory of what remains unconquered
boundary_rationale: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו opens a single divine speech that moves from Joshua's old age, through an inventory of unconquered Philistine and Geshurite territory, to the command 'divide this land for an inheritance,' all inside one unbroken quotation with no reintroduction of speaker between the age-notice and the land inventory.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the age-notice (v.1) from the land inventory and division command (vv.2-7) was considered, since v.1 could stand as narratorial scene-setting like 23:1's near-identical opening; it loses because here v.1 itself already contains the messenger formula introducing the very speech that continues through v.7, unlike 23:1 which precedes a separate assembly notice.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.13.1 וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו

literature_type_guess: narratorial summary: the Transjordan inheritance already granted by Moses
boundary_rationale: עִמּ֗וֹ הָרֽאוּבֵנִי֙ וְהַגָּדִ֔י לָקְח֖וּ נַחֲלָתָ֑ם shifts from divine speech to third-person narratorial summary, closing with the Levites' landlessness formula, אִשֵּׁ֨י יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ ה֣וּא נַחֲלָת֔וֹ. Disclosed at the near edge: v.8 opens on the bound form עִמּ֗וֹ, whose antecedent, וַחֲצִ֖י הַשֵּׁ֥בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּֽׁה, sits at the end of v.7 - the unit's first word cannot be parsed without reaching back across the seam. Weighed against this: the discourse-mode shift from second-person imperative ('divide this land,' v.7) to third-person narration ('the Reubenites and Gadites have taken,' v.8) is judged the more decisive signal, marking the transition from quoted command to narratorial exposition. A caveat on the comparison drawn to 3:14: that verse is not a clean 'boundary without a formula' precedent, since 3:14 itself opens on its own וַיְהִי-plus-infinitive-construct device (וַיְהִ֗י בִּנְסֹ֤עַ הָעָם֙ מֵאָ֣הֳלֵיהֶ֔ם), the same construction credited as unit-opening at M8-Josh-023; 13:8, by contrast, has no opener of its own at all, only the bound עִמּוֹ reaching back into v.7. The discourse-mode shift therefore has to carry this seam on its own merits, without a formula-free precedent to lean on; the resumptive עִמּוֹ is read as the narrator's own linking device into that exposition, not proof vv.7-8 form one unbroken unit. Confidence is lowered to reflect this unresolved backward dependency.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Leaving the עִמּוֹ dependency unaddressed, as originally drafted, is not defensible. Re-cutting to include v.7's second half inside this unit was considered to resolve the dependency structurally; not adopted because it would split a single grammatical sentence (Yahweh's one command, running to v.7's end) mid-verse, which this campaign avoids absent much stronger reason, and the discourse-mode boundary genuinely falls at the verse seam even though the pronoun reaches back across it.

literature_type_guess: tribal boundary description with city-catalogue notice: Reuben
boundary_rationale: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי רְאוּבֵ֖ן opens Reuben's own named grant, giving both border description and an embedded narrative aside (the death of Balaam, v.22, otherwise unexplained here), and closes with the נַחֲלַת-colophon, זֹ֣את נַחֲלַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי רְאוּבֵן֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔ם הֶעָרִ֖ים וְחַצְרֵיהֶֽן, that this draft treats consistently as marking the end of each tribal grant throughout the allotment section.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the Balaam notice (v.22) out as its own unit was considered, since it is a narrative aside amid a border list, but it has no independent speech-formula or scene-change of its own and functions as an appended detail within Reuben's inheritance report, so it stays inside the tribal unit.

literature_type_guess: tribal boundary description with colophon: Gad
boundary_rationale: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן מֹשֶׁה֙ לְמַטֵּה גָ֔ד repeats the same grant-formula used to open Reuben's territory, now with Gad as subject, and closes on the identical נַחֲלַת-colophon pattern, זֹ֛את נַחֲלַ֥ת בְּנֵי גָ֖ד לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם הֶעָרִ֖ים וְחַצְרֵיהֶֽם, confirming the colophon as this section's consistent tribal-unit boundary marker.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Reuben and Gad into a single 'Reubenite-Gadite' unit was considered, since both tribes share the same general Transjordan region and grantor (Moses), but each receives its own opening grant-formula and its own closing נַחֲלַת-colophon, and this draft treats that repeated bracket as the operative signal rather than shared geography.

literature_type_guess: tribal boundary description: half-Manasseh in Transjordan
boundary_rationale: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה לַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה opens the third and final Transjordan grant, naming Machir's descendants specifically, but unlike Reuben and Gad it lacks its own נַחֲלַת-colophon, running instead directly into the shared Transjordan summary of vv.32-33 - a genuine asymmetry in the pattern that this draft treats honestly rather than forcing a colophon that is not there.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending half-Manasseh's territory through the shared colophon (making it 13:29-33 in one unit, matching Reuben and Gad's self-contained pattern) was strongly considered for consistency; it is not adopted because vv.32-33 explicitly generalizes to 'these are the inheritances which Moses distributed' (all three Transjordan tribes together) rather than closing Manasseh alone, so the colophon is shared, not tribe-specific, and is better treated as its own unit below.

oshb:Josh.13.31 לִבְנֵ֤י מָכִיר֙ בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לַחֲצִ֥י בְנֵֽי מָכִ֖יר לְמִשְׁפְּחוֹתָֽם

literature_type_guess: shared colophon: Transjordan grants summarized; Levites' exception repeated in variant form
boundary_rationale: אֵ֕לֶּה אֲשֶׁר נִחַ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת מוֹאָ֑ב generalizes over all three preceding Transjordan grants at once with a plural demonstrative (אֵלֶּה), which cannot grammatically seal a single tribe's unit the way Gad's singular זֹאת does one cluster earlier at 13:28 - itself evidence the summary operates at a different structural level. v.33 then repeats the Levites'-no-inheritance notice from v.14, but in variant form rather than verbatim: v.33 opens with the conjunction וּ where v.14 has the restrictive רַק (רַ֚ק לְשֵׁ֣בֶט הַלֵּוִ֔י לֹ֥א נָתַ֖ן נַחֲלָ֑ה vs. וּלְשֵׁ֨בֶט֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י לֹֽא נָתַ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֖ה נַחֲלָ֑ה), v.33 names מֹשֶׁה as the explicit subject of the giving-verb where v.14 leaves it implicit, v.14's grounding clause אִשֵּׁ֨י יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ ה֣וּא נַחֲלָת֔וֹ ('the fire-offerings of Yahweh, he is their inheritance') is replaced in v.33 by the more direct יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ ה֣וּא נַחֲלָתָ֔ם with the grounding phrase dropped, and the pronominal suffixes shift from singular (נַחֲלָת֔וֹ, לֽוֹ) to plural (נַחֲלָתָ֔ם, לָהֶֽם). Four differences, not zero. As a formulaic-with-variation repetition it still forms a real inclusio bracketing the Transjordan section (vv.15-33) as a unit of units; that conclusion does not depend on exact identity. Disclosure: a samekh is attested after Josh.13.32, but that site falls inside this decision's own span, not at either edge, so it is recorded here as a non-driving interior marker rather than filed as boundary evidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the Levites repetition (v.33) as evidence of scribal duplication to be silently merged with v.14 rather than kept as a fresh decision was considered; it is retained as its own citation because it functions as a deliberate closing inclusio-bracket for this sub-section in formulaic-with-variation form, not as redundant material to be suppressed - the four recorded differences (subject, particle, grounding clause, suffix number) are consistent with deliberate restatement rather than accidental duplication.

literature_type_guess: superscription: process for the Cisjordan allotment
boundary_rationale: וְאֵ֛לֶּה אֲשֶׁר נָחֲל֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן opens a fresh superscription formula (matching the אֵלֶּה-openers used at 12:1, 12:7, and 13:32) naming the allotment officials - Eleazar, Joshua, tribal heads - and the lot-casting method, before Caleb's approach begins a new named episode in v.6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this superscription through Caleb's speech (making 14:1-12 one unit) was considered, since Caleb's approach happens 'at Gilgal' during this same allotment process, but v.6 opens with a fresh subject and location marker, וַיִּגְּשׁ֨וּ בְנֵֽי יְהוּדָ֤ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּגִּלְגָּ֔ל, introducing named individuals absent from the general superscription.

boundary_rationale: וַיִּגְּשׁ֨וּ בְנֵֽי יְהוּדָ֤ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּגִּלְגָּ֔ל introduces Caleb by name and patronymic, and his own first-person speech runs unbroken from the Kadesh Barnea recollection through the age-notice ('eighty-five years old, today') to the request for Hebron's hill country, with no reintroduction of speaker throughout.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the historical recollection (vv.6-9, quoting Moses' oath) from the present-day petition (vv.10-12) was considered, since the content shifts from past to present, but Caleb never stops speaking and no new formula intervenes, so campaign precedent keeps the whole speech as one unit.

literature_type_guess: grant of Hebron to Caleb, colophon, land-rest refrain

A pe stands after 15:19, at the same seam, but only as weak corroboration in a Prophets book, not as a driver; there is no WEB paragraph break unique to this seam that can be counted as evidence (WEB paragraphing is metadata under this campaign's own rule, stated at M8-Josh-098). v.21 itself opens its own specific catalogue formula, וַיִּֽהְי֣וּ הֶעָרִ֗ים מִקְצֵה֙ לְמַטֵּ֣ה בְנֵֽי יְהוּדָ֔ה - formally identical in shape to 18:21's וְהָי֣וּ הֶֽעָרִ֗ים לְמַטֵּ֛ה בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן, which M8-Josh-112 treats as unit-opening in its own right - but that formula sits inside this span and so cannot itself evidence the 15:19|20 seam; it is recorded as an internal feature only, not counted toward the near edge. The זֹאת נַחֲלַת...לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם wording is not read as one uniform function across this freeze, and that tension is stated rather than hidden: at 18:20 (M8-Josh-161) and 19:8 (M8-Josh-163) the identical formula closes a tribe's material, while at v.12 and here at v.20 it is the closing-colophon language itself that gets echoed to signal 'the list resumes' after the Caleb-Achsah interruption - a resumptive use of a normally closing form, not a fresh heading built from scratch. With the WEB citation removed and the pe demoted to weak corroboration, medium is what the near edge's single, real text signal supports; the far edge's numeral-plus-samekh close remains solid on its own.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v.20 as the closing colophon of the preceding Achsah narrative rather than the heading of the city list was considered, since its wording nearly duplicates v.12's; it is read here as heading material because it functions as a Wiederaufnahme resuming the list after the digression, not because of any marker. High confidence built on stacking a Prophets-book pe, a WEB paragraph break, and v.21's span-interior catalogue formula as three independent near-edge signals was the prior treatment; it is not adopted because the pe cannot drive, the WEB break is metadata, and a formula that sits inside the span cannot evidence the seam above it - leaving only the Wiederaufnahme as the near edge's actual support, which is real but singular, not the multiply-corroborated base high requires.

literature_type_guess: notice of failure to dispossess: the Jebusites at Jerusalem
boundary_rationale: This closing verse returns to narrative prose after eleven verses of pure catalogue, reporting that Judah 'could not drive out' the Jebusites - the first instance of this book's failure-notice family, structurally distinct from every city-list entry preceding it. The family is not one uniform construction: this verse and Josh.17.12 share the modal construction לֹא + יָכְלוּ + infinitive, while Josh.16.10 (now its own decision, M8-Josh-164) uses a plain unmodalized negated Hiphil with no ability verb, and Josh.17.13 adds a further intensified infinitive-absolute construction unique to that notice. The family resemblance (a recurring 'failed to dispossess' report) is real and worth tracking across the allotment chapters, but the claim that nothing differentiates their closural force does not hold and is not repeated here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating this verse as simply the closing line of the wilderness-cities cluster (folding it into 15:61-62) was considered, but it names a people-group failure rather than a city count, and this draft treats the 'could not drive out' notices as their own literary type throughout the allotment chapters, while now disclosing that the type has at least two distinct verbal sub-constructions rather than one uniform shape.

Family principle, stated once here for the whole family: these are related but formally distinct constructions, not one uniform type. 15:63 and this verse (17:12) share the modal construction לֹא + יָכְלוּ + infinitive; 16:10's וְלֹא הוֹרִישׁוּ is a plain unmodalized negated Hiphil with no ability verb and no explicit subject; and v.13 here adds a further intensification unique to this notice, the infinitive-absolute construction וְהוֹרֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א הוֹרִישֽׁוֹ. With 16:9-10 now split (M8-Josh-103/164), each of the three notices genuinely stands on its own as this row's rationale claims, rather than the claim being contradicted by an adjacent merge.

literature_type_guess: tribal boundary description: Benjamin, west quarter
boundary_rationale: וַיַּ֗עַל גּוֹרַ֛ל מַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי בִנְיָמִ֖ן opens Benjamin's own lot-formula, the same strong near-edge signal class used to open every other tribal allotment in this section, and traces the border through to its west-quarter close, זֹ֖את פְּאַת יָֽם - a deictic-plus-border-noun closing tag of the same shape as Judah's 15:4 (זֶה יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֥וּל נֶֽגֶב). Previously this whole span ran to 18:20 on the claim that none of Benjamin's internal directional headings carries its own closing tag; that claim is false. 18:14 and 18:19 both close on independent deictic tags, and 18:15 opens a fresh cardinal heading (וּפְאַת נֶ֕גְבָּה), so Benjamin's border description in fact supplies three discrete closures (west at v.14, south at v.19, east-plus-tribal-colophon at v.20) where Judah's supplies only two (south at v.4, then one continuous close at v.12 for the remaining three sides). The register-closure criterion, applied consistently, divides Benjamin into three units rather than one. strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the general instruction to speak (v.1-2) from the detailed procedural law (vv.3-6) was considered, since a second imperative, דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל, occurs at v.2; it loses because v.2 is itself still inside the same unbroken divine quotation to Joshua, not a new addressee shift the way, for example, ch.3's officers-then-priests pattern worked.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.20.1 וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹֽר
oshb:Josh.20.6 עַד מוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֑ם

literature_type_guess: execution notice: the six refuge cities named, with colophon
boundary_rationale: וַיַּקְדִּ֜שׁוּ shifts from command to fulfillment, naming the three western cities (Kedesh, Shechem, Hebron) and three eastern (Bezer, Ramoth, Golan), closing with a summary colophon, אֵ֣לֶּה הָיוּ֩ עָרֵ֨י הַמּֽוּעָדָ֜ה לְכֹ֣ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְלַגֵּר֙, that extends the law's protection explicitly to resident aliens.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging the naming of the cities (vv.7-8) with the divine speech that commissioned them (vv.1-6) as one continuous law-and-execution unit was considered, but the shift from second-person legal instruction to third-person fulfillment narration is the same speech-to-narration boundary applied consistently throughout this book.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.20.9 אֵ֣לֶּה הָיוּ֩ עָרֵ֨י הַמּֽוּעָדָ֜ה לְכֹ֣ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְלַגֵּר֙ הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֔ם
parashah_two_witness: pe after Josh.20.9 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: Levites' request and grant of cities, bracketed by a resumptive-repetition inclusio around the clan-by-clan lot totals
boundary_rationale: וַֽיִּגְּשׁ֗וּ רָאשֵׁי֙ אֲב֣וֹת הַלְוִיִּ֔ם opens a new petitioning group (the Levite family heads, paralleling Zelophehad's daughters' approach at 17:3-4, though 17:4's verb, וַתִּקְרַ֡בְנָה, is a different root and the parallel is thematic rather than lexical), invoking the Mosaic command for pasture-land cities. The request is granted at v.3, וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל לַלְוִיִּ֛ם מִנַּחֲלָתָ֖ם אֶל פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֶת הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֶת מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽן, and the same nine-word sequence recurs almost exactly at v.8's close, וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם ... אֶת הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֶת מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶ֑ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד מֹשֶׁ֖ה בַּגּוֹרָֽל. That resumptive repetition brackets the intervening clan-by-clan lot totals (vv.4-7, the Kohathite/Aaronic/remaining-Kohathite/Gershonite/Merarite distribution) as an insert within one continuous grant scene, on the same principle this draft already applies to the weaker, chiastic doubling at 22:6-8 (M8-Josh-131). Splitting at v.3/v.4 on the ground that v.4 reopens with its own lot-formula, as previously done, cuts across that bracket: a fresh lot-formula opening an interior insert is not evidence against a resumptive repetition closing around it, any more than the Manasseh aside at 22:7 was read as breaking that chapter's dismissal scene. Disclosed: samekh markers stand after 21:4, 21:5, and 21:6, all interior to this span; no marker of either kind stands at the 21:3/21:4 seam this decision's prior span treated as a boundary. Medium reflects a genuine textual bracket (the near-verbatim envelope) balanced against the acknowledged internal complexity of a merged span covering two originally distinct sub-genres (a request-and-grant narrative, then a numeric overview).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 21:3/21:4 into a request-and-grant decision (21:1-3) and a separate clan-totals overview (21:4-8) was the prior treatment, on the ground that v.4 opens its own lot-formula; it is not adopted because it cuts through the v.3//v.8 resumptive repetition without ever engaging it, and this campaign's own stated Wiederaufnahme rule (applied at 22:6-8, on weaker textual grounds) reads such doubling as bracketing an inserted aside within one continuous scene, not as evidence of two units.

oshb:Josh.21.8 וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם אֶת הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֶת מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶ֑ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד מֹשֶׁ֖ה בַּגּוֹרָֽל (nine-word resumptive repetition closing the bracket opened at v.3)

parashah_two_witness: samekh after Josh.21.4, Josh.21.5, Josh.21.6 (interior to this span, disclosed); pe after Josh.21.8 (weak corroboration, Prophets, at the far edge)

literature_type_guess: detailed city-list register with colophon: Aaron's priestly cities
boundary_rationale: וַֽיִּתְּנ֗וּ מִמַּטֵּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה opens the first detailed, named list - Hebron and eight others from Judah/Simeon, then four from Benjamin - explicitly for 'the children of Aaron... for theirs was the first lot,' closing on its own tally, כָּל עָרֵ֥י בְנֵֽי אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֑ים שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה עָרִ֖ים וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽן.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the Hebron/Caleb aside (vv.11-12, noting the city's fields went to Caleb rather than the priests) as its own decision was considered, since it briefly digresses from the pure list format; it loses because it has no independent formula and functions as an explanatory parenthesis within the single Aaron notice, resolving a tension with 14:13-14 and 15:13 rather than opening a new unit.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.21.9 וַֽיִּתְּנ֗וּ מִמַּטֵּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּמִמַּטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֑וֹן
oshb:Josh.21.19 כָּל עָרֵ֥י בְנֵֽי אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֑ים שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה עָרִ֖ים וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽן
parashah_two_witness: samekh after Josh.21.19 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: detailed city-list register with colophon: the remaining Kohathites' cities
boundary_rationale: וּלְמִשְׁפְּח֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי קְהָת֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם הַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים opens the second Levite-clan list (Ephraim, Dan, half-Manasseh), naming Shechem as a city of refuge among them - the second such notice after Hebron's in v.13 - and closing on its own tally, כָּל עָרִ֥ים עֶ֖שֶׂר וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶ֑ן.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging all four Levite-clan lists (vv.9-40) into one giant register on the model applied to ch.12's king tally was considered, but unlike ch.12's bare 'king of X, one' formula, each clan's list here is individually content-differentiated (different tribes contributing, different refuge-city notices, different totals) and each carries its own discrete closing tally, meeting this campaign's register/closure test for splitting rather than merging.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.21.20 וּלְמִשְׁפְּח֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי קְהָת֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם הַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים

literature_type_guess: detailed city-list register with colophon: the Gershonites' cities
boundary_rationale: וְלִבְנֵ֣י גֵרְשׁוֹן֮ opens the third clan-list (half-Manasseh in Bashan, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali), including Golan as a third refuge-city notice, and closes on its own tally, כָּל עָרֵ֥י הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה עִ֖יר וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽן.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping the Gershonite list with the Merarite list that follows into one 'remaining two clans' unit was considered, since both lack priestly status unlike the Kohathites; it loses on the same closure-test grounds applied throughout this chapter - the Gershonite tally is independent and complete in itself before the Merarite list opens with its own fresh heading.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.21.33 כָּל עָרֵ֥י הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה עִ֖יר וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽן

literature_type_guess: detailed city-list register with colophon: the Merarites' cities (including the disputed 21:36-37)
boundary_rationale: וּלְמִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת בְּנֵֽי מְרָרִי֮ opens the fourth and final clan-list, closing on its own tally, וַיְהִי֙ גּוֹרָלָ֔ם עָרִ֖ים שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵֽה. The Reubenite cities at vv.36-37 (Bezer, Jahzah, Kedemoth, Mephaath) are present in both OSHB and the UXLC tradition consulted for this campaign, but this pair of verses is well known to be absent from a number of medieval Masoretic manuscript witnesses and printed Rabbinic Bibles - a text-critical variance disclosed here rather than resolved. Two independent controls bear on it: removing vv.36-37 would break the stated total of twelve Merarite cities at v.40, and, independently of that arithmetic, Josh.21.7 already names Reuben among the three Merarite donor tribes (מִמַּטֵּ֨ה רְאוּבֵ֤ן וּמִמַּטֵּה גָד֙ וּמִמַּטֵּ֣ה זְבוּלֻ֔ן), so a Merarite list with no Reubenite cities at all would conflict with the donor-tribe list given earlier in the same chapter. Both controls point the same direction without depending on each other. Disclosed, non-boundary: a samekh is attested after Josh.21.37, but that site falls inside this span (before v.38), not at either edge, and is recorded here as an interior marker rather than filed as boundary evidence. Medium_low reflects that the heading-to-tally shape survives either textual reading of vv.36-37, while the closing number itself remains textually unstable - the discount properly reflects that the closing arithmetic, not the boundary location, is what the variance touches.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Silently omitting citation of the 21:36-37 controversy and treating the span as an unremarkable continuation of the list was considered and rejected, since the owner's hard test explicitly requires this manuscript variance to be disclosed in the affected decision's rationale rather than passed over; citing only the twelve-city arithmetic as the reason to retain vv.36-37, without the independent donor-tribe control at 21:7, was also considered and is now supplemented rather than left as the sole textual anchor.

oshb:Josh.21.7 מִמַּטֵּ֨ה רְאוּבֵ֤ן וּמִמַּטֵּה גָד֙ וּמִמַּטֵּ֣ה זְבוּלֻ֔ן (independent donor-tribe control for vv.36-37)
oshb:Josh.21.36 וּמִמַּטֵּ֣ה רְאוּבֵ֔ן אֶת בֶּ֖צֶר וְאֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֑הָ
oshb:Josh.21.40 וַיְהִי֙ גּוֹרָלָ֔ם עָרִ֖ים שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵֽה
disclosed, non-boundary: parashah_two_witness samekh after Josh.21.37 (interior to Josh.21.34-40, not an edge)

boundary_rationale: כֹּ֚ל עָרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל sums all four clan-totals into a single grand total, forty-eight cities, and adds a generalizing formula, כֵּ֖ן לְכָל הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה, that functions as the closing bracket for the entire Levitical-cities section opened at 21:1, distinct from the four individual clan colophons already given.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this grand total into the Merarite unit as its closing line was considered, since it immediately follows; it loses because it explicitly totals all four clans together (forty-eight, not the Merarite twelve alone), functioning at a different structural level than any single clan's colophon.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Josh.21.41 כֹּ֚ל עָרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עָרִ֛ים אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנֶ֖ה
parashah_two_witness: samekh after Josh.21.42 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

literature_type_guess: theological colophon: the land fully given, rest granted, no word failed
boundary_rationale: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת כָּל הָאָ֔רֶץ shifts from administrative tally to theological summation - the land given exactly as sworn, rest granted, no enemy standing - closing the entire allotment section (chs.13-21) with the refrain לֹֽא נָפַ֣ל דָּבָ֔ר מִכֹּל֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַטּ֔וֹב אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה, a formula that will be echoed almost verbatim by Joshua himself in 23:14.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this theological colophon with the numeric colophon of vv.41-42 as one undivided close to the chapter was considered, but the shift from administrative counting to covenant-fulfillment theology is a genre change this draft treats as a real boundary, matching the distinction already drawn between colophon types throughout the allotment section.
