boundary_rationale: Opens with Samson's direct prayer to Yahweh ('remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this once...that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes'), his first prayer since the thirst-cry of 15:18, and narrates his positioning between the two middle pillars and his final declaration, 'Let me die with the Philistines!' Closes with the collapse and the totalizing verdict that 'the dead that he killed at his death were more than those who he killed in his life' (v30). v31 shifts to his brothers' recovery of the body, a new set of participants and a calmer register.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through v31 (the burial and tenure notice) as one continuous death-and-aftermath span was considered; rejected because v31 introduces new participants performing a distinct action days or longer after the collapse, plus the second tenure-closure formula treated as its own decision.

literature_type_guess: burial notice and cycle tenure-closure (second half of the doubled colophon)
boundary_rationale: A single verse combining Samson's burial with the second occurrence of the tenure-formula. This decision discloses the doubled colophon explicitly rather than resolving it by omission: Samson's tenure is stated twice, once mid-career (15:20) and once at his death (here). The two notices are not verbally identical, and the corrected comparison strengthens rather than weakens the disclosure this decision exists to make: 15:20 uses wayyiqtol with no independent subject and adds 'in the days of the Philistines'; 16:31 uses a fronted independent pronoun (הוּא) plus qatal and omits that phrase. The shared material is limited to אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה, and the root שׁפט. Two structurally different colophon constructions bracket the same twenty-year figure; disclosing that divergence honestly is this decision's task, and the divergence itself is not read here as evidence one way or the other about deliberate design. This book's own comparandum runs the other direction: the refrain this campaign already treats as a deliberate literary bracket, 17:6/21:25 (M8-Judg-174), is byte-identical, cantillation included, and it is that identity, not divergence, that this campaign takes as the signature of an intentional inclusio. The 15:20/16:31 doubling is accordingly disclosed on its own terms - two notices, genuinely different in form, both standing at real narrative pauses - without the further claim that their divergence itself argues for a considered two-panel composition. Closes the entire Samson complex before ch17 opens the appendices with no framework formula at all.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged in conclusion: treating only this verse as the real closing formula and downgrading 15:20 to a mere narrative aside was considered and rejected; both notices stand at genuine narrative pauses, so privileging one over the other would suppress rather than disclose the doubling this campaign's hard tests require addressing. M8-Judg-122's own phrasing for the same relationship, 'an almost identical notice,' is the accurate formulation and now governs the language used here as well.

boundary_rationale: Opens the appendices with a wholly new register - no framework formula, simply 'There was a man of the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Micayehu' - and narrates his confession, his mother's blessing, his restitution, and her dedication of silver to a silversmith for a carved and molten image. Closes with the image's completion, 'It was in the house of Micayehu' (v4). The right edge is now credited with two independent signals beyond register alone: the disjunctive construction opening 17:5 (waw + fronted definite subject + nominal predicate, וְהָאִ֣ישׁ מִיכָ֔ה), and a name-form isogloss - the long form מִיכָיְהוּ occurs only at 17:1 and 17:4, and the short form מִיכָה governs from 17:5 through the end of chapter 18. The changeover coincides exactly with the drafted boundary. v5 shifts to a summary description of Micah's private shrine.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged: extending this unit through v6 (including the 'no king in Israel' refrain) as one continuous opening scene was considered and rejected; v5-6 shifts from the dialogue-driven theft-and-restitution narrative to a static inventory-and-editorial-comment register, a genuine form change from scene to summary, now additionally marked by the name-form changeover and the disjunctive clause opening v5.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the summary inventory of Micah's private religious establishment-'a house of gods...an ephod, and teraphim,' a consecrated son as priest-a static register distinct from the preceding dialogue scene. Closes with the full-form refrain, 'In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did that which was right in his own eyes' (v6), functioning here as editorial commentary closing this notice by explaining the social conditions that permitted a private, unauthorized cult to exist. This campaign's principled treatment reads the full two-clause form as a closing device bracketing units, distinct from the short one-clause form that opens units at 18:1 and 19:1. v7 opens an entirely new character, the wandering Levite.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the refrain here as opening the following Levite narrative (7-13), matching its function at 18:1/19:1, was considered; rejected because this occurrence uses the full two-clause form reserved, per this campaign's disclosed treatment, for closing bookends (matching 21:25), while the short form alone opens units elsewhere.

literature_type_guess: recruitment narrative (the wandering Levite hired as priest)
boundary_rationale: Opens with the introduction of 'a young man out of Bethlehem Judah...who was a Levite,' a wholly new named-but-unnamed character replacing the shrine-inventory register, and narrates his wandering, arrival at Micah's house, their negotiation over wages and role, and his consecration as household priest. Closes with Micah's confident theological conclusion, 'Now I know that Yahweh will do good to me, since I have a Levite as my priest' (v13)-a self-satisfied verdict ironically undercut by everything that follows in ch18. Ch18:1 opens with the refrain again, this time in short form fused with a new subject, marking a fresh narrative unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the Levite's journey and hiring (7-12) from Micah's concluding statement (v13) was considered; rejected because v13 is Micah's own direct-speech reaction to the hiring just completed, forming one continuous cause-and-reflection unit with no scene break.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the short-form refrain at 18:1, whose cohesion with the new Danite subject rests on resumptive repetition of the temporal adverbial (בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם...וּבַיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם), not on the two clauses being grammatically fused into a single continuous sentence - both clauses are independently athnach-divided, the same pausal structure the full-form refrain carries at 17:6 and 21:25. Narrates the dispatch of five spies; closes with their lodging (v2). v3's opening (הֵ֚מָּה עִם בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וְהֵ֣מָּה הִכִּ֔ירוּ) is a continuative circumstantial clause naming no new participant and restating the location v2 has just reached, which weakens rather than strengthens this decision's closing edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives are on record. (a) Treating the refrain (v1a) as its own micro-unit was considered and rejected on the corrected ground of resumptive repetition (not fusion) binding it to the Danite notice. (b) Testing whether 18:1-2 should instead extend through 18:6 (merging with M8-Judg-139) to close on the priest's oracle formula לְכ֣וּ לְשָׁל֑וֹם, where both parashah witnesses register a petuchah, was not previously tested. It is a real competitor - v3's circumstantial opener supplies no independent reset - but is not adopted: M8-Judg-139's own opening (the voice-recognition at 18:3, the first thing in the chapter that is not itinerary) is treated as a genuine scene-trigger in its own right, and collapsing the 138/139 boundary would lose a distinction the campaign protects carefully elsewhere between narration and the report or recognition that reframes it. The span is kept at Judg.18.1-Judg.18.2 with confidence lowered to reflect that its closing edge is soft.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the spies' recognition of 'the voice of the young man the Levite,' a specific personal encounter distinct from the general lodging-notice of v2, and their questioning of him about his role, his explanation, and their request for a divine oracle about their mission's prospects. Closes with the priest's favorable oracle, 'Go in peace. Your way in which you go is before Yahweh' (v6). v7 shifts location entirely to Laish, the spies' actual reconnaissance destination.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Including the Laish observation by running this unit to v7 was considered; v7's own wording, 'Then the five men departed and came to Laish,' is an explicit departure-and-arrival formula marking the move from Micah's house to the reconnaissance target itself.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse scene shift to Laish. The opening edge is stronger than previously credited: 18:7 opens וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לָ֑יְשָׁה, a full subject respecification after four verses of inflection-only reference, paired with a departure-arrival verb pair reaching a new place - genuine text signals, not merely 'no dialogue.' The closing edge is the one that is honestly weak: 18:8 continues וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם with no subject respecified and no temporal or spatial reset beyond the next stage of the same itinerary, simply repeating v7's arrival verb for the return leg. The only differentiator is register (third-person narration versus reported speech beginning at v8), and register alone does not carry an edge under this campaign's symmetric-marker-insufficiency principle. No parashah mark falls anywhere in 18:7-10, and WEB in fact runs 18:7-8 together as one paragraph, starting fresh only at 18:9 - external evidence that, if anything, favors folding v7 forward rather than treating it as freestanding.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The merge tested (folding 18:7 down into the report scene, 141) is the wrong one to have relied on alone. The alternative that actually threatens this decision - reading 18:7-10 as one reconnaissance-and-report unit bracketed by the two arrivals (וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ at v7, וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ at v8) - is now tested here honestly. It has real support: no independent text signal separates v7 from v8 beyond register, and WEB's own paragraphing runs the two together. Against it: the report in vv8-10 is explicitly cast as the spies' own reported dialogue to a different audience (their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol) at a different location, which this campaign treats elsewhere as a genuine narratorial-voice-versus-direct-speech distinction (compare the same distinction protecting 140/141 from 139 above). The span is retained as its own single-verse decision, but the confidence rating's own hedge is now correctly located: it protects against the closing edge's weakness, not against uniform uncertainty across the whole verse.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the Laish description (140) into this report as the spies' own words was considered; rejected because v7's description is narrated directly by the narrator in the third person without any 'they said' framing, while vv8-10 is explicitly cast as the spies' reported dialogue-a genuine narratorial-voice-versus-direct-speech distinction.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the formal muster notice, 'The family of the Danites set out from Zorah and Eshtaol with six hundred men armed with weapons of war,' a shift from persuasive speech to collective military action, and narrates their encampment at Kiriath Jearim (with its own etiological aside, 'Mahaneh Dan to this day') before continuing to the hill country of Ephraim. Closes with their arrival 'to the house of Micah' (v13). v14 opens the spies' specific proposal about the idols, a return to individual speech.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One march-and-raid span through v17, taking in the actual theft, seemed workable at first; it doesn't hold because v14 returns to the five original spies speaking, bringing individual dialogue back after the collective muster-and-march notice of 11-13.

literature_type_guess: theft narrative (idols taken under armed guard)
boundary_rationale: Opens with the five original spies' proposal to their kinsmen about the ephod, teraphim, and images (18:14), a return to individual speech after the collective muster notice, and narrates the theft while the six hundred armed men and the priest stand guard at the gate. The clause at 18:17 (arrival and taking of the four objects) is picked back up verbatim in structure at 18:18 (וְאֵ֗לֶּה בָּ֚אוּ בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וַיִּקְחוּ֙...) after the parenthetical gate-guard aside - a resumptive repetition (Wiederaufnahme) that signals continuity across what the original decisions treated as a boundary, not a fresh start. The priest's challenge (מָ֥ה אַתֶּ֖ם עֹשִֽׂים, 18:18b) sits behind that resumption, and the Danites' counter-offer and his acceptance follow in one unbroken sequence. Closes with the priest's glad assent and his crossing over to join the people (וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָעָֽם, 18:20). v21 turns the whole column around with וַיִּפְנ֖וּ וַיֵּלֵ֑ךְ, a genuine register change to logistics and departure, which is where the next unit (145) already opens. External evidence, previously undisclosed: WEB opens paragraphs at 18:18, 18:19, and 18:20 - the priest's challenge, the Danites' counter-offer, and his acceptance each set off as their own paragraph - but these read as dialogue-turn markers within one continuous exchange rather than section divisions, consistent with the chapter's dense paragraphing elsewhere (18:1, 18:4, 18:5, 18:6, 18:7, 18:9, 18:11, 18:14 are all turn- or beat-level breaks in the same stretch); the next section-level break does not fall until 18:24. The adopted close at 18:20|18:21 itself carries no external witness at all - WEB runs no break there, and the parashah tradition places no mark anywhere between the pe after 18:6 and the pe after 18:31 - so this boundary rests on the register change alone (dialogue and logistics to a march-and-departure notice), disclosed here as an evidenced, not a silent, choice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The alternative previously tested (splitting v14 from vv15-17) answered the wrong question and left the operative one - whether anything actually begins at 18:18 - unexamined. Tested now: closing at 18:17 and opening a fresh unit at 18:18 was considered and rejected, because 18:18's opening clause repeats material already given at 18:17 rather than introducing anything new; a boundary cannot be anchored on a signal (the priest's challenge) that arrives behind a resumptive clause. The unit is instead closed at 18:20, where the priest's assent and his physical crossing to the Danites is the real terminus, confirmed independently by M8-Judg-145's own already-frozen opening evidence at 18:21. This disclosure follows the standard M8-Judg-140 sets within this same chunk: state the paragraph and parashah evidence in full, including where it might be read to favor an alternative, rather than resting a register-change argument on an undisclosed record - now met here by the paragraph and parashah citations added to this decision's own evidence block.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the group's departure, dependants and goods placed before them (v21), and narrates the pursuit and confrontation. A stated rule now governs the pronoun-fronted circumstantial frame (הֵ֚מָּה / הֵ֥מָּה) across the range: where it introduces no new agent, it is continuative (18:3, opening M8-Judg-139); where it introduces one, it is ordinarily disjunctive and opens a unit (19:22, opening M8-Judg-152). 18:22 (הֵ֥מָּה הִרְחִ֖יקוּ מִבֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֑ה וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּבָּתִּים֙...נִֽזְעֲק֔וּ) is the one place the principle is not applied to open a unit, and that is now a stated, principled override rather than a silent inconsistency: departure, pursuit, confrontation and retreat here form one continuous escalating encounter carried by vav-consecutive with no reset at any interior seam, and splitting at 18:22 would sever the pursuers' mobilization from the very departure that triggers it. Closes with Micah's retreat home (v26), ending his role in the narrative. v27 shifts to the Danites' continued march with no further reference to Micah.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the departure/pursuit (21-23) from the confrontation-and-retreat (24-26) was considered and rejected, as before. Newly tested: splitting at 18:21/18:22 (departure alone, against pursuit-through-retreat as its own unit) under the new-agent-introduced principle that governs 19:22 elsewhere in this range. Rejected on the stated ground above - the pursuit is the direct and immediate consequence of the departure it follows, and treating 18:22 as an opener here would break a single escalating chain that the campaign keeps whole in comparable cases (e.g., the Gibeah demand-to-assault sequence at 19:22-26 itself, kept whole despite its own internal agent shifts).

literature_type_guess: cultic installation notice and priestly genealogy
boundary_rationale: Opens with the installation of Micah's image among the Danites and the genealogical notice naming the founding priest, printed in the consonantal text as בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה, 'son of Manasseh' - no accent mark belongs on the bare בֶּן here (a prior citation error inserted one; corrected below). Rabbinic tradition reads this as the Masorah's suspended-letter device (nun taluy: an extra nun raised above the line, traditionally read as inserted into what would otherwise read Mosheh, 'Moses') - the smoothing move, not the disclosure - but that suspension itself is a scribal/typographic convention this workspace's plain consonantal encoding does not represent in any form: the stored source shows an ordinary בֶּן with no raised letter, no ketiv/qere pair, and none of the marks (U+05C4, U+05C5) this same file uses elsewhere to encode such pairs (compare the bare-form-then-pointed-form sequences at 19:3, 1:27, and 4:11, none of which are present here). The startling detail (a line traced to Moses serving an idol at the book's structural hinge) is preserved instead in the traditional reading that WEB follows ('the son of Moses'), read against the plain consonantal מְנַשֶּׁה the workspace does show. The decision now states the divergence accurately, without asserting a Masoretic device this file cannot itself witness: the plain consonantal text reads 'Manasseh,' the traditional reading follows 'Moses,' and the assigned inputs are silent on which is prior or on how any suspended letter is to be represented. Closes with a second, parallel duration-notice (v31), corroborated by a pe, ending the whole Danite migration complex. Ch19:1 opens the refrain again in its short, unit-opening form.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged: treating v30 and v31 as two separate decisions was considered and rejected; both are parallel, complementary closing notices about the same installed image with no scene-break or speech-formula between them, reading as one compound closure.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the refrain at 19:1, correctly placed at a chapter line ahead of a new, previously unseen protagonist, but the refrain's own construction is now stated accurately rather than assimilated to 18:1's. 19:1 reads וַיְהִי֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם וּמֶ֖לֶךְ אֵ֣ין בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל - a wayehi-prefixed clause with the constituents inverted (וּמֶלֶךְ אֵין rather than אֵין מֶלֶךְ), continuing after the athnach into a second, parallel וַיְהִי clause (וַיְהִ֣י אִ֣ישׁ לֵוִ֗י גָּ֚ר) rather than fusing with the new subject in one sentence. This is a third distinct realization of the short-form refrain, differing from both 18:1 (which achieves its cohesion by repeating the bare temporal adverbial, בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם / וּבַיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם, with no wayehi and no inversion) and from the plain form at 17:6/21:25. The binding argument therefore differs verse by verse and must be stated for each: 18:1 binds by adverbial repetition, 19:1 binds by a parallel wayehi construction with inverted word order. Narrates the concubine's infidelity and departure, and the Levite's pursuit. Closes with the father's joyful welcome (v3), whose closing verb (וְלֹֽא)-object (לְהָשִׁיבָ֔הּ 'to bring her back') follows the qere against a ketiv reading להשיבו, now disclosed rather than silently adopted. v4 opens the father-in-law's extended hospitality, a new phase - a mild reset (participant respecified with a new kinship term one verse after his first appearance) rather than a strong formulaic marker.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged in conclusion: treating the refrain clause as its own micro-decision, mirroring 18:1, was considered and rejected - but not, as previously stated, 'for the identical reason given there,' since 18:1 and 19:1 are not built the same way. The refrain principle is restated in functional terms: the two-clause full form (17:6, 21:25) comments and closes; the one-clause short form heads a new complex, realized differently at its two outings (adverbial repetition at 18:1, an inverted-order wayehi clause at 19:1).

Closes correctly at v9, but now on its actual content and citation: 19:9 is the father-in-law's further plea to stay the night (הִנֵּ֣ה נָא֩ רָפָ֨ה הַיּ֜וֹם לַעֲרֹ֗ב...לִ֥ין פֹּה֙), refused by the Levite at 19:10 (וְלֹֽא אָבָ֤ה הָאִישׁ֙ לָל֔וּן) - a tight plea-and-refusal hinge, tighter than the misattributed citation it replaces. v10 opens the actual departure.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged in conclusion: splitting this into day-by-day decisions was considered and rejected, because each day's invitation is not content-differentiated in the way the minor-judges register's entries are, but forms a graded, cumulative delay sequence that stays whole per the register-closure criterion applied to prose.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the abrupt violent intrusion (v22), a scene deliberately echoing Genesis 19's Sodom narrative, and narrates the host's offer of the women instead, the mob's refusal to listen, and the assault. v25's grammatical subject is corrected a second time here: הָאִישׁ ('the man') is not disambiguated by the noun alone - the same designation is used for the guest (the Levite) at 19:7 and 19:9 and for the householder at 19:22-19:23, so 'the man' who seizes and puts out the concubine in v25 could, on the bare noun, be either. The possessive suffix on the object phrase, בְּפִילַגְשׁוֹ ('his concubine'), favors the Levite as the intended referent, since she is identified as his concubine throughout and the pronoun most naturally binds to the clause's own subject; but this is a lean, not a settled identification, and the row no longer states flatly that the host is 'the grammatical subject of both verbs.' What is secure regardless of which man performs the act is that she is the object throughout, not the agent of her own surrender. Closes with her collapse at the threshold 'until it was light' (v26), the atrocity's aftermath visible before the Levite wakes. v27 opens his discovery the next morning. Neither edge of this span carries admissible external evidence: WEB runs 19:21 together with 19:22 and 19:26 together with 19:27, opening paragraphs instead at 19:23 and 19:25 - disclosed as non-driving metadata under m8-mesh-r2, and in any case interior to the span rather than at either of its own edges - and this chapter carries no parashah mark before the petuchah after 19:30. With the internal escalating-scene argument as the only ground actually carrying the span, and no admissible witness at either edge, confidence is repriced from high to medium.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged: splitting the demand-and-negotiation (22-24) from the assault itself (25-26) was considered and rejected; both halves form one uninterrupted escalating scene of violence with no participant or location change.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse inquiry scene at Bethel: 'Who shall go up for us first to battle against the children of Benjamin?' This decision discloses a deliberate resumptive echo of the book's opening inquiry formula at 1:1-2, now stated precisely rather than overstated. The verbatim recurrence lives in the question-formula (מִ֚י יַעֲלֶה לָּ֣נוּ...בַתְּחִלָּ֔ה, near-identical to 1:1's מִ֣י יַעֲלֶה לָּ֧נוּ...בַּתְּחִלָּ֖ה), not in the answer: 1:2 gives יְהוּדָ֣ה יַעֲלֶ֑ה plus an attached land-grant clause, while 20:18 gives the shorter יְהוּדָ֥ה בַתְּחִלָּֽה, migrating the adverb בַתְּחִלָּה from the question into the answer rather than repeating 1:2's verb יַעֲלֶה. The two answers share only the named tribe and the shared opener וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יְהוּדָ֣ה. The civil war against a fellow Israelite tribe is still framed by a deliberate reuse of the conquest-opening oracle formula - an ironic structural signal - but the frame is a resumptive echo of the question, not a verbatim doubling of the whole exchange. Opens on the shift from troop-counting to cultic inquiry; closes before v19's fresh muster-and-encampment notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged: merging this oracle into the troop-muster unit (159) as its natural sequel was considered and rejected; the oracle is a discrete cultic act formally distinct from the numerical muster-register just completed, and its near-verbatim echo of 1:1's question-formula merits isolation as its own decision.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the ambush's assault on the city (35-38) from Benjamin's dawning realization (39-41) was considered; rejected because both halves are deliberately interwoven by the narrator, describing the ambushers' actions and Benjamin's simultaneous, unaware continued fighting, as one synchronized dramatic sequence building to the shared moment of recognition.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Benjamin's flight 'before the men of Israel to the way of the wilderness' (v42), a shift from realization to physical retreat, and narrates the relentless pursuit with successive, layered casualty figures. The clause opening v45 (וַיִּפְנ֞וּ וַיָּנֻ֤סוּ הַמִּדְבָּ֨רָה֙ אֶל סֶ֣לַע הָֽרִמּ֔וֹן) recurs byte-identical at v47 - Wiederaufnahme in its purest form in this range - with v46's summary casualty tally (אֶֽת כָּל אֵ֖לֶּה אַנְשֵׁי חָֽיִל, twenty-five thousand who drew the sword) sitting inside the bracket the repetition forms rather than at a genuine boundary. The unit now runs through the survivors' flight to the rock of Rimmon and the four-month refuge there (v47), and the war's final act of destruction, the remaining Benjaminite towns burned (v48). Closes at the petuchah after v48, confirmed present in both witnesses, where the war itself ends. Ch21:1 opens a new temporal-thematic register, beginning the resolution.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged in its own terms, now subsuming the alternative previously argued at 167: extending this unit through v48 was previously rejected on the ground that v46's tally is a complete rhetorical closure and v47 opens a distinguishable coda about the surviving remnant. That rejection is withdrawn: v47 is not a fresh narrowing-focus onset but the second half of the verbatim resumptive pair whose first half sits at v45, inside this unit, so no boundary can be drawn between them. The unit closes instead at v48, at the petuchah, where the war narrative itself ends and ch21's resolution begins.

Closes with that lament (v3). v4 opens a new ritual action, altar-building, shifting from speech to cultic response.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The altar-building unit of 4-7 could be read together with this one as a single mourning-and-cultic-response span; v4's 'On the next day, the people rose early and built an altar' marks a fresh temporal, action-based beat apart from the lament-speech of 1-3.

boundary_rationale: The seam is moved rather than the two decisions merged. This decision now covers only the cultic response: 'On the next day, the people rose early and built an altar there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings' (וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ הָעָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ שָׁ֖ם מִזְבֵּ֑חַ), a self-contained ritual beat opened by an unambiguous next-day temporal marker and closed by the offerings themselves, corroborated by a petuchah confirmed present after Judg.21.4 in both witnesses. The practical crisis and its restated deliberation - previously folded into this span through v7 - move to M8-Judg-170, which now opens at v5 and carries its own legal warrant (the מוֹת יוּמָת penalty clause) inside its own boundary rather than borrowed from across a seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two arrangements were weighed. (a) Merging 169 and 170 outright into one Judg.21.4-Judg.21.12 span was considered, since the altar-building and the enquiry that follows it are causally continuous. (b) Re-closing 169 at v4 alone and opening 170 at v5 was preferred instead: it resolves the internal inconsistency (170's own causal argument no longer depends on a clause quarantined in the neighboring decision) without collapsing two distinguishable beats - a discrete ritual act (altar and offerings) versus a discrete investigative-and-punitive sequence (the restated question through the raid's completion) - into one. The fixed record can carry the seam once it sits at v4/v5 instead of v7/v8, so the merge is not required.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Judg.21.4 וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ הָעָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ שָׁ֖ם מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיַּעֲל֥וּ עֹל֖וֹת וּשְׁלָמִֽים
parashah_two_witness: pe after Judg.21.4 (weak corroboration, Prophets - aligns with this span's own close, now that the span ends at v4)

boundary_rationale: Opens with the investigative question restated in full, now including its own legal basis: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ֠י אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא עָלָ֧ה בַקָּהָ֛ל מִכָּל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל יְהוָ֑ה (v5), which carries the מוֹת יוּמָת death-penalty clause the raid on Jabesh Gilead depends on - previously cited as this decision's warrant while sitting, inconsistently, inside the neighboring span. The question is put again in near-identical wording at v8 (מִ֗י אֶחָד֙ מִשִּׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא עָלָ֥ה אֶל יְהוָ֖ה הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה) once the specific absent tribe is identified - a lexical and thematic resumption of the question first posed at v5, restating rather than initiating the inquiry. The punitive expedition follows directly: twelve thousand men sent to destroy Jabesh Gilead except its unmarried women (the survivors are what the command at v11 leaves over, not an exception written into the order itself). Closes with the delivery of four hundred young women to the camp at Shiloh (v12), corroborated by a setumah confirmed present in both witnesses. v13 opens a new diplomatic act, the peace overture to Benjamin at Rimmon.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the census-discovery (5-9) from the raid's execution and result (10-12) was considered and rejected, as before; both halves form one uninterrupted cause-and-consequence sequence with no scene-break. The alternative newly resolved here is the opening edge itself: opening at v8 (as originally drafted) was tested and rejected, because v8 restates rather than initiates the question already posed at v5, and this decision's own reasoning about the Mizpah oath's penalty clause requires v5 to be read as part of the same unit that acts on it.

literature_type_guess: elders' deliberation on the oath problem
boundary_rationale: Opens with the elders of the congregation reopening the question, זִקְנֵ֣י הָעֵדָ֔ה named as speakers for the only time in the book - a genuine reset after the narrator's summary at v15. Closes with their restatement of the legal constraint in curse-formula language: אָר֕וּר נֹתֵ֥ן אִשָּׁ֖ה לְבִנְיָמִֽן (v18) restates the substance of the oath first given at v1 (אִ֣ישׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לֹא יִתֵּ֥ן בִּתּ֛וֹ לְבִנְיָמִ֖ן לְאִשָּֽׁה) but is not a verbatim quotation of it - different verb, different construction, a curse-formula recasting. The root ARR occurs elsewhere in the book only at 5:23, in a different grammatical form (imperative plus infinitive absolute, an intensifying 'utterly curse'), so 21:18's predicate participle usage is precisely, not loosely, its own. The close does not rest on a 'new speaker' at v19: 21:19 opens וַיֹּאמְר֡וּ with no expressed subject, continuing the elders introduced at v16 by inflection exactly as v17 does. The actual shift at v19 is one of content - the constraint-restatement giving way to a proposed way around it - and that content shift, together with a setumah confirmed present after 21:18 in both witnesses (weak, non-driving Prophets corroboration), is the edge's real basis.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged: merging this deliberation with the Jabesh Gilead solution (170) was considered and rejected; vv16-18 explicitly reopens the still-unresolved shortage after that solution proved insufficient, a new deliberative cycle rather than a continuation of the earlier resolved action.

boundary_rationale: Unchanged in substance. Opens with the proposed solution, 'Behold, there is a feast of Yahweh from year to year in Shiloh,' a concrete plan with detailed topographic description, and narrates the instructions for the Shiloh dance-abduction, including the legal-loophole rationale. Closes with the plan's successful execution and the Benjaminites' return to rebuild (v23), since v23's compliance formula (וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן) cannot itself head a unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged in conclusion, now with the fuller counter-signal picture disclosed: splitting the instructions (19-22) from their execution (v23) was considered and rejected by analogy to command-and-compliance sequences elsewhere in the book (Gideon's altar-destruction at 6:25-27, independently re-verified: no parashah mark interrupts that sequence either). Both available witnesses converge on that same 22|23 seam rather than one: a samekh falls after Judg.21.22, and WEB opens a paragraph at 21:23 as well - disclosed here together as weak, non-driving corroboration for the rejected alternative, consistent with how comparable marks are disclosed at 139, 147, 154, 159 and 166 in this range. Against that convergence stands the compliance formula itself, which cannot head a unit, and the fact that this span's own adopted close (v23) carries no external mark of any kind - WEB runs no break at 21:24, and this chapter's parashah marks are the petuchah after 21:4 and setumot after 21:12, 21:18 and 21:22, none of them at the 21:23|21:24 seam. The plan-execution unity reading is retained on the compliance-formula ground alone, against this disclosed and now fuller counter-case, not because the counter-case is weak.

literature_type_guess: dispersal notice and closing refrain (book-ending inclusio)
boundary_rationale: Opens with the general Israelite dispersal (v24), a wider closing notice bringing the civil-war-and-resolution narrative to a peaceful end - a genuine explicit-subject reset from the Benjaminite subject of 21:23 (בְּנֵי בִנְיָמִן) to the Israelite subject of 21:24 (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), the criterion this campaign treats as decisive at this unit's opening edge exactly as it does elsewhere (e.g. M8-Judg-001, M8-Judg-061). No external mark corroborates that edge - WEB's own paragraph break falls at 21:23, inside the preceding decision, and runs unbroken through 21:24-25, and this chapter's parashah marks (pe after 21:4; samekh after 21:12, 21:18, 21:22) fall short of it - but the reset itself is a text-internal signal, not metadata, and stands as this edge's driver on its own terms. Closes with the book's final verse, the full-form refrain repeated verbatim from 17:6 - confirmed byte-identical under NFC, cantillation included, so the inclusio claim here is exact rather than approximate - and that inclusio is this closing edge's own driver: unlike a successor-contrast signal, it does not require anything to follow, since it corroborates the unit's terminus by bracketing back to 17:6 rather than by distinguishing this unit from what comes next. That is the operative difference from M8-Judg-001's opening edge, whose own inclusio (with 20:18) likewise cannot resolve it, but for the opposite reason: 1:1 is the book's first verse, and a live boundary question stands open behind it (Joshua's narrative continues there), which no backward-looking bracket internal to Judges can settle. Nothing follows 21:25 at all, so no comparable live question remains open on this side; the closing question is fixed by the physical end of the text, and the inclusio is the affirmative signal that this ending is the deliberate, marked counterpart of 17:6 rather than an arbitrary stopping point. With a stated driver at each of its own two edges - the explicit-subject reset at 23/24 and the inclusio at the close - this decision's HIGH grade holds on text-internal grounds. This decision also notes the decision's structural echo of 20:18's frame with 1:1-2; that secondary reference now carries the correction made at M8-Judg-160: the 1:1-2/20:18 pairing is a deliberate resumptive echo concentrated in the question-formula (מִי יַעֲלֶה לָּנוּ...בַּתְּחִלָּה) and the shared opener, not a pair of verbally identical answers as previously overstated. The 17:6/21:25 pairing itself, and this decision's own span, confidence, and primary evidence, are untouched by that correction.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged: isolating v25 as its own single-verse decision, separate from the dispersal notice of v24, was considered and rejected; v24 and v25 are both narrator's-voice closing commentary with nothing between them - no speech frame, no participant change, no temporal reset at the 24/25 line.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the formulaic וַיְהִי בִּימֵי שְׁפֹט הַשֹּׁפְטִים time-notice that regularly launches a fresh narrative frame; the unit narrates one continuous causal chain (famine forces emigration, husband dies, sons marry and then also die) without a scene-relocation or new speaker interrupting the narrator's voice. Verse 2's own disjunctive, verbless naming clause (וְשֵׁ֣ם הָאִ֣ישׁ אֱֽלִימֶ֡לֶךְ) does not register as an independent seam of the kind found at 2:1 or 4:7: it names participants already inventoried in v1's household roster (ה֥וּא וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֥י בָנָֽיו), functioning as an appositive supplying detail within this single already-bounded exposition unit rather than introducing a participant genuinely new to the story ahead of a scene of his own — the test that lets 2:1 earn its own, weaker seam in decision 005 — and it carries none of the temporal deictic that places 4:7's aside outside story-time altogether in decision 015. It closes on וַתִּשָּׁאֵר הָאִשָּׁה מִשְּׁנֵי יְלָדֶיהָ וּמֵאִישָׁהּ, a bereavement formula that mirrors and inverts the household inventory given in v1 — the same husband/wife/two-sons triad now stripped to the widow alone, closing the exposition's arithmetic. The next verse pivots on a new subject-led movement verb (וַתָּקָם הִיא וְכַלֹּתֶיהָ), introducing the daughters-in-law as active participants for the first time and initiating the return journey the exposition never narrates.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through v7 (to include the notice that Naomi heard the famine had ended and set out) was considered, since v6's פָקַ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת עַמּ֔וֹ לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לָֽחֶם answers the רָעָב of v1 and could be read as the exposition's true resolution. Rejected because vv.6-7 introduce a new grammatical subject-cluster (Naomi with 'her daughters-in-law,' a phrase absent from vv.1-5) and a new narrative goal (the road back to Judah) that belongs with the dialogue it sets up rather than with the family's death-notices.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the new movement verb noted above (וַתָּקָם...וַתָּשָׁב) and stays grammatically plural-addressed throughout: Naomi's two speeches in this span (v8's לֵ֣כְנָה שֹּׁ֔בְנָה and v11-12's שֹׁ֤בְנָה בְנֹתַי / לֵ֔כְןָ) both use feminine-plural imperatives directed at BOTH daughters-in-law together, and the weeping that answers each speech is explicitly doubled — v14's וַתִּשֶּׂ֣נָה קוֹלָ֔ן וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ינָה ע֑וֹד uses עוֹד to hook back to the identical phrase in v9, marking the two weeping episodes as one resumed emotional beat rather than two separate scenes. Both v8 and v11 open with the same named-speaker formula, וַתֹּ֤אמֶר נָעֳמִי֙, which on its face looks like it could reset the unit twice; it does not, because a repeated named-speaker formula functions as a turn marker rather than a scene-reset throughout this dialogue-dense book — the clearest proof is Ruth 2:20 (decision 010), which carries the identical formula twice inside one unbroken exchange with no addressee change. Applying that same principle here, neither v8 nor v11 carries the second signal (relocation, addressee change, elapsed time) that a genuine seam requires, so the real binding device remains the עוֹד-Wiederaufnahme at v14, not the repeated speech-tags. The span ends the moment the audience narrows: v14b singles out Orpah's kiss and departure against וְר֖וּת דָּ֥בְקָה בָּֽהּ ('but Ruth clung to her'), and every verb of address from v15 on shifts to feminine-singular forms aimed at Ruth alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating vv.8-10, 11-13, and 14 as three separate decisions (one per Naomi speech-turn) was considered, since each speech is introduced by an explicit-subject וַתֹּאמֶר נָעֳמִי. Rejected because a repeated named-speaker formula is a turn marker in this book, not a unit-opener by itself — reading every such formula as a reset would fragment this and other dialogues into unwarranted single-turn pieces, exactly the mistake decision 010 avoids when it declines to cut Ruth 2:20's doubled וַתֹּאמֶר נָעֳמִי formula into two units — and because the doubled weeping refrain (עוֹד at v14 recalling v9) functions as the actual resumptive device binding the two speech-rounds into a single scene, with no relocation, new addressee, or elapsed time separating the speeches beyond the refusal-and-repeat rhythm of one ongoing roadside appeal.

boundary_rationale: This span opens with the address narrowing to Ruth alone (שׁ֖וּבִי, a feminine-singular imperative, against the plural imperatives of the preceding unit), Naomi's final, brief appeal pointing to Orpah's example. Ruth's reply (וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רוּת, an explicit-subject speech-formula naming her for the first time as the sole respondent) is the celebrated parallelistic pledge of vv.16-17, and the unit is closed off by the narrator's summary verdict in v18: וַתֵּ֕רֶא כִּֽי מִתְאַמֶּ֥צֶת הִ֖יא לָלֶ֣כֶת אִתָּ֑הּ וַתֶּחְדַּ֖ל לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶֽיהָ ('she stopped speaking to her') — a discourse-ending tag with no further quoted words, distinct in kind from the resumed-journey narration that opens the next span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating vv.16-17 (the oath itself) as a standalone decision was considered, given its distinct poetic cadence and its frequent treatment as a self-contained set-piece in commentary. Rejected because it carries no independent scene-marker of its own — no time notice, no relocation, no new addressee — and is introduced by the same ordinary narrative speech-frame used throughout this conversation; its poetic register is a function of content and rhetorical intensity, not of a textual seam, so lifting it out would sever it from the appeal (v15) it directly answers and the narrator's verdict (v18) it provokes.

boundary_rationale: The span begins with a fresh dual-subject movement verb, וַתֵּלַ֣כְנָה שְׁתֵּיהֶ֔ם ('the two of them went'), resuming the journey after the roadside dialogue closed and carrying it to its destination; the arrival is stated twice in close succession (עַד בֹּאָנָה בֵּית לָחֶם / כְּבֹאָנָה בֵּית לֶחֶם), a doubling that frames the 'is this Naomi?' commotion and the Mara speech it triggers. The span closes with v22's own restatement of the same arrival-notice — וְהֵ֗מָּה בָּ֚אוּ בֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם — a resumptive echo of v19 that folds the embedded Mara dialogue inside a repeated-arrival frame, and appends the harvest timestamp the next chapter's field scene depends on.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the unit at v19/20 (separating the townswomen's arrival-notice from the Mara speech proper) was considered, since v20 opens with a fresh וַתֹּאמֶר. Rejected because the 'is this Naomi?' question (v19b) has no self-contained content apart from setting up Naomi's answer, and because the resumptive arrival-notice at v22 only makes sense as the closing counterpart to v19's arrival-notice — separating them would strand the frame's second half from its first.

web:Ruth.1.22 They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

boundary_rationale: This single verse is built as a disjunctive, verbless circumstantial clause — וּֽלְנָעֳמִ֞י מוֹדַ֣ע לְאִישָׁ֗הּ ('and-to-Naomi [there was] a kinsman') fronts the prepositional phrase ahead of any finite verb, taking the narration off the wayyiqtol storyline to supply background the reader needs before the action resumes. The following verse returns to ordinary narrative sequence with an explicit-subject wayyiqtol, וַתֹּאמֶר֩ ר֨וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֜ה, restarting the plot. Disjunctive verbless syntax by itself is necessary but not sufficient to register its own seam in this book: the differentiating test is whether the clause introduces a participant genuinely new to the story ahead of that participant's own scene, and whether it further carries a temporal deictic placing the narrator outside story-time. Ruth 1:2 (וְשֵׁ֣ם הָאִ֣ישׁ אֱֽלִימֶ֡לֶךְ), the same construction type, fails the first test — it merely names participants already inventoried in 1:1's household roster and is rightly absorbed into decision 001 with no separate seam. Ruth 4:7 (וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל) passes both tests, since לְפָנִים adds a signal this verse lacks, which is why 4:7 is priced at high in decision 015 while this verse is not. This verse passes only the first test: Boaz is wholly new to the story and his introduction runs well ahead of his actual entrance at 2:4, earning a real but comparatively modest seam. The seam is genuine but the span itself is a single informational clause satisfying only one of the two tests, so confidence is priced down accordingly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into vv.2-3 as the opening of one 'setup' unit was considered, since nothing happens narratively in v1 by itself. Rejected because the verse passes the new-participant test stated above, sharing its verbless, no-finite-verb shape with 4:7's aside (וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל) — though 4:1's וּבֹ֨עַז עָלָ֣ה הַשַּׁעַר֮ is a related but distinct subject-fronted qatal clause with a finite verb, not a true syntactic parallel to this verse or to 4:7 — and because its content, establishing Boaz's status and lineage before Ruth 'happens' into his field, sets up dramatic irony that depends on being logically prior to, not fused with, Ruth's own initiative in v2.

boundary_rationale: The span opens with Ruth's own initiative, an explicit-subject speech-formula requesting permission to glean, and Naomi's terse consent (לְכִ֥י בִתִּֽי), then narrates her going out and the 'chance' that lands her in Boaz's field — closing on the loaded notice וַיִּ֣קֶר מִקְרֶ֔הָ חֶלְקַ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ לְבֹ֔עַז, naming the very field the reader was primed for in v1. The next verse opens with וְהִנֵּה בֹ֗עַז בָּ֚א, a הִנֵּה-marked entrance that shifts the narrative's viewpoint to track Boaz's arrival on scene, a distinct visual/participant cue absent from this span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this span forward into vv.4-7 (treating 'Ruth goes to the field' through 'Boaz identifies her' as one continuous field-arrival unit) was considered. Rejected because v3's 'chance' notice is a self-contained narratorial punchline that pays off v1's introduction of Boaz, and the הִנֵּה of v4 marks a genuine viewpoint shift onto a new participant entering the scene, which is a stronger seam than anything internal to vv.2-3.

boundary_rationale: Both edges of this span are independently marked. It opens on the הִנֵּה-fronted entrance already noted, introducing Boaz onto the scene and his greeting-exchange with the reapers (יְהוָ֣ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם / יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָֽה), then moves to his question about Ruth's identity addressed to his servant and the servant's answering report. It closes exactly where the addressee changes: v8 opens וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶל ר֜וּת, the first time in the chapter Boaz speaks directly TO Ruth rather than ABOUT her in the third person to an intermediary — a clean, checkable shift in who is being addressed.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v4 (the reaper-greeting) from vv.5-7 (the servant-inquiry) was considered, since they are formally distinct exchanges with different interlocutors. Rejected because both exchanges share the same participants on scene, the same location, and no time elapses between them — the greeting establishes Boaz's character immediately before the inquiry that turns his attention toward Ruth, and dividing a four-verse span into two two-verse fragments over an internal addressee change (reapers vs. servant) would be finer-grained than the addressee change that closes the whole span (about Ruth vs. to Ruth).

web:Ruth.2.4 May Yahweh be with you... May Yahweh bless you.
web:Ruth.2.8 Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen, my daughter."

boundary_rationale: This span is anchored by the recurring favor-word (חן) figure, but the figure is a three-member chain beginning at 2:2 (אֶמְצָא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֑יו, Ruth's request to Naomi, outside this span and inside decision 006) and continuing within this span at 2:10 (מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙, Ruth's question to Boaz) and 2:13 (אֶמְצָא חֵ֨ן בְּעֵינֶ֤יךָ אֲדֹנִי֙, her closing line to him) — a span-internal echo running 2:10-to-2:13, starting two verses inside the opening edge, not a bracket enclosing the whole 2:8-13 unit. The opening edge of this span is independently carried by Boaz's direct address to Ruth noted in decision 007 (וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶל ר֜וּת). The closing edge is softer than a bracket-reading implies: 2:14's לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל is post-verbal (וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לָ֨ה בֹ֜עַז לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל) rather than clause-initial, and the speaker-addressee pair (Boaz to Ruth) is unchanged from v13. The stronger, span-internal candidate for a closing signal sits one verse later, at 2:15's וַיְצַו֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶת נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר, which pairs a named subject with a genuinely new addressee (the young men, not Ruth) — the same signal pair decision 007 treats as seam-grade at 2:7/2:8. The span itself still stands, opened cleanly at 2:8 and closed reasonably at the mealtime pivot of 2:14, but only one edge (the opening) carries full seam-grade signal strength; the closing edge rests on a weaker, non-clause-initial temporal marker rather than on the חן figure, which is internal to the span rather than bracketing it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating Boaz's instructions (vv.8-9) from the favor-exchange proper (vv.10-13) was considered, since v8-9 is imperative/instructional in mood while v10-13 is question-and-blessing. Rejected because Ruth's question in v10 is a direct response to the instructions just given, and the 2:10-to-2:13 חן echo — not a full bracket, since its first member sits at 2:2 — still binds v10 to v13 as one exchange internal to this span. A second alternative, ending the span at 2:13 rather than 2:14, was also weighed against extending it through 2:15, since 2:15's named-subject-plus-new-addressee pairing (וַיְצַו֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶת נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר) is formally a stronger signal than 2:14's post-verbal mealtime notice. Rejected in favor of the 2:13/14 cut because 2:14 already introduces a genuinely fresh topic (provision/food) absent from the favor-exchange, even though its own marking is comparatively soft — a softness now reflected in the span's confidence rather than papered over by an inclusio claim the text does not fully support.

boundary_rationale: The span opens on a fresh temporal marker, לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל ('at mealtime'), pivoting the scene from the favor-dialogue to provision — the shared meal, then Boaz's supplementary instructions to the young men to deliberately leave extra grain for her. It closes on a quantified summary, וַיְהִ֖י כְּאֵיפָ֥ה שְׂעֹרִֽים ('it was about an ephah of barley'), a tally that answers the implicit question of a gleaning narrative before v18 pivots to a new movement verb and location (וַתִּשָּׂא֙ וַתָּב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר, 'she took it up and went into the city').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating vv.15-16 (Boaz's renewed instructions to the young men) as a separate decision from v14 (the meal) was considered, since they address different listeners (Ruth vs. the reapers). Rejected because both beats serve the same narrative function — Boaz quietly ensuring Ruth's provision exceeds what her own labor would secure — and neither carries an independent time, place, or participant marker strong enough to divide them; the ephah-tally at v17 is the first real closural device after v14, and it closes both beats together.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Ruth.2.14 At meal time Boaz said to her, "Come here, and eat some bread"
web:Ruth.2.17 it was about an ephah of barley.

boundary_rationale: The span begins with Ruth's return to the city and to Naomi (a location/participant shift from the field), moves through Naomi's questioning, the naming of Boaz, and Naomi's recognition of him as a גֹּאֵל ('redeemer') — the first appearance in the book of the legal term that will drive the rest of the plot — and closes on a chapter-length time-summary, עַד כְּל֥וֹת קְצִ֣יר הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים וּקְצִ֣יר הַֽחִטִּ֑ים ('until the end of barley harvest and wheat harvest'), which compresses the remainder of the season before ch.3 opens on Naomi's new initiative. The v20 recognition is anchored inside this span rather than split off, by a principle this book applies consistently: a named-speaker formula functions here as a turn marker within a running exchange, not as a scene-reset in its own right. Verse 20 itself supplies the clearest proof — it carries the identical formula וַתֹּאמֶר נָעֳמִי twice (וַתֹּ֨אמֶר נָעֳמִ֜י לְכַלָּתָ֗הּ ... וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ נָעֳמִ֗י) inside one uninterrupted conversation with no addressee change, the same pattern this book uses at 1:8 and 1:11 within a single appeal-and-refusal scene (decision 002). Reading every repeated speech-tag as an opener would fragment this dialogue into unwarranted two-verse pieces; the actual seams bounding this span are the location shift at v18 and the season-summary at v23.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off v20 (Naomi's גֹּאֵל recognition) as its own decision was considered, given its outsized thematic weight for the plot. Rejected because it is syntactically just the continuation of the same question-and-answer report Ruth and Naomi are having — no new speech-frame introduces a scene break, the repeated וַתֹּאמֶר נָעֳמִי formula within v20 itself functions as a turn marker rather than a reset (the same principle applied at 1:8/1:11 in decision 002), and the conversation carries on without interruption through v22 — so isolating a single thematically important clause from its surrounding dialogue would privilege content-importance over an actual textual seam, which the binding rules for this book do not permit.

oshb:Ruth.2.23 עַד כְּל֥וֹת קְצִֽיר הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים וּקְצִ֣יר הַֽחִטִּ֑ים

boundary_rationale: This span opens the chapter with Naomi's explicit-subject speech-formula, וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ נָעֳמִ֣י חֲמוֹתָ֑הּ, and her proposal to seek 'rest' (מָנ֖וֹחַ) for Ruth — a term that echoes, as a cognate nominal form of the same root נוח rather than the identical word, Naomi's own מְנוּחָ֔ה-wish for her daughters-in-law in 1:9, marking this as the start of a new initiative rather than a continuation of the previous chapter's harvest-summary. The unit is entirely instructional in content (wash, anoint, dress, go down, wait, note, uncover, lie down) and closes the moment Ruth gives her formulaic assent, כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמְרִ֥י אֵלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶֽׂה ('all that you say, I will do'), before the narration shifts to executed action.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through v6 (to include 'she went down and did as her mother-in-law commanded') was considered, since v6 could read as simply completing Naomi's sentence. Rejected because v6 is a narrator's compressed EXECUTION notice, using indirect summary (כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוַּ֖תָּה חֲמוֹתָֽהּ) rather than repeating the instructions verbatim, which is the book's regular device for marking the transition from planning-speech to enacted narrative — the true parallel is 2:2's request (אֵֽלְכָה נָּ֤א הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וַאֲלַקֳטָּ֣ה בַשִׁבֳּלִ֔ים) answered by 2:3's own compressed summary (וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ וַתָּבוֹא֙ וַתְּלַקֵּ֣ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה), not the instruction/fulfillment pattern later in this same chapter at 3:13/3:14. That later pair is in fact the opposite pattern — a near-verbatim repetition (שִׁכְבִ֖י עַד הַבֹּֽקֶר answered by וַתִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מַרְגְּלוֹתָיוֹ֙ עַד הַבֹּ֔קֶר) that this record's own decision 012 correctly treats as a continuity-binding echo rather than a compression device, and so is a counterexample to, not a parallel for, the compressed-summary claim made here.

boundary_rationale: This span covers one unbroken stretch of time and place — the threshing floor from nightfall to just before dawn — opened by the compressed execution notice discussed above and closed only when Boaz physically leaves the scene, וַיָּבֹ֖א הָעִֽיר ('he went into the city,' v15b), a location-change verb ending the encounter. Internally the span contains a temporal marker, עַד הַבֹּקֶר ('until morning'), used both in Boaz's instruction at v13 and in the narration of its fulfillment at v14 — a verbal echo this campaign's precedent treats as evidence of continuity binding the material together, not as grounds for a further split between the midnight dialogue and the pre-dawn departure. The span's strongest internal rival, the seam at 3:7/3:8, is engaged and refused below rather than left untested.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Dividing this span at 3:7/3:8 was considered and is the genuinely strongest rival, not the 13/14 division. Verse 8 stacks two device types this record treats as seam-grade elsewhere into a single verse: a fronted temporal clause, וַיְהִי֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֔יְלָה ('and it happened at midnight'), the only construction of its kind in the book apart from 1:1 and the arrival-frame inside 1:19, immediately followed by a presentative clause, וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִשָּׁ֔ה שֹׁכֶ֖בֶת מַרְגְּלֹתָֽיו ('and behold, a woman lying at his feet'), the same הִנֵּה-device treated as seam-grade at 2:4 (decision 007) and 4:1 (decision 014). Refused on the following ground: the presentative at 3:8 reports Boaz's startled perception of a person already on stage — Ruth arrived and lay down at his feet in 3:7 (וַתָּבֹ֣א בַלָּ֔ט וַתְּגַ֥ל מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו וַתִּשְׁכָּֽב), one verse earlier within this same span — whereas the הִנֵּה-presentatives at 2:4 and 4:1 walk a genuinely fresh participant onto an empty stage from outside it. The midnight notice similarly times a moment inside an already-running encounter rather than opening a new frame. A secondary division at 3:13/3:14 (separating the midnight dialogue from the dawn rising and the gift of barley) was also weighed, precisely because of the 'until morning' repetition and the shift from dialogue to narration it introduces, and is rejected on the same continuity ground: the repetition is a resumptive device signaling fulfillment of an instruction just given, not a scene break, so treating either internal repetition as a split point would mistake a continuity or perception marker for a boundary marker.

boundary_rationale: The span opens with a location/participant shift back to Naomi (וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל חֲמוֹתָ֔הּ), whose opening question, מִ֣י אַ֣תְּ בִּתִּ֑י ('who are you, my daughter'), deliberately echoes Boaz's own מִי אָ֑תּ at the midnight encounter (v9), framing this closing report as a structural counterpart to the night scene it recounts. It closes the chapter on Naomi's forward-looking counsel, כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשְׁקֹט֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ כִּֽי אִם כִּלָּ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַיּֽוֹם ('the man will not rest until he has settled this today'), a statement whose fulfillment is precisely what ch.4 opens by narrating.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this span backward into the threshing-floor unit (treating the whole of 3:6-18 as one report-inclusive scene) was considered, since Ruth's report recounts events already narrated to the reader. Rejected because a genuine location and participant shift occurs at v16 — the scene physically returns to Naomi's household — and because Naomi's closing counsel is addressed to the reader's anticipation of ch.4 rather than to anything within the threshing-floor encounter itself, making it a distinct unit rather than a coda glued onto the night scene.

boundary_rationale: The chapter opens with a subject-fronted clause, וּבֹ֨עַז עָלָ֣ה הַשַּׁעַר֮ ('and Boaz went up to the gate'), the verb placed after its subject rather than in the ordinary wayyiqtol-initial slot — a scene-launching construction paired with a wholly new location (the town gate) and, moments later, another הִנֵּה-marked entrance for the near-kinsman, echoing the device used to introduce Boaz himself in 2:4. The span covers the entire legal setup and land-redemption negotiation, closing on the kinsman's cession, גְּאַל לְךָ֤ אַתָּה֙ אֶת גְּאֻלָּתִ֔י ('redeem for yourself my right of redemption'), immediately before the narrator interrupts the scene with an explanatory aside.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the convening of witnesses (vv.1-2) from the negotiation proper (vv.3-6) was considered, since the content shifts from assembling participants to conducting business. Rejected because no textual marker separates them — the same wayyiqtol chain runs through both without a change of location, speaker set, or time, and the assembling of the ten elders in v2 is simply the necessary precondition the negotiation of vv.3-6 requires; dividing on topic alone, absent a text signal, would be exactly the kind of over-splitting this book's binding rules warn against.

boundary_rationale: This single verse is marked off by the same disjunctive syntax used at 2:1, opening with a fronted demonstrative rather than a wayyiqtol, וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל ('now this was formerly the custom in Israel'), and its temporal deictic לְפָנִים ('in former times') explicitly places the narrator's own vantage point AFTER and outside the story-time being narrated — the clearest signal in the book of the narrator addressing the reader directly rather than reporting character speech or action. Bare disjunctive, verbless syntax alone is not sufficient to earn its own seam in this book: compare 1:2 in decision 001, absorbed with no separate seam because it only names participants already inventoried in v1's roster. What earns a seam is passing at least one of two further tests — introducing a participant genuinely new to the story ahead of that participant's own scene (which is what earns 2:1 its own, weaker seam in decision 005), or carrying a temporal deictic of this kind. This verse passes the second test, independently of introducing any new participant at all, which is why it is priced three steps above 2:1 rather than merely one. The very next verse resumes ordinary narrative sequence with an explicit-subject wayyiqtol, וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַגֹּאֵ֛ל, and the kinsman enacts, in real time, the sandal-custom the aside just explained.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into v8 (treating the explanation and its enactment as one 'sandal custom' unit) was considered, since v8 is effectively the aside's own illustration. Rejected because the disjunctive-clause marker is a discourse-level signal, not a content-level one — the same test applied at 2:1 — and the aside is grammatically and temporally addressed to the reader across the gap between narrated events and the narrator's present, which is a genuinely different mode of speech from the wayyiqtol-narrated enactment that follows it.

boundary_rationale: The span resumes with the kinsman's sandal removal (enacting the just-explained custom) and moves directly into Boaz's own formal proclamation. That proclamation is framed by the witness formula עֵדִים אַתֶּם הַיּוֹם as a true inclusio rather than a matched pair of end-tags: in 4:9 the formula stands speech-initial, at the sixth through eighth words of Boaz's declaration — וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז לַזְּקֵנִ֜ים וְכָל הָעָ֗ם עֵדִ֤ים אַתֶּם֙ הַיּ֔וֹם — immediately after he addresses the elders and all the people and directly before the causal כִּי that introduces the acquisition clause (כִּ֤י קָנִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֶֽאֱלִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְכִלְי֖וֹן וּמַחְל֑וֹן מִיַּ֖ד נָעֳמִֽי) — while in 4:10 the identical formula, עֵדִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם, stands speech-final, closing the verse and the whole declaration. The frame therefore opens at the head of v9 and closes at the tail of v10, bracketing both the land-purchase clause and the levirate-wife clause as one continuous legal statement — a genuine opening-and-closing inclusio, which is stronger evidence for treating the proclamation as a single unit than a pair of repeated end-tags would have been. It closes the instant a different, plural subject takes over the speaking role: v11 opens וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ כָּל הָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר בַּשַּׁ֛עַר וְהַזְּקֵנִ֖ים, the assembled crowd's own voice replacing Boaz's.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the sandal-transfer narrative (v8) from Boaz's proclamation (vv.9-10) was considered, since one is narrated action and the other is direct speech. Rejected because the sandal transfer is the physical enactment that Boaz's own opening words in v9 immediately refer back to (קָנִיתִי, 'I have bought/acquired,' presupposes the just-completed exchange of the sandal), so the two halves of this span depend on each other for their sense and share the same participants and setting without a break.

boundary_rationale: This short span is the assembly's antiphonal answer to Boaz's proclamation, opened by the explicit-subject reset just noted (the people and elders replacing Boaz as speaker) and linked to what precedes by the catchword עֵדִים ('witnesses') repeated from the close of v10 into the crowd's own first word — a hinge marking both continuity of topic and change of speaker. It closes on the Perez/Tamar blessing, itself a forward-pointing detail anticipating the toledot genealogy at the chapter's end, before v13's wayyiqtol narrates the blessing's fulfillment.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this span with vv.8-10 into one undivided 'gate ceremony' unit was considered, since the catchword linkage argues for close continuity rather than sharp division. Rejected, though with some hesitation reflected in the confidence rating, because the explicit change of speaking subject (from Boaz individually to the assembled people and elders collectively) is a real, checkable marker distinguishing proclamation from communal ratification, even though the two are thematically and lexically bound together by the shared witness-language.

literature_type_guess: narrative with embedded communal speech (birth and naming scene)
boundary_rationale: The span opens on a wayyiqtol fulfillment — וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֹּ֤עַז אֶת רוּת֙ וַתְּהִי ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה ('so Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife') — narrating, as accomplished fact, exactly what the assembly's jussive blessing in v12 had only wished for, a wish-then-fulfillment shift that marks a real seam. Within the span the neighbor-women speak twice (a blessing at vv.14-15 and a naming-formula at v17) around Naomi's own adoptive gesture (v16), but no relocation or elapsed time separates any of these beats, so they are kept together as one birth-and-naming scene. The span closes on the genealogical tag ה֥וּא אֲבִי יִשַׁ֖י אֲבִ֥י דָוִֽד ('he is the father of Jesse, the father of David'), immediately before the formal תּוֹלְדוֹת heading of v18 shifts the text into a different genre altogether.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the neighbor-women's two speeches (vv.14-15 and v17) as distinct decisions, with Naomi's nursing gesture (v16) forming a third, was considered, since each beat has its own explicit-subject introduction. Rejected because none of the three beats is marked off by any scene-level signal (no new location, no new time, no new participant set — the same women, Naomi, and the child remain constant throughout), and fragmenting a five-beat scene at every internal speech-turn would produce single-verse decisions with no independent textual warrant, unlike the aside at 4:7 or the character-introduction at 2:1, both of which carry a genuine disjunctive-clause marker that this material lacks.

boundary_rationale: This span opens with an unmistakable formal genre-marker, the תולדות-heading וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ תּוֹלְד֣וֹת פָּ֔רֶץ ('now these are the generations of Perez'), the same fixed formula used elsewhere in the canon to open a genealogical section — at Genesis 2:4, 25:19, and 37:2, for instance, the identical heading opens a section that goes on to narrate rather than merely list, so the formula itself marks a section boundary and does not by itself guarantee register-only content. What makes this span function as a register is internal to Ruth's own text: it proceeds as a uniform ten-member הוֹלִיד ('became the father of') chain with no narrative or dialogue content at all, closing the book on the name דָּוִֽד ('David') toward which the whole chain has been building. The book's single parashah mark (a pe, per the two-witness freeze file, with both OSHB and UXLC agreeing) falls after 4:17 — exactly at the seam between the narrative ending and this genealogical register — and is cited here as weak corroboration only, consistent with this book's near-total marker silence, never as a driver of the decision itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Subdividing the genealogy internally (for instance, separating the heading v18 from the chain, or breaking the ten links into smaller groups) was considered. Rejected under this book's list/register-function principle: a formulaic genealogical chain with no internal variation in form functions as a single unit by genre convention, and slicing it verse-by-verse would treat each 'begat' clause as if it carried independent narrative weight, which it does not — the register's function is cumulative and only complete at David's name.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the standard 'there was a certain man' formula that begins several Judges/Samuel family narratives, then runs through the double-wife exposition and Elkanah's rhetorical question to Hannah, which closes the unit without an answer and hands the scene forward.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off v.1-2 as a bare genealogical notice was considered, but the genealogy has no independent register-formula closure of its own and reads as the front half of one continuous exposition sentence-cluster with the rivalry material.

boundary_rationale: A location shift ('Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost') pulls the scene from the family meal to the sanctuary threshold, and the unit holds together as one continuous encounter between Hannah and Eli through her vow, his misjudgment, and the resolving exchange that ends with her face no longer sad.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Considered cutting at v.12/13 where the narrator pauses to explain that only Hannah's lips moved, but this is an explanatory aside inside a single ongoing dialogue turn, not a scene seam by the Ruth-refinement standard for dialogue-dense narrative.

boundary_rationale: A temporal-formula reset ('rose up in the morning early') plus a location change (return to Ramah) opens this unit, and it closes on the naming etiology, a recognizable closural device distinct from what precedes and follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this pair into the preceding temple scene was rejected because the couple's departure and the conception notice belong to a different setting and season than the doorpost exchange, even though no new characters appear.

boundary_rationale: The yearly-sacrifice notice reintroduces Elkanah as agent ('The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up') against Hannah's staying behind, and the unit is held together by the weaning negotiation, closing on the narrator's summary that she nursed the child until weaning.
strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative would fold this into the following presentation scene since both concern the same vow, but the deferral dialogue is set at home before weaning while vv.24-28 open with a fresh 'when she had weaned him' clause and a change of location to Shiloh.

boundary_rationale: The front edge is weaker than a 'clean temporal hinge': the Hebrew opens with the wayyiqtol vatta'alehu, and the trailing ka'asher gemalattu clause repeats the gamal root that just closed 1:23 (ad gomlah oto), a tail-head continuity signal rather than a break, and WEB's paragraph break falls inside 1:23, not at 1:24. What does hold this edge is content, not syntax: the weaning-length time gap, the relocation from the household to beit YHWH Shiloh, and the cast reduction from the Elkanah/Hannah exchange to mother-child-plus-offerings. The rear edge is independently strong and unaffected: 1:28 closes with a single vayishtachu ('and he worshiped') clause capping a doubled dedication/lending wordplay on Saul's name-root (not a doubled worship notice as previously described), and the poem's own speech formula opens fresh at 2:1, corroborated by the pe sited after 1:28.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this span through 2:11 to capture the Wiederaufnahme link back to 'worshiped... there' was weighed, but the poem's own speech-formula onset at 2:1 is a stronger and more immediate seam than the delayed echo, so the dedication scene is better closed here.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating vv.1-11 as one span (poem plus its narrative frame) was considered on the strength of the Wiederaufnahme at v.11, but the poem/prose seam is the more concrete text signal named in this campaign's binding rules and it falls precisely at v.10/v.11, not v.11/v.12.

boundary_rationale: This single verse is not a resumptive repetition of 1:28 (which contains no serve/Eli language at all) but the first term of a three-point 'ministering' refrain -- na'ar...mesharet...et YHWH...Eli -- that runs 2:11, 2:18, and 3:1a nearly verbatim, bracketing the entire Eli's-sons corruption complex in parallel to the separately-tracked growth refrain (2:21/2:26). Both flanking edges are attested: WEB opens a paragraph at 2:11 and a pe sits after 2:10, corroborating the front; Eli's name here also anticipates 'the sons of Eli' in v.12.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this verse to the following corruption-of-the-priesthood material was the live alternative, since Eli's name here anticipates 'the sons of Eli' in v.12, but the verbal echo running forward to 3:1 (and secondarily 2:18) is specific enough to warrant treating it as its own bridge unit rather than folding it either direction.

boundary_rationale: A disjunctive nominal opening ('Now the sons of Eli were wicked men,' 2:12) pivots the topic away from the resumptive ministering-refrain verse and introduces one continuous iterative description of the priests' fork-custom (2:13-14) escalating into the servant's coercive demand and threat of forced seizure (2:15-16, gam beterem continuing the same iterative mode rather than opening a new register), closing on the narrator's own verdict, 'The sin of the young men was very great before Yahweh' (2:17). This merges the formerly separate M8-1Sam-008 (2:12-2:14) and M8-1Sam-009 (2:15-2:17): the seam previously drawn at 2:14|2:15 rested only on a WEB paragraph marker at 2:16 (one verse later than the drafted cut) and on misattributing 2:16's seizure threat to 2:15, neither of which supports a division at 2:14|2:15. The unit's own edges are independently marked: a disjunctive nominal clause opens it at 2:12, and 2:18's adversative uShemuel mesharet ('But Samuel ministered') closes it with a clean contrastive pivot.

boundary_rationale: The chapter closes with a generalizing summary formula ('Samuel grew... let none of his words fall to the ground... All Israel... knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet') that steps outside scene-time entirely. This is a durative, office-establishment notice, not a regnal accession formula (no age, reign-length, or death formula is present, unlike the true accession notice at 13:1), so the tag is corrected to narrative_prose. The front edge against Samuel's dialogue is unmistakable. The rear edge is genuinely contested rather than settled: 4:1a (vayehi devar Shemuel lechol Yisrael) shares the devar catchword and durative, all-Israel register with 3:19/3:21, and WEB's own paragraph break falls mid-verse inside 4:1, after the devar-clause and before the battle report - grouping 4:1a with this unit rather than with what follows. But 4:1a is also bound forward to 4:1b by a wayyiqtol chain (vayehi...vayetze Yisra'el) with no disjunctive marker, which pulls toward the battle narrative - though the chain's second verb re-expresses its subject (vayetze Yisra'el names Israel explicitly, rather than continuing on an implicit subject), a construction this campaign elsewhere treats as its own boundary-relevant signal (045's 9:5 hemmah ba'u, 057's vehinneh Sha'ul ba), which weakens, without eliminating, this forward pull as a counterweight to the devar-catchword reading. Since the grammar genuinely supports both readings, this decision discloses the devar-chain reading as a live, unresolved alternative rather than silently asserting the drafted cut, and downgrades confidence accordingly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the span to 1Sam.3.19-1Sam.4.1 to keep the devar-catchword material together, on the strength of the shared vocabulary with 3:19/3:21 and WEB's mid-verse paragraph break after 4:1a, is a live and undecided alternative rather than a rejected one: 4:1a is genuinely Janus-faced, bound backward by register and catchword and forward by a wayyiqtol chain with no disjunctive marker, though that forward pull is weakened (not eliminated) by the chain's second verb re-expressing its subject (vayetze Yisra'el) rather than continuing null-subject. Folding this into the preceding dialogue (i.e. not isolating the summary at all) remains rejected, since the shift from scene-bound speech to durative, all-Israel-scope narration is a real register-driven signal.
