strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the Gershonite treasury notice (vv21-22) from the Amramite/Shebuel-Shelomoth notice (vv23-28) into two rows loses because v23's clan list carries no independent head formula and functions only as a hinge inside v20's single governing topic.

boundary_rationale: "לַיִּצְהָרִ֞י כְּנַנְיָ֣הוּ וּבָנָ֗יו לַמְּלָאכָ֤ה הַחִֽיצוֹנָה֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים וּלְשֹׁפְטִֽים" ('of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to the outward business') opens on the same Izharite gentilic already listed at 26:23 (inside the preceding row D131), so the verse resumes a four-clan programme already under way rather than opening an unheralded topic; scanning oshb:1Chr.26.29 word by word turns up neither the divine name nor the royal noun, so the verse itself does not fall inside the Yahweh/king envelope that brackets what follows -- the tie it carries forward includes more than the shared root לַמְּלָאכָ֤ה ('for the... business'), answered by מְלֶ֣אכֶת ('the business of...') in v30: both v.29 and v.30 open on the same lamed-plus-gentilic register-head type (לַיִּצְהָרִ֞י / לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י), and both share the על...ישראל jurisdiction-over-Israel formula (עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל in v.29; עַ֚ל פְּקֻדַּ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל in v.30) -- an inventory that strengthens, rather than weakens, the case for holding v.29 with what follows. This row falls under the single governing head opened at 26:20, וְֽהַלְוִיִּ֑ם אֲחִיָּ֗ה עַל אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים (WEB 'Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God's house...'), which continues unbroken through this row's own span with no register-head formula of a different shape intervening at v.29. A pe follows 26:28 itself (oshb:1Chr.26.28, single-witness), weak corroboration standing exactly at this row's own opening edge -- inside the stretch this row claims one head (26:20) governs unbroken -- disclosed here rather than passed over. That Yahweh/king envelope proper does bracket vv30-32: v30 reads "לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ֩ וְאֶחָ֨יו בְּנֵי חַ֜יִל אֶ֣לֶף וּשְׁבַע מֵא֗וֹת עַ֚ל פְּקֻדַּ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן מַעְרָ֑בָה לְכֹל֙ מְלֶ֣אכֶת יְהוָ֔ה וְלַעֲבֹדַ֖ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ", WEB 'Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of valor, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Yahweh and for the service of the king.', and v32 closes on the matching pair from "וְאֶחָ֣יו בְּנֵי חַ֗יִל אַלְפַּ֛יִם וּשְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֑וֹת וַיַּפְקִידֵ֞ם דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עַל הָראוּבֵנִ֤י וְהַגָּדִי֙ וַחֲצִי֙ שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשִּׁ֔י לְכָל דְּבַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וּדְבַ֥ר הַמֶּֽלֶךְ", which WEB renders 'His relatives, men of valor, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom King David made overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.' (checked word-for-word against 1Chr_web_clean.txt). v30 and v31 both open on the same repeated head, לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י / לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִי֙ ('of the Hebronites'), a possible internal seam that does not in fact carry one: v31 supplies the search notice, "לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִי֙ יְרִיָּ֣ה הָרֹ֔אשׁ לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֥י לְתֹלְדֹתָ֖יו לְאָב֑וֹת בִּשְׁנַ֨ת הָֽאַרְבָּעִ֜ים לְמַלְכ֤וּת דָּוִיד֙ נִדְרָ֔שׁוּ וַיִּמָּצֵ֥א בָהֶ֛ם גִּבּ֥וֹרֵי חַ֖יִל בְּיַעְזֵ֥יר גִּלְעָֽד", that grounds only v32's total of 2,700 (Jerijah's kin, dated to David's fortieth year at Jazer of Gilead), not v30's separate 1,700 (Hashabiah's men, a notice carrying no search language of its own) -- so the repeated לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י head marks two members of one census report rather than two independent units, and the row does not split there. The chapter division itself gets a weak second: v32 ends with a pe (oshb:1Chr.26.32, single-witness), sitting exactly at the seam into 1Chr 27's census-and-course material: "וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָֽאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('the children of Israel after their number').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating Chenaniah's Izharite oversight (v29) from the Hebronite oversight (vv30-32) into two rows is the genuinely live rival: v29 carries neither the divine name nor the royal noun that brackets vv30-32, and its own strongest tie forward is the shared מלאכה/מלאכת root plus its resumption of 26:23's four-clan list (D131) rather than a shared Yahweh/king envelope. The row holds v29 with vv30-32 anyway because both fall under 26:20's single governing head with no register-head formula of a different shape intervening at v29, not because one envelope phrase encloses all four verses alike.

boundary_rationale: "וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָֽאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('the children of Israel after their number') opens a census-and-course register unrelated to the treasuries and business notices just closed, and immediately sets the refrain quantity, הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף -- gloss: 'the one division: twenty-four thousand' -- הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ is the cardinal 'one' agreeing with the definite noun, not an ordinal; 'first' is reserved for the true ordinal, הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙, which the row itself quotes two sentences later at v.2 (oshb:1Chr.27.1; WEB smooths the clause into the general statement 'of every division were twenty-four thousand.', so the English here is the author's own literal rendering of the Hebrew, not a WEB quotation), which recurs almost verbatim after every captain through v15, e.g. "עַ֞ל הַמַּחֲלֹ֤קֶת הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן יָֽשָׁבְעָ֖ם בֶּן זַבְדִּיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַֽחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('and over his division were twenty-four thousand'). A samekh follows nearly every one of these month-entries (oshb:1Chr.27.1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 samekh, single-witness) -- exactly the list-item density the marker policy warns against letting pull row granularity down, since the whole cycle is one formulaic course rotation. v6 briefly breaks the refrain's closing formula to note Benaiah's command of the Thirty, "ה֧וּא בְנָיָ֛הוּ גִּבּ֥וֹר הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֖ים וְעַל הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֑ים וּמַ֣חֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עַמִּיזָבָ֖ד בְּנֽוֹ" ('he was Benaiah, the mighty man of the thirty, and over the thirty; and his division was Ammizabad his son'); that aside stays inside the row because the very next verse resumes the same captain-and-number pattern without any new head. The sequence closes at the twelfth month, "הַשְּׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ לִשְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֣ר הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ חֶלְדַּ֥י הַנְּטוֹפָתִ֖י לְעָתְנִיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('the twelfth, of the twelfth month'), after which a pe mark follows (oshb:1Chr.27.15 pe, single-witness), corroborating the shift at v16 to a differently-headed list: "וְעַל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֣י נָגִ֔יד אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר בֶּן זִכְרִ֑י לַשִּׁ֨מְעוֹנִ֔י שְׁפַטְיָ֖הוּ בֶּֽן מַעֲכָֽה" ('now over the tribes of Israel').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving each of the twelve captains its own row loses because the pervasive samekh chain marks list-item punctuation inside one formulaic 12-fold refrain, the exact case the campaign's granularity guidance names as a single decision.

boundary_rationale: oshb:1Chr.27.15's closing pe (single-witness) sits right where the topic changes: "וְעַל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֣י נָגִ֔יד אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר בֶּן זִכְרִ֑י לַשִּׁ֨מְעוֹנִ֔י שְׁפַטְיָ֖הוּ בֶּֽן מַעֲכָֽה" 'Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, Eliezer the son of Zichri was the ruler; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;' (web:1Chr.27.16/oshb:1Chr.27.16) opens a differently-formed list, one officer per tribe rather than one captain per month. Internally the list carries its own fine punctuation -- double samekh follows both v16 and v21 (oshb:1Chr.27.16 samekh+samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.21 samekh+samekh; both single-witness; two of the book's ten double-samekh verses per the campaign's verified marker profile) -- but that granularity sits below the row, inside the tribe-by-tribe listing. The roll closes with its own formula, "לְדָ֕ן עֲזַרְאֵ֖ל בֶּן יְרֹחָ֑ם אֵ֕לֶּה שָׂרֵ֖י שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('these were the captains of the tribes of Israel'), yet what follows is not a fresh register head but a continuing negative clause, "וְלֹא נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם לְמִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָ֑טָּה כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לְהַרְבּ֥וֹת אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם" ('and David didn't take their number'), which reaches back lexically to v1's opening, "וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָֽאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('the children of Israel after their number'), on the same root. Because vv23-24 open no independent unit -- v24's continuation, "יוֹאָ֨ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֜ה הֵחֵ֤ל לִמְנוֹת֙ וְלֹ֣א כִלָּ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י בָזֹ֛את קֶ֖צֶף עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א עָלָה֙ הַמִּסְפָּ֔ר בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר דִּבְרֵֽי הַיָּמִ֖ים לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד" ('Joab the son of Zeruiah began to number'), simply extends the same aside -- the census note stays inside this row per the inset rule rather than forcing a fresh row at v23. The row ends before v25's differently-headed steward list, "וְעַל֙ אֹצְר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַזְמָ֖וֶת בֶּן עֲדִיאֵ֑ל וְעַ֣ל הָֽאֹצָר֡וֹת בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה בֶּעָרִ֤ים וּבַכְּפָרִים֙ וּבַמִּגְדָּל֔וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן בֶּן עֻזִּיָּֽהוּ" ('and over the king's treasures'). A samekh follows this row's own terminal verse, 27:24, itself (oshb:1Chr.27.24, samekh, single-witness), tier-3 corroboration of the closing edge (the 27:24/27:25 seam), without driving the call.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carving vv23-24 into their own row loses on close reading because the clause opens with a waw-disjunctive background clause (וְלֹא נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙, waw + negative particle + qatal -- the disjunctive, interrupting pattern, not a continuing wayyiqtol), which is what makes vv.23-24 a comment on the preceding registers rather than a new register head; its 'number' vocabulary answers v1's opening rather than starting anything new; folding it back into 27:1-15 instead is a live but weaker alternative, since the tribal-officer roll (16-22) intervenes between the two 'number' notices.

boundary_rationale: "וְעַל֙ אֹצְר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַזְמָ֖וֶת בֶּן עֲדִיאֵ֑ל וְעַ֣ל הָֽאֹצָר֡וֹת בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה בֶּעָרִ֤ים וּבַכְּפָרִים֙ וּבַמִּגְדָּל֔וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן בֶּן עֻזִּיָּֽהוּ" ('and over the king's treasures') begins a run of parallel we'al-headed ('and over...') appointment notices -- fields, tillage, vineyards, olive and sycamore trees, herds, camels, donkeys, flocks -- with no intervening register-head formula of a different shape anywhere in the run. Fine list-item marks punctuate individual entries (oshb:1Chr.27.25 samekh+samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.27 samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.28 samekh+samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.29 samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.30 samekh; all single-witness, with vv25 and 28 counted among the book's ten double-samekh verses in the campaign's verified marker profile), but none of them coincides with a topic change, so they corroborate list density rather than a row seam. A witness-specific caution applies at 27:30/31: WEB 27:30 runs three clauses through 'Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite. Over the donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite. Over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite.' (1Chr_web.usfm), while MT 27:30 stops at יֶחְדְּיָ֖הוּ הַמֵּרֹנֹתִֽי ('Jehdeiah the Meronothite') and MT 27:31 opens with the flocks clause itself, "וְעַל הַצֹּ֖אן יָזִ֣יז הַֽהַגְרִ֑י" ('and over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite'), immediately followed by the run's own closing formula. Both witnesses count 34 verses in this chapter, so this is a clause-level content divergence under matching verse numbers, not a numbering-scheme difference; the samekh keyed to oshb:1Chr.27.30 (single-witness) therefore falls inside WEB's v30 rather than at a WEB verse boundary, and citing web:1Chr.27.30 alongside oshb:1Chr.27.30 as co-extensive material is not accurate at the clause level. This row's own span is unaffected, since v32 begins at the same content point in both witnesses (WEB 'Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.' = MT "וִֽיהוֹנָתָ֤ן דּוֹד דָּוִיד֙ יוֹעֵ֔ץ אִישׁ מֵבִ֥ין וְסוֹפֵ֖ר ה֑וּא וִֽיחִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן חַכְמוֹנִ֖י עִם בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ"). The run closes with its own summary, "וְעַל הַצֹּ֖אן יָזִ֣יז הַֽהַגְרִ֑י כָּל אֵ֨לֶּה֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרְכ֔וּשׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד" ('all these were the rulers of the property'), a formula built the same way as the tribal roll's close just before it ("לְדָ֕ן עֲזַרְאֵ֖ל בֶּן יְרֹחָ֑ם אֵ֕לֶּה שָׂרֵ֖י שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל", 'these were the captains of the tribes of Israel'). v32 then drops the we'al pattern entirely for a named-person-plus-apposition notice, WEB 'Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.' (web:1Chr.27.32/oshb:1Chr.27.32, checked against 1Chr_web_clean.txt), marking the row's close by a genuine syntactic shift rather than by a mark.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the field/orchard stewards (vv25-28) from the herd/flock stewards (vv29-31) loses because both halves use the identical we'al-plus-name format with no head-formula change between them, and both fall under the single closing formula of v31.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:1Chr.27.30 (WEB clause content diverges from MT at 27.30/31 -- see rationale)
oshb:1Chr.27.30 (samekh, single-witness; falls inside WEB v30, not at a WEB verse end)

boundary_rationale: Against the we'al-headed steward list just closed (e.g. "וְעַל֙ אֹצְר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַזְמָ֖וֶת בֶּן עֲדִיאֵ֑ל וְעַ֣ל הָֽאֹצָר֡וֹת בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה בֶּעָרִ֤ים וּבַכְּפָרִים֙ וּבַמִּגְדָּל֔וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן בֶּן עֻזִּיָּֽהוּ"), v32 shifts to naming the person first and appending his role: WEB 'Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.' (web:1Chr.27.32/oshb:1Chr.27.32). The same shape continues through v33, "וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל יוֹעֵ֣ץ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְחוּשַׁ֥י הָאַרְכִּ֖י רֵ֥עַ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ" ('Ahithophel was the king's counselor. Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.'), with a samekh after it (oshb:1Chr.27.33 samekh, single-witness) marking that internal item boundary, and closes with a succession note followed by a second clause naming the army's commander that in the MT is role-phrase-first, with the name in final position: וְשַׂר צָבָ֥א לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יוֹאָֽב ('and commander of the army for the king, יוֹאָֽב'), the reverse of the name-first pattern that opens vv.32-33 (וִֽיהוֹנָתָ֤ן..., וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל..., וְחוּשַׁ֥י...); WEB's own rendering inverts this to a subject-first English clause, 'Joab was the captain of the king’s army.' (web:1Chr.27.34/oshb:1Chr.27.34, WEB's own wording per 1Chr_web_clean.txt -- the row's prior citation had further inverted WEB's own order and inserted an unwarranted leading 'and'). Unlike the two preceding rows, this short counselor notice has no 'these are' summary of its own; its unity rests on the shared named-person-plus-role pattern across all three verses rather than on a closing formula, which is why the row is held at a lower confidence than the we'al-headed lists around it. oshb:1Chr.27.34 does close on a pe (single-witness), a weak second placed exactly at the part's own terminal edge, where 1Chr 28 opens an assembly scene outside this range.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv32-34 into the preceding stewards row (25-31) as one combined unit loses because v32 replaces the we'al-headed appointment pattern with a named-person-plus-apposition pattern, a syntactic break that is sufficient on its own; the closing pe after v34 (oshb:1Chr.27.34, single-witness) would fall at the same location whether this is read as a standalone 32-34 row or as part of a combined 25-34 row, so it cannot discriminate between the two options and is not treated here as evidence for either.

boundary_rationale: The part begins with a hiphil summons, "וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל דָּוִ֣יד אֶת כָּל שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שָׂרֵ֣י הַשְּׁבָטִ֣ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמַּחְלְק֣וֹת הַמְשָׁרְתִ֪ים אֶת הַמֶּ֟לֶךְ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֲלָפִ֣ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י כָל רְכוּשׁ וּמִקְנֶה֩ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וּלְבָנָ֜יו עִם הַסָּרִיסִ֧ים וְהַגִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וּֽלְכָל גִּבּ֥וֹר חָ֖יִל אֶל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם", that governs a single enumerated catalogue of officeholder classes -- tribal princes, rotation-captains who served the king, captains of thousands and hundreds, stewards of royal property and livestock, officers, and mighty men -- terminating in the phrase WEB renders 'David assembled all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes, the captains of the companies who served the king by division, the captains of thousands, the captains of hundreds, and the rulers over all the substance and possessions of the king and of his sons, with the officers and the mighty men, even all the mighty men of valor, to Jerusalem.' Verse 2 opens with a consecutive wayyiqtol, "וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל רַגְלָ֔יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר" ('the king stood up on his feet and said'), which formally continues rather than breaks the narrative chain v1's own וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל opens -- Hebrew wayyiqtol chains run through unit boundaries rather than sealing them, so the seam here is discourse-level, not syntactic closure. It is real on its own narrower ground: v1's roster opens no quotation frame of any kind, and the imperative that follows, "שְׁמָע֖וּנִי אַחַ֣י וְעַמִּ֑י" ('hear me, my brothers and my people'), is a bare vocative that names no group by itself -- its referent is recoverable only from the enumerated officer-classes v1 just gathered. A closed participant-list handing straight into a newly inaugurated speech is the seam: v1 anticipates no quotation, and v2 supplies both the first inquit and the audience v1's own roster set up.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v1 into the address that follows (making 28:1-7 or longer one row) is the genuinely live rival the corrected grounds must still answer: no syntactic break forces the split, since v2's wayyiqtol continues v1's own chain. The split holds because v1 opens no quotation frame and v2 supplies both the first inquit and the addressee v1's roster sets up -- a register-to-speech-inauguration transition, not a chain break.

boundary_rationale: David's speech, inaugurated in the preceding verse, runs continuously through this span: his own account of wanting to build 'a house of rest for the ark of Yahweh's covenant' and God's refusal, "וְהָאֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֣מַר לִ֔י לֹא תִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י כִּ֣י אִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמ֛וֹת אַ֖תָּה וְדָמִ֥ים שָׁפָֽכְתָּ" ('But God said to me, ‘You shall not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.’', 28:3), then the election chain opened by the wayyiqtol וַיִּבְחַ֡ר ('and he chose') -- Yahweh chose David out of his father's house (28:4), then chose Solomon among many sons for the throne, וַיִּבְחַר֙ בִּשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֔י (28:5, 'and he chose Solomon my son') -- culminating in a quoted divine promise about Solomon's kingdom (28:6-7). That quoted promise closes on its own temporal tag, כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה / 'as it is today,' ending the embedded divine word David is reciting. The next verse pivots on the adverb וְ֠עַתָּה ('now therefore') at 28:8, a single pivot marking the move from rehearsed background into imperative charge -- רְאֵ֣ה עַתָּ֗ה at 28:10 is a related but distinct hinge, and the later וְ֠עַתָּה instances at 29:13 and 29:17 belong to the prayer, a separate speech-act, where they open thanksgiving rather than imperative charge -- so the true seam falls between v7 and v8 on the strength of the pivot itself, without any claim to frequency.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking before v4, where the wayyiqtol election-chain begins, would separate David's personal account from the election chain it grounds, but no inquit reopens there -- it stays one uninterrupted first-person address. Two embedded inquits inside this same span do report speech but do not seam it either: "וְהָאֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֣מַר לִ֔י " ('God said to me', v3) and "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔י" ('he said to me', v6) are first-person recollections nested inside David's own recital -- 'X said TO ME' -- not narrator-level frames that redirect the addressee the way the framing inquits at 28:20, 29:1, and 29:10 do; an inset that stays syntactically resumed within its host speech stays inside the row it is embedded in, so neither supplies a stronger seam than the וְ֠עַתָּה pivot at v8.

boundary_rationale: The pivot וְ֠עַתָּה just discussed opens a self-contained charge addressed with second-person plural imperatives, שִׁמְר֣וּ וְדִרְשׁ֔וּ ('observe and seek out'). The addressee is not named by the witness-phrase that follows: "וְ֠עַתָּה לְעֵינֵ֨י כָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל קְהַל יְהוָה֙ וּבְאָזְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ" ('in the sight of all Israel, Yahweh's assembly, and in the audience of our God') stands as two parallel adverbial witness-phrases governed by לְעֵינֵ֨י/וּבְאָזְנֵ֣י, not as a vocative -- since God plainly cannot be the addressee of the imperatives that follow, neither parallel member is; the 2mp addressee itself is unnamed here and recoverable only from 28:1's own participant list. The verse closes on its own inheritance formula, עַד עוֹלָֽם ('forever'). The very next verse reopens with a new vocative and a grammatically singular addressee, "וְאַתָּ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹֽה בְנִ֡י" ('but you, Solomon, my son'), paired with singular imperatives (דַּע֩ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֨י אָבִ֜יךָ וְעָבְדֵ֗הוּ, 2ms) -- a plural-to-singular addressee shift that is grammatical, not merely rhetorical, and v9's casus-pendens vocative has no counterpart at all in v8. This particular seam also carries a WLC petuchah at 28:8 (single-witness), which happens to land exactly at the addressee change described above -- offered strictly as corroboration, never as what drives the call.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 28:8-10 as a single exhortation because both halves share the surrounding 'now therefore...be strong' envelope discounts the fact that the addressee and grammatical number both change at v9, which is the stronger signal.

boundary_rationale: Following the addressee shift argued above, the singular charge דַּע֩ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֨י אָבִ֜יךָ וְעָבְדֵ֗הוּ ('know the God of your father and serve him') runs to its climax in the imperative pair חֲזַ֥ק וַעֲשֵֽׂה ('be strong and do it,' v10), which closes the entire 28:2-10 address. Verse 11 opens a new wayyiqtol with a different subject-verb pattern, וַיִּתֵּ֣ן דָּוִ֣יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֡וֹ אֶת תַּבְנִ֣ית הָאוּלָם֩ ('David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch'), shifting from second-person imperative speech to third-person narration of a handed-over object -- a change in both grammatical person and verb-type marks the seam. Worth noting only in passing: the WLC divides here too, with a petuchah after 28:10 (single-witness) -- a detail that lines up with, but does not establish, the person/verb-type break just argued.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this span through v19 -- one row for the charge plus the whole pattern-transfer -- would erase the person/verb-type break at v11 and swallow the internal pattern-word inclusio that the next row argues on its own terms.

boundary_rationale: The narrative wayyiqtol that closes the prior row, "וַיִּתֵּ֣ן דָּוִ֣יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֡וֹ אֶת תַּבְנִ֣ית הָאוּלָם֩ וְֽאֶת בָּ֨תָּ֜יו וְגַנְזַכָּ֧יו וַעֲלִיֹּתָ֛יו וַחֲדָרָ֥יו הַפְּנִימִ֖ים וּבֵ֥ית הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת" ('David gave...the pattern of the porch'), opens a register in which תַּבְנִ֣ית ('pattern') is the recurring spine: v12 "וְתַבְנִ֗ית כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה בָר֨וּחַ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ לְחַצְר֧וֹת בֵּית יְהוָ֛ה וּלְכָל הַלְּשָׁכ֖וֹת סָבִ֑יב לְאֹֽצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּלְאֹצְר֖וֹת הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים" ('the pattern of all he had by the Spirit'), v18 "וּלְמִזְבַּ֧ח הַקְּטֹ֛רֶת זָהָ֥ב מְזֻקָּ֖ק בַּמִּשְׁקָ֑ל וּלְתַבְנִ֣ית הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֗ה הַכְּרֻבִ֤ים זָהָב֙ לְפֹ֣רְשִׂ֔ים וְסֹכְכִ֖ים עַל אֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית יְהוָֽה" ('the pattern of the chariot, the cherubim'), and the closing tally at v19, "הַכֹּ֥ל בִּכְתָ֛ב מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה עָלַ֣י הִשְׂכִּ֑יל כֹּ֖ל מַלְאֲכ֥וֹת הַתַּבְנִֽית" ('all the works of this pattern') -- an inclusio bracketing the intervening itemized list of courts and treasuries (12) and priestly/Levite divisions (13), and the weighed gold and silver vessels marked by the recurring word בַּמִּשְׁקָל֙ ('by weight,' 14-17). WEB's inserted quotation-tag at v19, 'David said,' has no Hebrew inquit-verb behind it -- הַכֹּ֥ל בִּכְתָ֛ב מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה is David's own summary clause, not a new speech-opening -- so it is a translator's continuity marker, not textual evidence of a fresh unit. The enumeration therefore runs unbroken from 11 to 19. A WLC pe closes 1Chr.28.19 (oshb:1Chr.28.19, single-witness), agreeing with but not driving this edge -- disclosed here since every sibling row in this cluster discloses its own adjacent mark as corroboration. Verse 20 is where a genuine new inquit appears, "וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֗וֹ חֲזַ֤ק וֶאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָ֑ת כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֱלֹהַי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֤א יַרְפְּךָ֙ וְלֹ֣א יַֽעַזְבֶ֔ךָּ עַד לִכְל֕וֹת כָּל מְלֶ֖אכֶת עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית יְהוָֽה" ('David said to Solomon his son'), and that is the true close of this register-inset.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v14, where the weight-refrain begins, would cut a single prepositional chain that the pattern-word inclusio shows is one list; an itemized register this formulaic should not be sliced at the verse level.

boundary_rationale: The fresh inquit that ends the previous row, "וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֗וֹ" (David said to Solomon his son), carries the imperative triplet "חֲזַ֤ק וֶאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָ֑ת" ('be strong and courageous, and do it; don't be afraid, nor be dismayed'), which echoes -- rather than purpose-builds a bracket around -- 28:10's own briefer חֲזַ֥ק וַעֲשֵֽׂה: an in-book sweep for חזק co-occurring with אמץ across 1 Chronicles returns only two verses, 22:13 and 28:20. 22:13 supplies the same imperative pair and the same negated pair that 28:20 reproduces, "חֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָ֔ץ אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָֽת" (oshb:1Chr.22.13, 6 tokens), against 28:20's "חֲזַ֤ק וֶאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָ֑ת" (oshb:1Chr.28.20, 7 tokens) -- not word-for-word identical, since the do-imperative וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה is wedged between the two pairs at 28:20 only. 22:16's "ק֣וּם וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה וִיהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ" (oshb:1Chr.22.16) separately supplies the do-imperative-plus-accompaniment pairing that 28:20's own עִמָּ֔ךְ repeats. The charge at 28:20 thus draws on a Chronicles-wide David-to-Solomon charge repertoire spanning ch 22 and ch 28, of which 28:10 is itself an abbreviation, rather than a bracket purpose-built around the intervening 28:11-19 pattern-register; the element 28:20 shares uniquely with 28:10 is only the shared do-imperative. Verse 21 continues the same address -- וְעִמְּךָ֙ ('and with you') -- to list the human support available to Solomon: priestly and Levite divisions ("וְהִנֵּ֗ה מַחְלְקוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְכָל עֲבוֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים"), willing skilled workers, captains, and, closing the verse, "וְהַשָּׂרִ֥ים וְכָל הָעָ֖ם לְכָל דְּבָרֶֽיךָ" ('the captains and all the people at your every word'). Then 29:1 opens an entirely new speech-inauguration formula, "וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל" ('David the king said to all the assembly'), addressed now to the wider assembly rather than to Solomon, and turning to a new subject, funding the temple -- a clean chapter-crossing seam. The WLC's own paragraphing agrees, for what that is worth: a petuchah (single-witness) follows 28:21, right where the chapter-crossing seam falls -- supporting evidence, not the argument itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 28:20-21 to the preceding pattern-register as one long row would submerge the inclusio-closing echo of 'be strong...do it' inside the list it answers, when the fresh inquit at v20 marks it as its own closing movement.

boundary_rationale: The new inquit that opens this row, "וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל", has David naming Solomon נַ֣עַר וָרָ֑ךְ ('young and tender') for a task too great for a man, then cataloguing his own preparation and private gift of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and precious stones (29:2-4) before posing the appeal itself: "וּמִ֣י מִתְנַדֵּ֔ב לְמַלֹּ֥אות יָד֛וֹ הַיּ֖וֹם לַיהוָֽה" ('who then offers willingly to consecrate himself today to Yahweh,' 29:5b). Verse 6 answers with a matching wayyiqtol, "וַיִּֽתְנַדְּבוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת" ('then the princes of the fathers' households'), and the itemized totals and Jehiel's oversight (29:7-8) resolve into one joy-notice naming both parties, "וַיִּשְׂמְח֤וּ הָעָם֙ עַל הִֽתְנַדְּבָ֔ם כִּ֚י בְּלֵ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם הִֽתְנַדְּב֖וּ לַיהוָ֑ה וְגַם֙ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׂמַ֖ח שִׂמְחָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה" ('the people rejoiced... and David the king also rejoiced with great joy,' 29:9), binding appeal and response into a single episode. Verse 10 opens a different speech-act altogether, David's blessing of Yahweh rather than his appeal to the assembly, "וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל", so that is where this row ends. For completeness, a petuchah (single-witness) is keyed to 29:9 in the WLC, coinciding with the joy-notice that closes this episode; the coincidence corroborates rather than proves the boundary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v6, where the subject shifts from David's appeal to the princes' response ("וַיִּֽתְנַדְּבוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת", a subject-changing wayyiqtol), has genuine grammatical support, but the נדב stem-chain running from v5's appeal verb through v9's double hitpael, plus the shared joy-notice at v9 that names both David and the people together in one clause, binds appeal to response into one cause-and-effect episode on tier-1 grounds alone.

boundary_rationale: David's blessing-inquit, "וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל" ('David blessed Yahweh before all the assembly, and said'), is answered at once by the address formula "בָּר֨וּךְ אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙" ('blessed are you, Yahweh') that opens the doxology (29:11-12). A second-person vocative toward Yahweh recurs at every internal pivot of what follows -- v13's "וְעַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ מוֹדִ֥ים אֲנַ֖חְנוּ לָ֑ךְ" ('now therefore, our God, we thank you'), the self-examining movement of 14-17, and the patriarchal invocation of v18, "יְהוָ֗ה אֱ֠לֹהֵי אַבְרָהָ֞ם יִצְחָ֤ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ" -- without any inquit ever reopening the address; the prayer stays one uninterrupted utterance from its blessing-formula to the climactic petition for Solomon, "וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֗י תֵּ֚ן לֵבָ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם" ('and to Solomon my son give a perfect heart,' 29:19), which itself closes by echoing a term first introduced in the preceding row, not by returning to this row's own opening: "וְלִבְנ֖וֹת הַבִּירָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר הֲכִינֽוֹתִי" ('and to build the palace, for which I have made provision') picks up the word הַבִּירָ֔ה ('the palace') from 29:1, inside D143, not from inside this row's own 29:10 opening. Verse 20 turns outward again with a fresh third-person narrative inquit directed at the congregation rather than at God, "וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל", which is where the prayer ends. The WLC likewise breaks after 29:19 with a petuchah (single-witness), matching the point where the prayer's address to Yahweh gives way to David's address to the assembly -- again, corroboration only.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking at v13's now-therefore pivot would isolate the thanksgiving from the doxology it thanks God for, but no new inquit or change of addressee happens there -- the second-person address to Yahweh runs straight through. A second rival, reading 29:1-19 as one combined arc bracketed by the two הבירה occurrences (29:1 and 29:19), is the genuinely live alternative once the misattributed echo above is corrected; it loses to the v10 blessing-inquit because that inquit pairs with a real addressee shift -- from the assembly (29:1's own address) to Yahweh (29:10's בָּר֨וּךְ אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙) -- and book_strategy_draft.md's own device matrix names 'the great blessing 29:10-19' as a standing Chronicles speech-and-prayer-frame device keyed to that same shift; a named, recurring device is the stronger seam-driver here, not a two-point lexical inclusio on a single rare noun.

boundary_rationale:
The fresh third-person inquit at v20, "וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל בָּֽרְכוּ נָ֖א אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם" ('David said to all the assembly, now bless Yahweh your God'), carries its own second-person plural imperative directed at the assembly. The strongest rival to opening a fresh unit here is lexical, not merely pragmatic: a consonantal sweep of the ברך root across ch 29 returns exactly two verses, 29:10 and 29:20, and no others -- 29:10 opens "וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל" ('David blessed Yahweh in the sight of all the assembly') and 29:20 pairs "בָּֽרְכוּ נָ֖א" with "וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ כָֽל הַקָּהָ֗ל" ('and all the assembly blessed'), so the same three elements -- the ברך root, דָּוִיד֙, and כָֽל הַקָּהָ֗ל -- stand at both ends of 29:10-20 and nowhere else in the chapter, which could as easily be read as a closing inclusio for the prayer as an opening re-head for this row. It functions as the latter: v20 supplies David's own second address inaugurating a new congregational act (an imperative followed by the assembly's own enactment, "וַיִּקְּד֧וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ לַיהוָ֖ה וְלַמֶּֽלֶךְ", 'and they bowed down and worshiped Yahweh and the king'), where v10 supplied only David's own solitary act of blessing before the assembly as onlookers; the addressee and grammatical shape change even though the root repeats, so the repetition re-heads rather than closes.

The row continues through the next-day sacrifice at v21, "וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה זְ֠בָחִים וַיַּעֲל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת לַיהוָ֗ה לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ פָּרִ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף אֵילִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף כְּבָשִׂ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֑ם וּזְבָחִ֥ים לָרֹ֖ב לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('they sacrificed sacrifices to Yahweh and offered burnt offerings to Yahweh on the next day after that day... for all Israel'), which the book strategy's own §7 item 15 flags as a live interior question ('29:21-25 enthronement notice: close of assembly vs its own unit'), naming the day-shift clause לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ this row's rationale must argue rather than merely narrate. Argued here: the wayyiqtol subject at v21 (וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ, 3mp) continues the same collective-plural subject the assembly held at v20 (וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ...וַיִּקְּד֧וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ), with no new addressee or inquit intervening -- the day-shift moves the scene forward in time but not to a new speaker or audience, so v21 stays inside one unbroken liturgical occasion rather than opening a fresh unit, on this first leg alone. A second leg does not help this argument and is dropped: v.21 has already displaced the scene to לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ ('the morrow of that day'), so v.22's own demonstrative, בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא ('on that day'), most naturally denotes that newly introduced morrow rather than reaching back to v.20's original day; the join is carried unaided by v.21's continuing subject, without help from an 'explicit anchor' claim the text does not in fact support. The subject then narrows from the collective assembly to Solomon alone at v23, "וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּ֨א יְהוָ֧ה לְמֶ֛לֶךְ" ('Solomon sat on the throne of Yahweh as king'), a focus-narrowing within the same liturgical day rather than a register-level break of the kind the gathering verbs at 11:1 and 28:1 mark. The row closes on an evaluative summary, "וַיְגַדֵּ֨ל יְהוָ֤ה אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְמַ֔עְלָה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא הָיָ֧ה עַל כָּל מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('Yahweh magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and gave to him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel,' 29:25; the relative clause's antecedent, ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת, is carried in full here rather than elided, and WEB's own closing restriction, 'not been on any king before him in Israel.', is retained). Verse 26 opens the regnal résumé with a subject-first clause, "וְדָוִיד֙ בֶּן יִשָׁ֔י מָלַ֖ךְ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel'), which shifts away from the enthronement scene into a summary of the completed reign.

The book strategy's own §6 block map affirmatively lists '29:10-19 David's blessing-prayer; 29:20-25 worship + Solomon enthroned' as settled, and its only live flag in this range is §7 item 15's interior question at 29:21-25, not a dispute over whether v20 itself belongs with the prayer that precedes it; I hold this row's confidence at medium because, even with the day-shift and subject-narrowing arguments given above, the interior seam §7.15 names remains one the strategy itself treats as genuinely open, not because the 29:19|20 edge is in question.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuinely strongest rival is not whether v20 attaches to the prayer before it -- the ברך root's repetition at 29:10/29:20 is a real echo, but v20's imperative-plus-new-addressee shape re-heads rather than closes, as argued above -- but whether v21 opens its own unit at the day-shift the book strategy flags at §7.15; that rival loses because the wayyiqtol subject at v21 continues v20's own collective assembly with no new inquit or addressee -- the join needed to keep v.21 inside this row rests on that continuity alone, not on v.22's own demonstrative, which on the row's continuity principle points to the newly introduced morrow rather than back to v.20's day.

boundary_rationale: The subject-first regnal clause that opens this row, "וְדָוִיד֙ בֶּן יִשָׁ֔י מָלַ֖ךְ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל", answers the previous row's own closing verse on the מלך root rather than reproducing a throne formula: 29:25 closes "עַל כָּל מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('than any king before him, over Israel'), and this row's opening verb, מָלַ֖ךְ ('reigned'), answers that same noun מֶ֛לֶךְ with its own עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל tail -- the throne-sitting formula proper, "וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּ֨א יְהוָ֧ה לְמֶ֛לֶךְ" ('Solomon sat on the throne of Yahweh as king'), sits two verses earlier, inside the preceding row's own span rather than at its closing edge. Here the מלך root opens a new unit -- no scene-verb, no addressee -- answered by the reign-length count, "וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָלַךְ֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּחֶבְר֤וֹן מָלַךְ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֥ם מָלַ֖ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֽוֹשׁ" ('the days that he reigned over Israel, forty years'), and the death notice (29:28). The same unit turns into the source-citation colophon at v29, "וְדִבְרֵי֙ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאֲחרֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל דִּבְרֵי֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל הָרֹאֶ֔ה וְעַל דִּבְרֵי֙ נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא וְעַל דִּבְרֵ֖י גָּ֥ד הַחֹזֶֽה" ('the acts of David the king, first and last, are written in the records of Samuel the ro'eh-seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the chozeh-seer' -- WEB itself renders both הָרֹאֶ֔ה and הַחֹזֶֽה as 'seer' at 29:29, matching 1Chr_web_clean.txt and collapsing the same lexical distinction; the two Hebrew nouns are in fact different roots, disclosed here since the colophon's three-way title variation, alongside 'the prophet,' is part of what marks this as a source-citation colophon), which picks up the same completed reign just totaled in 26-28 with no intervening scene-change, and the row closes on 29:30's summary tag, "עִ֥ם כָּל מַלְכוּת֖וֹ וּגְבוּרָת֑וֹ וְהָעִתִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבְר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ וְעַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעַ֖ל כָּל מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאֲרָצֽוֹת" ('with all his reign and his might, and the events that involved him, Israel, and all the kingdoms of the lands'), which ends both this row and the book itself, leaving no further verse to argue a closing edge against. Two petuchah breaks (both single-witness) bracket this closing unit in the WLC, one after 29:25 and one after 29:30 -- neither supplies the reason for these edges, both merely agree with them.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 29:26-28 (the résumé) from 29:29-30 (the colophon) into two rows would cut a single closing movement in two: v29's report of David's acts picks up the very reign just totaled, with no new scene-verb or addressee intervening between them.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens with the book's own first verse and its accession formula וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֛ק שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בֶן דָּוִ֖יד עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ ('Solomon the son of David was firmly established in his kingdom,' web:2Chr.1.1), which sets the עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ ('over his kingdom') theme that v.13 will later echo. Verses 2-6 narrate one continuous action — Solomon's summons to the nation's officials (web:2Chr.1.2) and the assembly's move to the Gibeon high place for sacrifice (web:2Chr.1.3-1.6), noting in passing why the ark at Jerusalem and the Gibeon tabernacle stood apart (web:2Chr.1.4-1.5) — closing on וַיַּ֧עַל עָלָ֛יו עֹל֖וֹת אָֽלֶף ('and offered one thousand burnt offerings on it,' web:2Chr.1.6). The next verse pivots on a temporal disjunction, בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נִרְאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ('That night, God appeared to Solomon,' web:2Chr.1.7), switching register from public cultic action to private nocturnal theophany, so the sacrifice act is the natural close of this opening notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through v.7 to include the theophany would blur the sacrifice scene's own closure at 'a thousand burnt offerings' into an event the night-formula deliberately sets apart as a separate occasion.

boundary_rationale: בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נִרְאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ('That night, God appeared to Solomon,' web:2Chr.1.7) opens a self-contained exchange: God's invitation to ask for anything (web:2Chr.1.7), Solomon's petition for wisdom over riches, honor, or long life (web:2Chr.1.8-1.10), and God's grant of both wisdom and the unrequested wealth (web:2Chr.1.11-1.12). It closes with the return notice, וַיָּבֹ֨א שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה לַבָּמָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר בְּגִבְעוֹן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל ('So Solomon came from the high place that was at Gibeon...to Jerusalem; and he reigned over Israel,' web:2Chr.1.13). A samekh follows v.10 (oshb:2Chr.1.10, samekh, single-witness), tier-3 evidence disclosed here that neither drives nor defeats this unit's boundary; it falls at the petition/answer hinge inside the span (petition 1:8-1:10, answer 1:11), and the question-and-answer exchange itself runs unbroken across it. The shared element between v.13's closing verb, וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and v.1's עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ is the root מלך (lemma citation, not itself an attested pointed form) -- מַלְכוּת is the -ut abstract noun built on that root, not the shared root, and remains the correct citation below for the noun's own recurrences, each attested with the 3ms suffix וֹ, but a book-wide check shows the same root recurring past this span, at oshb:2Chr.1.18 (= web:2Chr.2.1, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ) and again at oshb:2Chr.3.2 (וַ֠יָּחֶל לִבְנ֞וֹת בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי֙ בַּשֵּׁנִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֖ע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ); the recurrence is a passing thematic thread running through the wider Solomon narrative, not an exclusive envelope confined to 1:1-1:13, so no inclusio claim rests on it here. A PE follows v.13 (oshb:2Chr.1.13, pe, single-witness), weak corroboration for the close. Verse 14 then opens an unrelated administrative topic, וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ ('Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen,' web:2Chr.1.14), so the reign-confirmation at v.13 is where this dialogue unit properly ends.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reassigning v.13 to the following wealth notice as its opening frame is the closest rival, but it would strip v.13 of its own return-and-reign-confirmation report and orphan the oracle from the narrative resolution that closes it.

boundary_rationale: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ (web:2Chr.1.14) turns from the Gibeon oracle to a wealth-and-trade inventory -- chariots and horsemen (web:2Chr.1.14), silver, gold, and cedar made common as stone (web:2Chr.1.15), and the horse-and-chariot trade with Egypt and Kue (web:2Chr.1.16) -- running through the closing trade notice, וְ֠כֵן לְכָל מַלְכֵ֧י הַֽחִתִּ֛ים וּמַלְכֵ֥י אֲרָ֖ם בְּיָדָ֥ם יוֹצִֽיאוּ (web:2Chr.1.17), rendered by WEB as 'They also exported them to the Hittite kings and the Syrian kings.' rather than an unlabeled translator gloss. The next verse, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ (web:2Chr.2.1 = oshb:2Chr.1.18 (MT), 'Solomon decided to build a house for Yahweh's name, and a house for his kingdom'), is a 3ms wayyiqtol with Solomon as its explicit subject throughout and no independent first-person pronoun anywhere in it; the pivot from this row's third-person commercial reportage to that verse's third-person notice of royal building-resolve (a wayyiqtol plus an infinitive-of-purpose clause) is the register shift that marks the close, not a shift into first person -- the independent pronoun אֲנִי first stands three verses later -- the interval from oshb 1:18 running 2:1, 2:2, 2:3 -- at web:2Chr.2.4 = oshb:2Chr.2.3 (MT), הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י בֽוֹנֶה, which is decision M8-2Chr-005's own opening line; first-person reference has already entered Solomon's letter one verse earlier, however, at web:2Chr.2.3 = oshb:2Chr.2.2 (MT), whose כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ עִם דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔י carries a 1cs suffix inside the direct speech opened by לֵאמֹ֑ר -- material that belongs to decision M8-2Chr-005's own span, not this row's, since it follows this row's own closing verse, web:2Chr.2.1 = oshb:1.18 (MT), by two verses. book_strategy_draft.md §6 lists this exact span, '1:14-17 (inclusio partner status),' among the campaign's roughly fifteen expected low-confidence regions, tied to the disputed 9:25-28 inclusio-partner identification; that identification is corroborating context from outside this part, not the primary boundary evidence, which rests on the in-part topic pivot on both edges (theophany-to-commerce at v.14, commerce-to-building-resolve at 2:1 = 1:18 MT).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 1:14-17 forward into the temple-decision notice as one long 'transition' unit ignores the sharp register switch from third-person commercial reportage to third-person building resolve that opens web:2Chr.2.1 (= oshb:1.18 MT), not a seam the strategy conceded doubt about -- book_strategy_draft.md §6 flags 1:14-17 only for its disputed 9:25-28 inclusio-partner status, a different question, so no strategy-level concession attaches to this register-switch seam itself.

boundary_rationale: web:2Chr.2.1 = oshb:2Chr.1.18 (MT), וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ ('Solomon decided to build a house for Yahweh's name, and a house for his kingdom'), opens the temple-preparation pericope with Solomon's own building resolve, immediately paired with the workforce count at web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT), וַיִּסְפֹּ֨ר שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ אִ֣ישׁ סַבָּ֔ל וּשְׁמוֹנִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ חֹצֵ֣ב בָּהָ֑ר וּמְנַצְּחִ֣ים עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת ('Solomon counted out seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand men who were stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them'). A PE follows this verse (web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT), pe, single-witness), weak corroboration for treating decision-plus-census as one opening notice. The next verse turns outward with a sending formula, web:2Chr.2.3 = oshb:2Chr.2.2 (MT), וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶל חוּרָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ צֹ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר ('Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying'), which begins direct diplomatic correspondence and so closes this internal notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 2:1-2 with the letter that follows into one undivided 'temple-preparation' block is the strongest rival, but it effaces the sending-formula boundary that opens direct correspondence only at web:2Chr.2.3.

boundary_rationale: The frame is explicit on both sides, satisfying the inset rule for isolating a letter as its own row: the internal decision-and-census notice closes at web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT) (with its PE), and the sending formula web:2Chr.2.3 = oshb:2Chr.2.2 (MT), וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶל חוּרָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ צֹ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר, opens direct first-person discourse — beginning at web:2Chr.2.4 = oshb:2Chr.2.3 (MT), הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י בֽוֹנֶה בַּ֜יִת לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֗י ('Behold, I am about to build a house for the name of Yahweh my God'), and continuing through the rhetorical question of God's greatness (web:2Chr.2.5-2.6), the request for a skilled craftsman (web:2Chr.2.7), and the timber and provisions request (web:2Chr.2.8-2.9) — that runs to web:2Chr.2.10 = oshb:2Chr.2.9 (MT), וְשֶׁ֕מֶן בַּתִּ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אָֽלֶף ('and oil, twenty thousand baths,' the last item Solomon promises), where a PE also falls (web:2Chr.2.10 = oshb:2Chr.2.9 (MT), pe, single-witness). The reply that follows, web:2Chr.2.11 = oshb:2Chr.2.10 (MT), וַיֹּ֨אמֶר חוּרָ֤ם מֶֽלֶךְ צֹר֙ בִּכְתָ֔ב וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ('Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing...to Solomon'), reverses both the sending direction and the speaker, closing this request-letter as its own bounded unit within the census-framed pericope.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Combining Solomon's request and Huram's reply into a single 'letter exchange' row is plausible given their shared subject matter, but it erases the speaker-change and reply-marker (בִּכְתָ֔ב) that the text itself uses to hand the correspondence to a new voice.

boundary_rationale: Huram's own reply begins where Solomon's request left off: web:2Chr.2.11 = oshb:2Chr.2.10 (MT), וַיֹּ֨אמֶר חוּרָ֤ם מֶֽלֶךְ צֹר֙ בִּכְתָ֔ב וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה בְּאַהֲבַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת עַמּ֔וֹ נְתָנְךָ֥ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ, is itself a third-person narrative frame naming the responding king and marking the reply's written form with בִּכְתָ֔ב ('in writing'), reversing the sending direction against Solomon's own letter-opening at web:2Chr.2.3 = oshb:2Chr.2.2 (MT), וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶל חוּרָ֥ם; the doxology that follows at web:2Chr.2.12 = oshb:2Chr.2.11 (MT), בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ('Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel'), continues that frame as Huram's own quoted speech -- a book-wide check shows the identical phrase recurs verbatim in consonants, points, and accents at oshb:2Chr.6.4, בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, spoken by Solomon himself, so the doxology is not speaker-exclusive; the seam rests instead on the changed grammatical subject, the בִּכְתָ֔ב reply-marker, and the reversed sending direction. The commendation of Huram-abi and his lineage (web:2Chr.2.13-2.14) and the logistics for shipping the provisions (web:2Chr.2.15) run to web:2Chr.2.16 = oshb:2Chr.2.15 (MT), וְאַתָּ֛ה תַּעֲלֶ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם ('then you shall carry it up to Jerusalem,' web:2Chr.2.16), with a PE following (web:2Chr.2.16 = oshb:2Chr.2.15 (MT), pe, single-witness). Sustained third-person narrative action -- as opposed to the reply's own opening frame clause -- resumes only at the next verse, web:2Chr.2.17 = oshb:2Chr.2.16 (MT), וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כָּל הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הַגֵּירִים֙ ('Solomon counted all the foreigners'), whose opening verb וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר echoes the same verb's only other occurrence in this book, the opening census at web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT) rather than continuing Huram's letter, so this reply closes here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:11-16 as mere continuation of Solomon's own letter rather than an independent reply would require ignoring the explicit change of grammatical subject to Huram, the בִּכְתָ֔ב reply-marker, and the reversed sending direction, none of which depend on the doxology's wording.

boundary_rationale: The 70,000/80,000/3,600 figures from the opening census (web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT)) recur almost verbatim at the close: web:2Chr.2.18 = oshb:2Chr.2.17 (MT), וַיַּ֨עַשׂ מֵהֶ֜ם שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ סַבָּ֔ל וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֹצֵ֣ב בָּהָ֑ר וּשְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת מְנַצְּחִ֖ים לְהַעֲבִ֥יד אֶת הָעָֽם ('he set of them seventy thousand to bear burdens, eighty thousand stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers to assign the people their work'), closing the inclusio that frames the whole temple-preparation pericope. The bridge verse into this close, web:2Chr.2.17 = oshb:2Chr.2.16 (MT), וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כָּל הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הַגֵּירִים֙ ('Solomon counted all the foreigners who were in the land of Israel'), drops the direct speech of Huram's letter for third-person narration opened by וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר, the same verb (וַיִּסְפֹּ֨ר) that opened the pericope's census. Beyond the pericope's end, the next verse launches construction with a different act-verb outside the offset zone, oshb:2Chr.3.1, וַיָּ֣חֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֤וֹת אֶת בֵּית יְהוָה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם ('Then Solomon began to build Yahweh's house at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah'), whose opening וַיָּ֣חֶל ('began') decisively ends the preparatory frame and opens the construction catalog.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing 2:17-18 into Huram's reply as its logistical tail is the closest rival, but the return to third-person narration opened by וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר and the near-verbatim repetition of the workforce figures mark an independent closing notice, not a continuation of direct speech.

boundary_rationale: 3:1 opens וַיָּ֣חֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֤וֹת אֶת בֵּית (gloss: "Solomon began to build the house of..."), naming site and etiology (Moriah, David's appointment, Ornan the Jebusite's threshing floor); 3:2 repeats the same inceptive verb and adds the date, בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי֙ בַּשֵּׁנִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֖ע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ (gloss: "in the second month, the second, in the fourth year of his reign"). The verb wayyahel ("he began") occurs only in these two verses across the whole 3:1-5:1 span (checked programmatically), so the doubled inceptive frame is a self-contained commencement notice: site, then date. It closes before 3:3, which pivots to the catalog's own header sentence, וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֖וֹת אֶת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (gloss: "and these are [the foundations] laid for Solomon's building of the house of..."; הוּסַ֣ד is a Hophal perfect 3ms of the root ysd, a passive form, so Solomon is not this clause's grammatical agent -- WEB's own restructuring, 'Now these are the foundations which Solomon laid...,' likewise avoids treating him as the verb's subject), a list-opening device distinct in form from the narrative inceptive of 3:1-2. The opening edge continues the seam-out already fixed at Phase 0 for the part boundary following the temple-preparation chapter.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping 3:1-3 as one 'opening' unit is possible since v3 still names Solomon, but the shift from narrative notice to the list-header formula is a sharp enough genre change to seat the boundary between v2 and v3.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the catalog header וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֖וֹת אֶת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (gloss: "and these are [the foundations] laid for Solomon's building of the house of..."; per M8-2Chr-008, הוּסַ֣ד is Hophal passive), giving foundation length/width (3), then two further named spaces: the porch, וְהָאוּלָ֡ם אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל פְּנֵ֨י הָאֹ֜רֶךְ (v4, WEB 'the porch'), and the great house/main hall, וְאֵ֣ת הַבַּ֣יִת הַגָּד֗וֹל (v5, WEB 'the larger room'), with its cypress ceiling and gold overlay and palm-tree ornament (5), precious-stone decoration with Parvaim gold (6), and full gold overlay of beams, thresholds, walls, and doors, closing וּפִתַּ֥ח כְּרוּבִ֖ים עַל הַקִּירֽוֹת (gloss: "and engraved cherubim on the walls"); a samekh follows v7 (weak corroboration, single-witness). Porch and great house are genuinely distinct named spaces, not one undifferentiated room, but both stay subordinate to the v3 header's single foundation-and-construction report, not because a fresh wayyiqtol-plus-subject test picks them out -- v4's וְהָאוּלָ֡ם and v5's וְאֵ֣ת הַבַּ֣יִת הַגָּד֗וֹל are waw-plus-noun openings, not verb-initial wayyiqtols, and 3:6's וַיְצַ֧ף and 3:7's וַיְחַ֨ף are themselves subjectless verb-initial wayyiqtols that continue the already-governing הַבַּיִת rather than opening a new unit, so 'subject' is not what the test turns on; the actual discontinuity arrives only at 3:8, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת בֵּֽית קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים (gloss: "and he made the house of the holy of holies"), a verb-initial wayyiqtol -- itself subjectless, like 3:6-3:7 -- that names בֵּֽית קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים, a space not previously governing this report -- not, as previously framed, a disappearance of house/great-house vocabulary, since a consonantal sweep confirms that root occurs in every verse from 3:3 through 3:8 (twice in 3:8's own construct chain and measuring phrase), missing only from 3:9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The porch/great-house naming shift at vv4-5 is the genuinely strongest rejected alternative -- a real seam candidate, not the undifferentiated space this row once claimed -- but neither verse opens with its own wayyiqtol-plus-subject the way 3:8's fresh construct does, so both stay inside the v3 header's single foundation report.

boundary_rationale: Opens naming the room, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת בֵּֽית קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים (gloss: "and he made the house of the holy of holies"), reusing 3:4's עַל פְּנֵ֤י רֹֽחַב הַבַּ֨יִת֙ formula and its twenty-cubit width for this different space, though not 3:3's sixty-cubit length (שִׁשִּׁ֔ים), which is not repeated (8); v9's coda names the nail-weight, then a second, distinct location, וְהָעֲלִיּ֖וֹת חִפָּ֥ה זָהָֽב (gloss: "and the upper rooms he overlaid with gold") -- a brief aside inside the same report on Solomon's unnamed-subject construction work, not part of the holy-of-holies room itself. V10 resumes with the same room named again, now in a locative slot: v8's אֶת בֵּֽית קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים (accusative אֶת) becomes v10's בְּבֵֽית קֹ֤דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ (locative prefix בְּ) in וַיַּ֜עַשׂ בְּבֵֽית קֹ֤דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ כְּרוּבִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם (gloss: "and he made in the house of the holy of holies two cherubim") -- not a byte-identical rerun of v8's phrase, but the same room continuing to govern the unit rather than a fresh location -- the test that separates this from v15's pivot below, where the locative names a place not previously governing this unit -- and the two carved gold cherubim with their wingspans run 10-13. The unit closes with the veil, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת הַפָּרֹ֔כֶת (gloss: "and he made the veil"), which carries no locative of its own; its attachment here rests instead on the כְּרוּבִֽים catchword closing v14 answering the cherubim of 10-13, not on any stated location. It closes before v15, which relocates the action to a genuinely new place, וַיַּ֜עַשׂ לִפְנֵ֤י הַבַּ֨יִת֙ עַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם (gloss: "and he made before the house two pillars"), whose לִפְנֵ֤י הַבַּ֨יִת֙ never governs any verse in 8-14 and so cannot be read as continuing this report -- outside the interior entirely.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The mark cluster (samekh after 3:13, samekh after 3:14, both single-witness) could be read as favoring a split between the cherubim-images clause (10-13) and the veil notice (14), but both stay bound by the shared כְּרוּבִֽים catchword (v10's cherubim, v14's cherubim on the veil) with no subject change, and marks are tier-3 weak, never drivers.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the locative pivot וַיַּ֜עַשׂ לִפְנֵ֤י הַבַּ֨יִת֙ עַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם (gloss: "and he made before the house two pillars"), moving the report outside the interior spaces catalogued in 8-14 for the first time since v3's foundation notice. The three verses form one action sequence on a single object-pair: fabrication with capital measure (15), chain ornament for the pillars (16 -- WEB 'chains in the inner sanctuary,' בַּדְּבִ֔יר, a term found only here and at 4:20 in chs 3-4; the pillars themselves remain the exterior objects named at v15 and set up 'before the temple,' עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַהֵיכָ֔ל, at v17, so this is read as a crux describing how, or in whose style, the chains were made, rather than relocating the pillars indoors -- flagged rather than resolved here), and erection-with-naming, closing וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם הימיני הַיְמָנִי֙ יָכִ֔ין (gloss: "and he called the name of the right-hand one Jachin"; הימיני is ketiv and הַיְמָנִי֙ is qere) -- Boaz follows for the left. Chapter 3 ends here; a samekh also follows this closing verse (oshb:2Chr.3.17, samekh, single-witness), alongside the samekh already disclosed after v15. It closes before 4:1, a fresh object opening chapter 4 with an explicit new material label, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח נְחֹ֔שֶׁת (gloss: "and he made an altar of bronze"), unseen in the gold-dominated report of chapter 3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A samekh follows 3:15 (single-witness, weak), which might tempt isolating v15 alone from the chain-and-naming notices in 16-17, but fabrication, ornament, and installation-with-naming form one uninterrupted action on the same referent and read better as a single installation report.

boundary_rationale: Opens the chapter on a freestanding object, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח נְחֹ֔שֶׁת (gloss: "and he made an altar of bronze"), then the molten sea (2-5), ten wash-basins (6), ten gold lampstands and ten tables set in the hall (7-8), the priests' court with bronze-plated doors (9), and the sea's placement, closing וְאֶת הַיָּ֗ם נָתַ֞ן מִכֶּ֧תֶף (gloss: "and the sea he set from the shoulder..."). Checked programmatically, no proper name (neither Solomon nor Huram) appears anywhere in 4:1-10, though Solomon is named as the subject governing this construction work two verses earlier, at both 3:1 (וַיָּ֣חֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה) and 3:3 (הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה); the construction verbs of 4:1-10 continue that same unnamed-in-context 3rd-person builder without renaming him, while the descriptive clauses at 4:3-4:5 take the sea and its oxen as grammatical subject instead -- סוֹבְבִ֣ים/מַקִּיפִ֥ים ('surrounding'/'encircling') at 4:3, עוֹמֵ֞ד ('standing') at 4:4, and מַחֲזִ֣יק/יָכִֽיל ('holding'/'could hold') at 4:5 -- before the construction verbs resume at 4:6. It closes before v11, where וַיַּ֣עַשׂ חוּרָ֔ם אֶת הַ֨סִּיר֔וֹת (gloss: "and Huram made the pots") switches the grammatical subject to a named craftsman for the first time in this catalog.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The material/location pattern near v7 is a real seam candidate, corroborated by samekh marks after 4:1, 4:5, 4:6, and 4:7 (single-witness, weak, all four now disclosed); but it does not run cleanly bronze-court(1-6)/gold-hall(7-10) as first framed -- gold appears only at 4:7-8 (the lampstands and tables set 'in the hall'), while bronze returns at 4:9's court doors, וְדַלְתוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם צִפָּ֥ה נְחֹֽשֶׁת, and 4:10 places the sea, itself a court object; the true pattern is a hall(7-8)/court(9-10) alternation, not a two-part material split. It is rejected in either form because book_strategy_draft.md §5 directs the construction chapters (3-4) be kept coarse as register-catalogs, and the subject-attribution seam at v11 -- corroborated by the zero-hit name-sweep above -- is the stronger, unambiguous divider.

boundary_rationale: Opens naming Huram as subject, וַיַּ֣עַשׂ חוּרָ֔ם אֶת הַ֨סִּיר֔וֹת (gloss: "and Huram made the pots"), with the items list, אֶת הַ֨סִּיר֔וֹת וְאֶת הַיָּעִ֖ים וְאֶת הַמִּזְרָק֑וֹת (gloss: "...the pots, the shovels, and the basins"), then the completion-plus-heading clause וַיְכַ֣ל חירם (ketiv) חוּרָ֗ם (qere) לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים (gloss: "and Huram finished doing the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God") -- the only finite כלה ('finish') form in chapters 3-5. What follows this clause is not a new independent report but an appositional itemization of 'the work' just named: pillars, bowls, capitals, networks, pomegranates, bases, basins, the sea and its oxen (12-15), and no wayyiqtol at all runs from v12 through v17 -- v16's עָשָׂ֞ה חוּרָ֥ם אָבִ֛יו ('Huram-abi ... made,' his remaining bronze tools) and v17's יְצָקָ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ ('the king cast them,' the Jordan-plain casting site) are full qatal predicates naming two distinct explicit agents, not appositional continuations of v11's heading, though still carrying no wayyiqtol of their own; a single-witness SAMEKH follows v11 itself, weak corroboration for treating v11 as its own closing unit, but the absence of any wayyiqtol through v17 argues instead that v11's clause is a heading caption for the recap rather than a self-contained completion report, so the seam is not adopted here. The unit's actual closing tally comes only at v18, וַיַּ֧עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה כָּל הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד כִּ֛י לֹ֥א נֶחְקַ֖ר מִשְׁקַ֥ל הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת (gloss: "Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance, for the weight of the bronze was not measured") -- not a subject-restoration, since v17's own subject, הַמֶּלֶךְ ('the king'), is already Solomon; the tally rests instead on v18's own summarizing כָּל הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד and the unmeasured-bronze coda, which nothing in 12-17 carries -- not, as previously framed, a lexical inclusio with v11, since bronze itself is named only at v16 and v18, never at v11; what the material sweep does support is gold's total absence across 11-18 against its presence in every verse of 19-22, and a PE follows v18 (single-witness). It closes before 4:19, where an almost identical 'made all the vessels' formula, וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֵ֚ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (gloss: "Solomon made all the vessels that were [in] the house of God"), reopens for a materially distinct, gold-only inventory.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v11 from 12-18 at the SAMEKH is the row's live internal rival -- v11's own וַיְכַ֣ל...לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים clause could read as a stand-alone completion report -- but the list it introduces is entirely appositional (verbless or qatal, no new wayyiqtol subject until v18), so v11 functions as the recap's heading rather than its own closed unit; treating v18 instead as the opening line of the next unit (paired with 19-22 as one long 'all the vessels' summary) is tempting given the phrasal echo, but v18's own clause names bronze specifically as the closing tally's subject matter, tying it to Huram's recap rather than to the gold catalog that follows.

boundary_rationale: Opens with וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֵ֚ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (gloss: "Solomon made all the vessels that were [in] the house of God"), a clause that shares its subject, verb form, and 'all the vessels' object with the immediately preceding v18, וַיַּ֧עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה כָּל הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד כִּ֛י לֹ֥א נֶחְקַ֖ר מִשְׁקַ֥ל הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת (gloss: "Solomon made all these vessels...") -- a formula doublet, not a subject-restoration, since Solomon is already the explicit subject of the identical wayyiqtol one verse earlier (a name-sweep across 3:1-4:22 confirms Solomon named at 3:1, 3:3, 4:11, 4:16, 4:18, and 4:19, with only 4:11 and 4:16 genuinely benefactive -- 'for king Solomon' -- and 4:18/4:19 sharing subject and verb). What separates the two is not the subject but the material: every verse from 19-22 names gold -- golden altar and show-bread tables (19), lampstands of pure gold (20), flowers, lamps, and tongs of purest gold (21), and closing וּפֶ֣תַח הַ֠בַּיִת דַּלְתוֹתָ֨יו הַפְּנִימִיּ֜וֹת לְקֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֗ים וְדַלְתֵ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת לַהֵיכָ֖ל זָהָֽב (gloss: "and the entrance of the house, its inner doors for the holy of holies, and the doors of the house for the main hall, gold") -- while bronze, which closed the immediately preceding tally at v18 (מִשְׁקַ֥ל הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת), never recurs; checked programmatically, every verse 19-22 contains the word for gold and none contains the word for bronze, the reverse of 19-22's gold saturation, not a symmetric mirror, since bronze within 11-18 is itself confined to only two of its eight verses (16 and 18), while gold is absent from all eight. The disclosed PE after v18 (single-witness) offers weak further corroboration for a seam at exactly this doublet. It closes before 5:1, where the discourse shifts from itemized 'he made X' clauses to a summary completion statement.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Appending 4:19-22 to the Huram unit (11-18) as one long inventory is possible, but the explicit renaming of Solomon as subject and the total absence of bronze vocabulary mark a fresh, materially distinct list rather than a continuation of Huram's bronze recap.

boundary_rationale: וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ כָּל הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה (gloss: "and all the work that Solomon did was completed") breaks the repeated wayyaas ("he made") item-notice pattern -- verified programmatically at sixteen occurrences across 3:8-4:19 -- with a feminine completion verb agreeing with 'the work' itself as grammatical subject: a discourse-level closure, not another manufacture clause. The same verse's deposit notice, וַיָּבֵ֨א שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת קָדְשֵׁ֣י דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֗יו וְאֶת הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְאֶת הַזָּהָב֙ וְאֶת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֔ים נָתַ֕ן בְּאֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים (gloss: "and Solomon brought in the dedicated things of David his father... and put [them] in the treasuries of God's house"), belongs to the same closing unit, reporting Solomon's final act before the narrative reopens with the assembly summons. A samekh+pe double mark follows (single-witness; the doubling is disclosed, not treated as double-strength evidence). It closes before 5:2's assembly-summons opening, a fresh scene outside this part's range.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Appending 5:1 to the preceding gold-vessels row (4:19-22) as its capstone verse is the closest rival, but the shift from itemized 'he made' clauses to a summary completion-and-deposit statement is a strong enough genre change -- and the book strategy's Phase-0 crosswalk already seats the part boundary here -- for it to stand alone.

boundary_rationale: This unit opens on אָז֩ ('then'), immediately after the completion formula that closed the temple-construction section at 5:1 (וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ כָּל הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה...), a verse carrying one of the book's two double-mark verses (SAMEKH+PE, single-witness; the other is 13:3's SAMEKH+SAMEKH) -- weak corroboration only, since tier-3 marks in Writings neither drive nor confirm a boundary on their own. WEB's 'Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel... to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark' (v2, אָז֩ יַקְהֵ֨יל שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה...) is answered directly by v3's fulfillment, 'all the men of Israel assembled themselves to the king' (וַיִּקָּהֲל֧וּ אֶל הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ...), echoing the same root as v2's opening verb, and v3 closes on its own dated notice, 'at the feast, which was in the seventh month' (בֶּחָ֑ג ה֖וּא הַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִֽי). V4a, וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ('all the elders of Israel came'), still names the identical elders-of-Israel body summoned at v2 (אֶת זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל) and reads as the summons frame's own continuation rather than new material; the genuinely new action begins only at v4b, 'the Levites took up the ark' (וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ הַלְוִיִּ֖ם אֶת הָאָרֽוֹן), which starts the physical procession. The whole-verse cut at v3/v4 remains the practical edge -- v3's own dated close is a natural resting point before the ark itself is touched -- but the case rests on that dated closure and the summons/response root-echo, not on v4 as a whole marking a clean subject-and-verb change.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 5:2-10 as one unbroken procession scene erases the summons/response symmetry that gives vv2-3 their own closed shape before the Levites act at v4b; splitting instead at v4a/v4b, inside v4, is the finer-grained alternative the whole-verse cut declines in favor of the dated closural formula at v3.

boundary_rationale: Verse 4's opening clause, וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ('all the elders of Israel came'), is a bare wayyiqtol continuing 5:3's וַיִּקָּהֲל֧וּ with no fronted element and no particle, and its subject is the identical body Solomon summoned at v2 (אֶת זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל) -- not a change of grammatical subject, as decision M8-2Chr-016 now also states. The genuinely new material sits in v4's second clause, וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ הַלְוִיִּ֖ם אֶת הָאָרֽוֹן ('the Levites took up the ark'), which starts the procession's own action for the first time. The scene then tracks one continuous movement: bearing the ark and Tent of Meeting up (v5), sacrificing innumerable flocks en route (v6 -- the span's one genuinely disjunctive clause, וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְכָל עֲדַ֧ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הַנּוֹעָדִ֥ים עָלָ֖יו לִפְנֵ֣י הָאָר֑וֹן מְזַבְּחִים֙, waw plus fronted compound subject plus participle, widening the cast to king-and-whole-assembly), and installing the ark beneath the cherubim in the inner sanctuary (vv7-8). It closes on two scribal asides that both read as closural: the poles-visibility note ending 'there to this day' (וַֽיְהִי שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה, v9) and the ark-contents note recalling the Horeb tablets (אֵ֚ין בָּֽאָר֔וֹן רַ֚ק שְׁנֵ֣י הַלֻּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּחֹרֵ֑ב, v10); WLC marks a single-witness PE right after v10, a small extra nod toward the same edge. Verse 11 opens a new temporal clause shifting focus from the ark itself to the priests leaving the holy place and the massed choir, arguing against extending this unit further.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v4 itself -- treating v4a as still part of decision M8-2Chr-016's summons unit and only v4b as this unit's true opening -- is rejected in favor of the whole-verse cut adopted here because 016's own dated closural formula at 5:3 (בֶּחָ֑ג ה֖וּא הַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִֽי, 'at the feast, which was in the seventh month') and the summons/response root-echo (יַקְהֵ֨יל/וַיִּקָּהֲל֧וּ) together close 5:2-3 before v4 opens, not merely because the sub-verse split overstates the syntax; a further, weaker alternative -- folding vv4-6 backward into 016's summons unit outright, since v4a shares its subject with v2/v3 -- is rejected because the procession's own action (the ark-lifting) and destination only begin at v4b, giving vv4-10 a coherent movement-and-installation shape distinct from the summons proper.

boundary_rationale: The opening clause of v11 (וַיְהִ֕י בְּצֵ֥את הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים מִן הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ כִּ֠י כָּל הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַֽנִּמְצְאִים֙ הִתְקַדָּ֔שׁוּ...) pulls attention from the ark's placement to the priestly withdrawal and the long description of the Levitical singers, Asaph/Heman/Jeduthun, and the hundred-twenty trumpeting priests (11b-13a), a stage-setting aside kept here because its whole purpose is to prepare the doxology it introduces. That doxology, 'For he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever' (כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ, v13), is genuinely rare: a book-wide check of 2Chr_oshb.txt turns up the full two-clause form only here and at 7:3 (7:6 carries a shorter single-clause cousin, לְהֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּֽי לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔וֹ, describing the instruments David made rather than repeating the congregation's cry, so it is not a third occurrence of the pair). The cloud that immediately fills the house closes the unit on divine acceptance (וְהַבַּ֛יִת מָלֵ֥א עָנָ֖ן בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה), ending 'for Yahweh's glory filled God's house' (כִּֽי מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד יְהוָ֖ה אֶת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים, v14) -- WLC's single-witness PE after this verse adds its usual thin support to the edge. 6:1 then pivots to Solomon's own speech with the same pivot-word that opened 5:2 (אָ֖ז אָמַ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה יְהוָ֣ה אָמַ֔ר לִשְׁכּ֖וֹן בָּעֲרָפֶֽל...), a genuine new beat rather than a continuation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the priestly/choir aside (11b-13a) from the doxology-and-cloud (13b-14) would strand a stage direction from the very event it exists to stage, against the inset principle that frames travel with what they introduce.

boundary_rationale: אָ֖ז אָמַ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה יְהוָ֣ה אָמַ֔ר לִשְׁכּ֖וֹן בָּעֲרָפֶֽל ('Then Solomon said, Yahweh has said he would dwell in the thick darkness') answers the cloud that has just filled the house, and pairs structurally with the assembly's own opening at 5:2 as the complex's two hinge-openings. The two verses form a closed couplet with no named human addressee -- 'I have built you a house and home, a place for you to dwell in forever' (וּמָכ֥וֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ֖ עוֹלָמִֽים, v2). Verse 3 changes both grammatical subject and addressee: 'the king turned his face, and blessed all the assembly of Israel,' a deliberate gesture toward a named audience that opens the next unit rather than continuing this one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 6:1-3 as one continuous introduction to the blessing speech is plausible since v3 frames the speech that follows, but the turn from reflecting on Yahweh's dwelling to physically facing a named audience is a real seam, and the couplet's self-contained parallelism argues for its own boundary.

boundary_rationale: 'The king turned his face, and blessed all the assembly of Israel; and all the assembly of Israel stood' (וַיַּסֵּ֤ב הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת פָּנָ֔יו וַיְבָ֕רֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל..., v3) is the frame for the direct speech opening at v4, 'He said, Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel,... and has with his hands fulfilled it,' (וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל...וּבְיָדָ֥יו מִלֵּ֖א) -- the same assembly named in the frame is still standing through the speech. The recital moves from the choice of Jerusalem and David (vv5-6) to the transfer of the building charge from David to Solomon (vv7-9), closing on Solomon's two-verse fulfillment report: v10's 'Yahweh has performed his word that he spoke' (וַיָּ֣קֶם יְהוָ֔ה אֶת דְּבָר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר), the nearer thematic echo of v4's promise-fulfilled announcement even though it shares no root with v4's מִלֵּ֖א (קום, not מלא), and v11's own placement notice, 'there I have set the ark, in which is Yahweh's covenant' (וָאָשִׂ֥ים שָׁם֙ אֶת הָ֣אָר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֖ם בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה) -- together a two-verse resolution of what v4 announced, not a single lexically-repeated inclusio. Verse 12 opens a new action clause, 'he stood before Yahweh's altar,' shifting Solomon's posture and addressee from the assembly to God and beginning the prayer's own frame.
